courses.title: Nicotine Addiction and Smoking: Health Effects and Interventions
courses.description: The Surgeon General reports that nicotine addiction produces 480,000 fatalities each year in the United States, with more casualties than all other addictions combined. Around 23% of the world's population inhales cigarettes, and the prevalence of electronic inhalation or "vaping" of nicotine has skyrocketed in recent years, particularly in young people. Studies have linked tobacco smoking to a range of devastating illnesses, including coronary artery disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, cancers in every human organ system, and decreased reproductive health. Diagnosing nicotine addiction involves assessing patient history and behaviors and using screening tools. Treatment plans are personalized, combining behavioral counseling with pharmacotherapy options like nicotine replacement therapies, bupropion, or varenicline. Support systems such as support groups and quitlines offer ongoing encouragement. Relapse prevention strategies and continued follow-up are essential for maintaining cessation efforts and achieving long-term success in abstaining from tobacco use. This activity for healthcare professionals is designed to enhance learners' proficiency in evaluating and managing nicotine addiction. Participants gain a deeper insight into the condition's risk factors, complications, and evidence-based diagnostic and management strategies. Greater competence enables learners to work effectively within an interprofessional team caring for patients with nicotine addiction.

courses.title: Antisocial Personality Disorder
courses.description: Antisocial personality disorder (ASPD) encompasses a chronic pattern of disregard for the rights of others, impaired empathy, deceitfulness, impulsivity, and persistent behavioral dysfunction that often begins with conduct disorder in childhood or adolescence. This course examines the associated medical, psychiatric, legal, and social consequences that contribute to substantial morbidity, elevated mortality risk, substance use disorders, interpersonal violence, and recurrent healthcare utilization with ASPD. This activity reviews the advances in neurobiology, genetics, developmental psychology, and behavioral science that have expanded understanding of ASPD, psychopathy, and related Cluster B personality disorders while highlighting the complexity of diagnosis and long-term management. Participants will gain an in-depth understanding of diagnostic criteria, differential diagnosis, developmental risk factors, neurobiological findings, psychiatric comorbidities, and evidence-based management strategies. This activity for healthcare professionals is designed to enhance the learner's competence in identifying ASPD, performing longitudinal assessment and mental status examination, evaluating suicide risk, engaging in therapeutic communication, planning treatment, and implementing an appropriate interprofessional approach when managing this condition to reduce harmful behaviors and improve psychosocial functioning.

courses.title: Generalized Anxiety Disorder

courses.title: Benign Eyelid Lesions
courses.description: Benign eyelid lesions can be inflammatory, infectious, traumatic, or neoplastic in origin. They are a common condition that requires differentiation from malignant and pre-malignant lesions. courses.title: Osteoporosis in Females
courses.description: Osteoporosis is a silent, progressive disease that disproportionately affects postmenopausal women and predisposes them to fracture. This chronic metabolic bone disorder is characterized by decreased bone mass and deteriorated bone microarchitecture. Risk factors include declining estrogen levels, aging, family history, low body weight, and insufficient calcium or vitamin D intake. Osteoporotic fractures, especially of the hip, spine, and wrist, significantly impact morbidity, mortality, and quality of life. Early diagnosis through bone mineral density (BMD) testing and appropriate management strategies are essential for preventing fractures and preserving bone health in women. Despite the heightened global prevalence, the condition is often underdiagnosed, and in multiple instances, there are missed opportunities to initiate screening or treatment. There is poor awareness amongst both healthcare professionals and at-risk individuals. This educational activity reviews the epidemiology, pathophysiology, risk factors, diagnostic approaches, and evidence-based management of osteoporosis in females, equipping healthcare professionals with the latest clinical strategies for identifying and managing osteoporosis. Learners explore the latest guidelines, become familiar with differing techniques for assessing BMD, and compare various management options, including both pharmacological and nonpharmacological, to prevent and treat fractures. This activity also highlights the role of an interprofessional healthcare team in detecting osteoporosis and individualizing treatment plans, improving outcomes with the overall goal of reducing the burden of osteoporotic fractures and complications.

courses.title: Anxiety
courses.description: Fear is an automatic neurophysiological state of alarm characterized by a fight or flight response to a cognitive appraisal of present or imminent danger (real or perceived). Anxiety is linked to fear and manifests as a future-oriented mood state that consists of a complex cognitive, affective, physiological, and behavioral response system associated with preparation for the anticipated events or circumstances perceived as threatening. This activity reviews the pathophysiology of anxiety, its presentation, diagnosis and highlights the role of the interprofessional team in its management.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Naloxone
courses.description: Over the past 2 decades, the increase in opioid overdose incidents nationwide has resulted in a significant surge in morbidity and mortality rates. Naloxone is a crucial intervention in this crisis and has been used for over 50 years as an opioid antidote. Naloxone operates as a competitive antagonist to the -opioid receptor. Beyond its conventional hospital deployment, naloxone is used extensively by emergency medical personnel and law enforcement agencies, and its accessibility as an over-the-counter product allows family members and caregivers to administer this antidote when needed. This activity provides healthcare professionals with important information about naloxone, including its indications, mechanism of action, administration modalities, notable adverse effects, contraindications, monitoring protocols, precautions, and pharmacokinetic profiles. The focus of this discussion is to deliver the requisite knowledge and discuss resources for proficient patient management during naloxone administration. By fostering a deeper understanding, this educational endeavor allows learners to determine effective dosage regimens, mitigate adverse reactions, and enhance overall patient outcomes in situations requiring naloxone intervention.

courses.title: Methadone
courses.description: Methadone is a synthetic, long-term opioid agonist medication used in the management and treatment of opioid use disorder (OUD) and for analgesic purposes in chronic pain. The drug is approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for treating moderate-to-severe pain that has not responded to nonopioid medications or as an alternative if the pain is unresponsive to other opioid drugs. Methadone is frequently prescribed to address severe pain associated with cancer, neuropathy, or other conditions in pediatric populations. This activity comprehensively reviews the indications, mechanism of action, and contraindications of methadone as a valuable agent in treating chronic pain and managing OUDs. This activity highlights the role of the interprofessional healthcare team in the utilization of methadone for detoxifying and treating OUD as a crucial component of medication-assisted treatment, which is significant in light of the ongoing opioid use epidemic.

courses.title: Image-Guided Breast Biopsy
courses.description: Globally, over 2 million new cases of breast cancer were diagnosed in women in 2020, and breast cancer remains the second most common cause of cancer-related deaths. In the United States, breast cancer accounts for 30% of new yearly cancer diagnoses in women. However, the mortality from breast cancer has been declining due to improved detection and advanced treatments. Vigorous screening and sophisticated diagnostic techniques increase the detection of occult breast cancer. This activity delves into the current standards of image-guided biopsies, emphasizing ultrasound, mammography, and magnetic resonance techniques. The advantages and disadvantages of the procedure are highlighted. This course empowers clinicians to enhance diagnostic accuracy and improve the management of breast cancer by elucidating the interplay between imaging equipment, tissue sampling devices, and biopsy guidance modalities. Participants will gain proficiency in applying various tissue sampling devices, including fine needle aspiration, vacuum-assisted biopsy, and spring-loaded core needle biopsy devices. Interprofessional collaboration among primary care clinicians and treating surgeons is emphasized for positive postoperative outcomes.

courses.title: Histrionic Personality Disorder
courses.description: Histrionic personality disorder (HPD) is a chronic, enduring psychiatric condition characterized by a consistent pattern of pervasive attention-seeking behaviors and exaggerated emotional displays. This condition typically emerges in late adolescence or early adulthood. Individuals with HPD are often described as narcissistic, self-indulgent, flirtatious, dramatic, and extroverted. They may feel undervalued when not in the spotlight, leading to a persistent need for validation. This condition is life-long and treatment-resistant, with psychotherapy being the primary but often ineffective treatment. Diagnosis requires longitudinal observation due to the overlap with other psychiatric conditions. Understanding HPD is limited, as most knowledge comes from small studies and older classification systems. Therefore, experts advocate for shifting from the cluster model to a dimensional model of personality, which may become standard as research evolves, changing the approach to diagnosing HPD. This activity reviews the evaluation, treatment, and management of HPD as a life-long psychiatric disorder, incorporating current guidelines addressing gender bias in clinical knowledge. This activity also provides clinicians with the knowledge and tools to differentiate HPD from other personality disorders, emphasizing the need for interprofessional collaboration when considering HPD as a diagnosis rather than a personality trait.

courses.title: Laboratory Evaluation of Coagulopathies
courses.description: Laboratory evaluation of coagulopathy involves specialized tests to study impaired blood clotting, which can lead to excessive bleeding or thrombosis. This process is fundamental to modern hematology practice and essential for diagnosing several coagulopathies. Many medical specialties are involved with initial treatment, monitoring, perioperative assessment, and management to prevent complications. Evaluation encompasses a range of factors, including assessing clotting factors, platelet function, and fibrinolytic pathways. Primary hemostasis disorders typically result in mucocutaneous bleeding, such as easy bruising, epistaxis, and heavy menstruation. Secondary hemostasis disorders typically cause deep tissue hematomas and intracranial hemorrhages, particularly in severe factor deficiencies such as hemophilia A and B. Prolonged coagulation times do not always correlate with bleeding risk, as observed in cases of lupus anticoagulants. Thrombophilia testing is recommended when therapeutic management is concerned, especially in venous thromboembolism or obstetric complications. This activity describes an overview of screening and coagulation tests, the type of specimens required, sample collection, handling and processing, interfering factors, interpretation of results, quality control, and providing healthcare professionals with the knowledge and tools to collaborate effectively within the healthcare team. Enhancing team collaboration and emphasizing the role of laboratory professionals optimizes patient outcomes.

courses.title: Opioid Equivalency
courses.description: Understanding opioid equivalency is essential to effectively managing cancer-related and chronic pain. Tailored for healthcare providers involved in pain management, the activity emphasizes the significance of comprehending and applying opioid equivalent dosing, especially for opioid-tolerant patients needing opioid rotation. Participants will explore the methods and principles of equianalgesic conversion between different opioids, aiding in therapeutic transitions while optimizing analgesic effectiveness and mitigating potential adverse effects. This activity for healthcare professionals highlights insights into the nuances of opioid equivalency calculations, enabling more informed decisions when transitioning patients between opioid therapies. Emphasis is placed on the interprofessional collaboration required to establish appropriate opioid rotations, ensuring patient safety and pain relief. Participants refine their skills in selecting suitable opioid doses while maintaining patient-centered care. This activity aims to empower clinicians with the knowledge and tools necessary to navigate opioid rotation strategies effectively and includes case examples to illustrate opioid equivalency concepts, thereby improving pain management outcomes for patients with cancer-related or chronic pain.

courses.title: Azoospermia
courses.description: Male infertility contributes to approximately 50% of infertility cases, making comprehensive evaluation of male factors essential when assessing couples experiencing difficulty conceiving. This course reviews azoospermia, defined as complete absence of spermatozoa in 2 separate centrifuged semen specimens, which represents the most severe form of male infertility and affects approximately 1% of men and 10% to 15% of infertile males. This activity examines the evaluation and management of obstructive and nonobstructive azoospermia, including relevant endocrine, genetic, infectious, medication-related, and structural causes. Participants will gain knowledge to distinguish etiologic categories, interpret diagnostic testing, and select appropriate medical, surgical, and assisted reproductive interventions. This activity for healthcare professionals is designed to enhance the learner's competence in identifying clinical features, applying sperm retrieval techniques and genetic considerations, improving treatment outcomes, understanding the emotional and psychosocial effects of azoospermia, supporting informed counseling and coordinated fertility care, and implementing an appropriate interprofessional approach when managing this condition.

courses.title: Duane Retraction Syndrome
courses.description: Duane retraction syndrome is a rare, congenital ocular motility disorder characterized by limitation of horizontal eye movements, globe retraction, and narrowing of the palpebral fissure on attempted adduction. This interprofessional continuing education activity is designed to provide ophthalmologists, optometrists, pediatricians, orthoptists, and rehabilitation specialists with a comprehensive understanding of Duane retraction syndrome, from its embryologic basis and genetic associations to its varied clinical presentations and modern management strategies. Participants review epidemiology, classification (Huber types I through III), and diagnostic approaches, including orthoptic evaluation, forced duction testing, and advanced imaging. This activity emphasizes evidence-based surgical and non-surgical interventions, patient-specific decision-making, and postoperative considerations. Learners also explore how coordinated care through timely referrals, shared decision-making, and rehabilitation planning enhances patient safety, functional outcomes, and quality of life. By integrating the perspectives of ophthalmologists, neurologists, genetic counselors, orthoptists, and low-vision specialists, the program fosters improved diagnostic accuracy, procedural planning, and long-term follow-up strategies. Upon completion, participants are equipped to identify Duane retraction syndrome confidently, differentiate it from other ocular motility disorders, counsel patients and families effectively, and collaborate across disciplines to deliver patient-centered, ethically sound care that optimizes both visual function and psychosocial well-being.

courses.title: Depression in Children
courses.description: Pediatric depression includes major depressive disorder (MDD), disruptive mood dysregulation disorder, persistent depressive disorder, and unspecified depressive disorder. Among these, MDD is a leading cause of disability in adolescents in this age group. The etiology is multifactorial, involving genetic, environmental, and neurobiological risk factors that contribute to depression in children and adolescents. Screening is recommended for adolescents aged 12 to 18 with validated tools, and a comprehensive evaluation is essential for accurate diagnosis. Diagnosis requires a thorough clinical evaluation and differentiation from other conditions, such as attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, anxiety, and medical illnesses that mimic depressive symptoms. Treatment aims for complete remission and functional recovery through a biopsychosocial approach, combining psychotherapy (first-line for mild-to-moderate cases) and pharmacotherapy. Prevention strategies encompass school-based programs, family interventions, and policy initiatives designed to support healthy development. This activity focuses on the latest evidence-based strategies for identifying, diagnosing, and managing pediatric depression, with an emphasis on early intervention and improving long-term outcomes. This activity highlights the role of validated screening tools, structured clinical interviews, and standardized assessment scales in enhancing diagnostic accuracy across various care settings. This activity also explores established and emerging treatment modalities, including pharmacologic interventions, digital health tools, and single-session therapies, providing clinicians with practical approaches to individualized care. This activity further examines novel research findings that inform prevention strategies aimed at reducing the incidence and severity of depressive disorders in youth. This activity highlights the importance of interprofessional collaboration among healthcare providers in...

courses.title: Avoidant Personality Disorder
courses.description: Avoidant personality disorder describes a pervasive pattern of social anxiety, extreme sensitivity to rejection, and feelings of inadequacy, but with a strong underlying desire for companionship. This activity reviews the diagnostic evaluation and management of avoidant personality disorder and highlights the role of the interprofessional team in managing patients with this condition.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Transrectal Ultrasonography and Image-Guided Biopsies of the Prostate
courses.description: Transrectal prostate ultrasound is a key tool for diagnosing many prostatic disorders, such as prostate cancer, prostatitis, prostatic abscess, and benign prostatic hyperplasia. Besides traditional grayscale imaging, multiple additional technologies, such as shear wave elastography, color Doppler imaging, and contrast enhancement, may aid the diagnosis. Transrectal ultrasonography is described along with the different ultrasound appearances of various prostatic pathologies. Transrectal ultrasound-guided prostate biopsies with or without magnetic resonance imaging fusion guidance are reviewed in detail, as they are the primary methods of obtaining confirmatory tissue samples in patients suspected of prostate cancer. This activity outlines the indications for transrectal ultrasound evaluation of the prostate, describes the technique for transrectal ultrasound-guided prostate biopsies, outlines the role and selection of prophylactic antibiotics, summarizes the methods of local anesthesia for transrectal prostate biopsies, reviews the role of prostatic magnetic resonance imaging and magnetic resonance imaging fusion-guided prostate biopsies, compares the benefits and deficits between transrectal and transperineal biopsy procedures, and highlights the interprofessional team's role in improving care for patients with prostatic disease.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Fentanyl
courses.description: Fentanyl is a potent synthetic opioid, which, similar to morphine, produces analgesia but to a greater extent. This robust pharmacologic agent is typically 50 to 100 times more potent. A dose of only 100 micrograms can produce equivalent analgesia to approximately 10 mg of morphine. However, fentanyl exhibits vastly different properties and pharmacokinetics. Clinically, its most common use is as a sedative in intubated patients and in severe cases of pain in patients with renal failure due to its primarily hepatic elimination. At times, fentanyl may also be indicated to treat chronic pain patients who have developed tolerance to opiates. When used as a sedative, drug administration is most commonly via a drip. Lastly, fentanyl use can extend to the treatment of epilepsy. That is, in combination with certain neuroleptic medications as part of therapeutic neuroleptanalgesia. This activity outlines the indications, mechanism of action, administration methods, significant adverse effects, contraindications, monitoring, and toxicity of fentanyl so that providers can direct patient therapy to optimal outcomes.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Male Infertility
courses.description: Male infertility is a common contributor to couple infertility and may result from endocrine, genetic, testicular, post-testicular, medication-related, infectious, environmental, or functional causes. Evaluation requires timely semen analysis, targeted hormonal and genetic testing, assessment for reversible conditions, and coordination with reproductive specialists when assisted reproductive options are needed. Clinicians may inconsistently obtain appropriate repeat semen analyses, recognize indications for hormonal or genetic evaluation, counsel patients about testosterone-related infertility, or select evidence-based referral and treatment pathways. This continuing medical education activity addresses this gap by reviewing the epidemiology, differential diagnosis, evaluation, and treatment of male infertility, including lifestyle modification, varicocele repair, gonadotropic therapy, reproductive technologies, and counseling. Participants are expected to gain practical strategies to improve diagnostic accuracy, risk assessment, patient counseling, complication prevention, and interprofessional coordination to support patient-centered reproductive outcomes.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Oxycodone
courses.description: Oxycodone is a potent semisynthetic opioid with agonistic properties on mu-, kappa-, and delta-type opioid receptors. This drug is beneficial when used judiciously for pain management, yet it carries the risk of inducing physical dependence and addiction. The immediate-release formulation of oxycodone is approved by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for managing acute or chronic moderate-to-severe pain when opioid medication is considered suitable and alternative pain management strategies are inadequate. The extended-release formulation is FDA-approved for managing severe pain that necessitates continuous, long-term opioid treatment when no alternative options are available to address the pain. The FDA has also approved an abuse-deterrent formulation of oxycodone, containing inactive ingredients to render the formulation resistant to misuse and abuse. This activity comprehensively reviews the indications, mechanism of action, administration, adverse effects, and contraindications of oxycodone while highlighting its distinctions from other opioids in pain management. This activity also underscores the crucial role of the interprofessional healthcare team in assisting patients with pain management with oxycodone.

courses.title: Suicide Risk in Children and Adolescents: Assessment and Management
courses.description: Suicidality among children and adolescents represents a critical and growing public health concern, with rising rates of ideation and behavior contributing to significant morbidity and mortality. Clinical prediction at the individual level remains limited, necessitating standardized approaches to identification and management across care settings. This activity reviews developmental patterns, key risk factors, and evidence-based strategies for screening and assessment using structured tools. Emphasis is placed on a 3-step clinical pathway involving brief screening, focused suicide safety assessment, and risk-based disposition planning. The participant learns to apply validated frameworks to improve early detection, ensure appropriate intervention, and support safe transitions of care. Collaboration among an interprofessional team including clinicians, nurses, mental health specialists, and social workers enhances care coordination, facilitates timely referral, strengthens safety planning, and improves follow-up, ultimately leading to better patient outcomes and reduced suicide-related risk.

courses.title: Laser Enucleation of the Prostate (HoLEP and ThuLEP)
courses.description: The prostate gland is found in the adult male pelvis, enclosing and surrounding the posterior urethra. The primary and only function of the prostate gland is reproductive, as its secretions form a quarter of the seminal fluid. Benign prostatic hyperplasia causes gland enlargement and is a normal physiological process. However, it may lead to obstruction of the urinary flow and present as lower obstructive or irritative urinary tract symptoms. Although there are many medical and surgical methods of dealing with benign prostatic hyperplasia causing significant symptoms, treating larger glands (>80 grams in size) is especially difficult. One of the more successful, less invasive surgical treatment options for symptomatic benign prostatic hyperplasia is laser therapy, which can be used for tissue vaporization in smaller prostates or prostate gland enucleation in larger prostate glands (80 grams or more). This activity provides a detailed explanation of the HoLEP and ThuLEP techniques, highlights the indications and patient selection, reviews the benefits, and discusses strategies to avoid, recognize, and treat major complications of the procedure.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Morphine
courses.description: Morphine remains a foundational agent in the treatment of moderate to severe pain, both acute and chronic, with particular value in oncology, palliative care, and vaso-occlusive crises associated with sickle cell disease. This activity equips healthcare professionals with essential knowledge of morphine s FDA-approved indications, along with a comprehensive review of its mechanism of action, pharmacokinetics, and key contraindications. It also addresses proper administration techniques, potential drug interactions, and adverse effects, particularly those emphasized in FDA-issued warnings, to support safe and informed clinical decision-making. A detailed understanding of morphine s pharmacological profile enables clinicians to develop individualized pain management strategies that optimize efficacy while minimizing risks. This activity emphasizes evidence-based approaches to pain control using morphine across various care settings, with a special focus on the collaborative role of the interprofessional healthcare team in monitoring treatment, adjusting dosages, and ensuring patient safety.

courses.title: Duane-Radial Ray Syndrome (Okihiro Syndrome)
courses.description: Duane-radial ray syndrome (DRRS), also known Okihiro syndrome, is a rare autosomal dominant congenital disorder characterized by the Duane anomaly and radial ray malformations of the upper limbs. Caused by heterozygous pathogenic variants in the spalt-like transcription factor 4 (SALL4) gene, DRRS is part of the spectrum of SALL4-related disorders. Clinical manifestations include limited ocular abduction with globe retraction and narrowing of the palpebral fissure, along with thumb hypoplasia, triphalangeal thumbs, or partial to complete absence of the radius. Multisystem involvement may include cardiac, renal, auditory, and other skeletal anomalies, with variable phenotypic expression even within families. Diagnosis is established by recognizing characteristic clinical findings and confirmed by molecular genetic testing. This continuing education activity reviews the genetic basis, clinical presentation, differential diagnosis, and multidisciplinary management of DRRS. Clinicians will be able to recognize key diagnostic features, differentiate DRRS from overlapping syndromes, initiate appropriate genetic testing, coordinate multisystem evaluation, and implement evidence-based, team-based management strategies to optimize patient outcomes.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Alcohol-Related Psychosis
courses.description: Alcohol-related psychosis (ARP) is a well-documented but poorly understood complication of heavy alcohol use, distinct from other alcohol-related conditions such as delirium tremens, Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome, and alcohol-induced dementia. ARP often presents with auditory hallucinations, delusions, and cognitive disturbances that resemble schizophrenia, though it typically develops within days of alcohol cessation and resolves with abstinence. The disorder is associated with neurotransmitter imbalances involving dopamine, serotonin, and glutamate, but its exact pathophysiology remains unclear. This course explores the complexities surrounding this phenomenon, including the current diagnostic challenges that require differentiation from primary psychotic disorders and elusive pathophysiology. Standardized diagnostic screening is also essential for recognizing ARP and optimally initiating effective interventions. This activity for healthcare professionals is designed to enhance the learner's competence in identifying ARP, performing the recommended evaluation, and implementing an appropriate interprofessional approach when managing this condition.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Postpartum Psychosis
courses.description: Postpartum psychosis is an acute illness of multifactorial origin and is considered a psychiatric emergency. In this activity, the common presentations, diagnosis, and treatment options for postpartum psychosis are reviewed. This activity also outlines the role of interprofessional team members in increasing awareness and decreasing latency between onset and diagnosis of this condition to improve treatment outcomes in patients experiencing postpartum psychosis.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Gender-Affirming Surgery of the Head and Neck
courses.description: This continuing education activity examines facial gender-affirming surgical care for transgender individuals, including patient selection, preoperative evaluation, procedural planning, perioperative risk reduction, postoperative care, and complication prevention. Facial characteristics strongly influence how gender is perceived and may affect safety, psychological well-being, and quality of life for patients with gender dysphoria. Current practice may be inconsistent because clinicians do not always apply evidence-based eligibility criteria, recognize procedure-specific risks, or coordinate care across surgical, endocrine, behavioral health, nursing, and speech therapy disciplines. The activity narrows this gap through practical guidance on surgical candidacy, hormone-related thromboembolic risk, imaging, operative options, patient counseling, and longitudinal follow-up. Participants improve risk assessment, shared decision-making, complication recognition, expectation setting, and interprofessional coordination while supporting respectful, inclusive, patient-centered care and informed procedural choices.

courses.title: Drug Addiction
courses.description: The definition of addiction among the general population is a fact or condition of being addicted to a particular substance, thing, or activity. Medically, there are 2 categories: substance and nonsubstance addiction, and many risk factors predispose individuals to both. In particular, a history of risk-taking behavior, genetic predisposition, and propensity for stress play a role. Over time, addiction changes parts of the brain, specifically the dopaminergic system, responsible for perceiving rewards. Addiction is a chronic, relapsing brain disease that leads to medical, psychological, and social complications. This activity outlines the importance of the interprofessional team in treating patients with addiction to ensure the best long-term outcomes. Participating clinicians review the importance of considering a holistic approach to the care of their patients.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Cat Eye Syndrome (Schmid-Fraccaro Syndrome)
courses.description: Cat eye syndrome (CES), also known as "Schmid-Fraccaro syndrome," is a rare, multisystem disorder caused by a supernumerary marker chromosome derived from chromosome 22. Classic features include ocular colobomas, anal atresia, congenital heart defects, preauricular anomalies, and renal malformations. Healthcare professionals will gain practical tools for shared care planning, performance tracking, facilitating smooth transitions to adult care, and providing genetic counseling for family planning and recurrence risk. This activity offers a comprehensive overview of CES, detailing its genetic basis, phenotypic variability, and advanced diagnostic methods such as chromosomal microarray analysis and fluorescence in situ hybridization for precise characterization. This activity also reviews key clinical features, including epibulbar dermoids, preauricular skin tags, and renal malformations, and engages with case-based scenarios illustrating interdisciplinary management across pediatric surgery, cardiology, ophthalmology, audiology, nephrology, and developmental pediatrics. In addition, this activity also emphasizes early recognition of red-flag symptoms, implementation of structured surveillance protocols, long-term follow-up, and development of individualized care plans incorporating family education and psychosocial support. This activity emphasizes the importance of interprofessional collaboration among healthcare providers to ensure coordinated, patient-centered care and enhances the ability to deliver evidence-based, tailored, and family-focused treatment for patients with CES throughout their lifespan.

courses.title: Pennsylvania Child Abuse Recognition and Reporting
courses.description: Healthcare providers in Pennsylvania must adhere to the Pennsylvania Child Protective Services Law (CPSL), 23 Pa.C.S. Chapter 63 (relating to child protective services) when recognizing and reporting suspected child abuse. The CPSL was established in 1975 to protect children from abuse, allow the opportunity for healthy growth and development, and preserve and stabilize the family whenever possible. This activity outlines the categories and common indicators of child abuse, as well as the requirements and procedures for reporting suspected child abuse.

courses.title: Artificial Corneal Transplantation
courses.description: Artificial corneal transplantation, commonly referred to as keratoprosthesis, represents a transformative advancement in the management of severe corneal blindness, particularly when conventional penetrating or lamellar keratoplasty is unlikely to succeed. Conditions such as multiple failed corneal grafts, severe ocular surface disease, limbal stem cell deficiency, chemical injuries, and autoimmune cicatrizing disorders often leave clinicians with limited therapeutic options. In such complex scenarios, artificial corneal transplantation offers the potential to restore vision and improve quality of life in otherwise visually debilitating conditions. This activity provides a comprehensive, clinically focused overview of artificial corneal transplantation, including indications; patient selection criteria; device types, such as the Boston Keratoprosthesis and other evolving designs; surgical principles; postoperative care; and long-term outcomes. Learners can expect a detailed discussion of preoperative evaluation, perioperative decision-making, complication prevention, and management of sight-threatening adverse events, including glaucoma, retroprosthetic membrane formation, infection, and device extrusion. Emphasis is placed on evidence-based practices and current consensus guidelines. Participation in this activity highlights the critical role of the interprofessional healthcare team, including cornea specialists, glaucoma specialists, retina surgeons, anaesthesiologists, optometrists, nurses, pharmacists, and rehabilitation professionals. Through coordinated care, shared decision-making, and vigilant long-term follow-up, the team enhances patient safety, surgical success, and visual outcomes. This activity is designed to strengthen clinical competence, promote collaborative practice, and equip healthcare professionals with the skills necessary to manage one of the most challenging areas in modern corneal surgery.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Hydrocodone and Acetaminophen
courses.description: Hydrocodone is a potent analgesic commonly prescribed for moderate-to-severe pain management in postoperative settings, trauma patients, and individuals with cancer. When combined with acetaminophen, hydrocodone demonstrates increased efficacy without significantly altering the adverse effect profile, as evidenced by randomized studies. This combination is also frequently used as an antitussive agent. This activity reviews the indications, mechanism of action, pharmacokinetics, methods of administration, and potential adverse effects of hydrocodone/acetaminophen. Additionally, it outlines important precautions, contraindications, monitoring guidelines, and toxicity risks associated with this drug combination. By improving the interprofessional team s understanding of hydrocodone/acetaminophen, this program aims to optimize patient care and safety in pain management.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Malignant Pleural Effusion
courses.description: Malignant pleural effusion (MPE) has an incidence of 500,000 new cases a year in the United States and Europe and has long been recognized as a cause of significant morbidity in patients with advanced cancer. Associated loculations have been identified as a poor prognostic factor. Diagnosing MPE typically involves a combination of clinical assessment, imaging studies, and laboratory analysis of pleural fluid. Symptoms such as dyspnea, chest pain, and cough prompt further evaluation, often starting with a chest x-ray or computed tomography to detect fluid accumulation. Thoracentesis allows for cytological examination to identify malignant cells. Additional tests like pleural biopsy or biomarkers may be conducted to confirm the diagnosis. Advanced imaging techniques and molecular testing can aid in determining the primary malignancy and guiding treatment strategies. Management of malignant pleural effusion involves therapeutic thoracentesis for symptom relief, pleurodesis or indwelling pleural catheters to prevent fluid recurrence, and treatment of the underlying malignancy to address the root cause. Spengler was the first to perform chemical pleurodesis using hypertonic glucose in 1901. Controversy over the ideal agent for this procedure has evolved since then. However, talc has been recognized as the most widely used and studied agent. This activity for healthcare professionals is designed to enhance learners' competence in evaluating and managing MPE. Participants gain a deeper understanding of the condition's pathogenesis, various clinical presentations, and evidence-based diagnostic and management strategies. Greater proficiency prepares learners to work within an interprofessional team caring for patients with MPE.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Tuberculosis Prevention, Control, and Elimination
courses.description: The World Health Organization declared tuberculosis (TB) a public health emergency 30 years ago. However, despite intensive global efforts, TB regained the dubious distinction as the leading infectious cause of death worldwide after being unseated by COVID-19 for 3 years. Clinicians should have a thorough understanding of TB as a usually curable yet persistent global health challenge, including its prevention, control, and eventual elimination. Effective TB management is influenced by patient, healthcare, and system-level considerations, such as multidrug-resistant TB, delayed diagnosis, competing governmental priorities, and the impact of medical and socioeconomic factors on TB acquisition and progression. TB elimination efforts necessitate patient- and population-centered care that integrates screening, diagnosis, and treatment within broader public health frameworks to empower healthcare professionals to combat TB in their practice while supporting sustained progress toward eliminating TB. This activity for healthcare professionals is designed to enhance the learner's competence in differentiating TB infection from TB disease, leveraging emerging diagnostic and treatment advancements, and identifying the critical importance of reporting, surveillance, program and policy development, advocacy, and research as well as implementing an appropriate interprofessional management approach to improve patient outcomes.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Nonseminomatous Testicular Tumors
courses.description: Testicular nonseminomatous germ cell tumors represent a highly curable malignancy when diagnosed and treated with evidence-based protocols. Optimal management requires a thorough understanding of the pathophysiology and patterns of metastatic dissemination among healthcare professionals. Despite its malignant nature, nonseminomatous germ cell tumors demonstrate an excellent prognosis with appropriate treatment, particularly with the advent of cisplatin-based chemotherapy. Multidisciplinary coordination involving urologists, oncologists, radiologists, and pathologists is paramount to achieving favorable clinical outcomes. This review underscores the critical role of an interprofessional team in the comprehensive evaluation and management of testicular nonseminomatous germ cell tumors.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Heroin Toxicity
courses.description: Heroin toxicity is a life-threatening emergency caused by excessive activation of opioid receptors following the use of heroin, a powerful opioid derived from morphine. After administration, heroin is rapidly metabolized to morphine and 6-monoacetylmorphine, producing profound central nervous system and respiratory depression. Patients commonly present with slow or absent respirations, decreased consciousness, and pinpoint pupils, though findings may vary with coingestants such as alcohol, benzodiazepines, sympathomimetics, or anticholinergics. Management focuses on airway protection, ventilatory support, and administration of naloxone, an opioid antagonist that reverses respiratory depression. Ongoing care includes assessment for opioid use disorder, harm reduction interventions, and coordinated referral for addiction treatment and recovery support. This activity for healthcare professionals is designed to enhance the learners' understanding of the pathophysiology, recognition, and management of heroin toxicity while fostering practical, patient-centered approaches to improve outcomes. Participants will strengthen their ability to identify key clinical features of heroin toxicity, such as respiratory depression, altered mental status, and miosis, and implement evidence-based interventions, including airway management, naloxone use, and post-reversal monitoring. Clinicians will also gain insight into effective harm reduction and relapse prevention strategies, such as naloxone distribution, initiation of medication-assisted treatment, and patient and family education on overdose prevention. By emphasizing interprofessional communication and coordinated care among physicians, advanced practitioners, nurses, pharmacists, and behavioral health professionals, this activity further enhances participants' ability to deliver compassionate, evidence-based treatment, improve team performance, reduce recurrent overdose, and promote long-term patient safety and recovery.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Facial Nerve Palsy
courses.description: Facial paralysis has profound functional and psychosocial consequences, affecting expression, speech, eye protection, and quality of life. This course reviews the pathophysiology and clinical features of acute facial paralysis, which commonly presents with facial asymmetry, impaired eye closure, oral incompetence, and reduced social confidence, with most cases attributed to Bell s palsy, though the differential diagnosis is broad and includes stroke, trauma, infection, neoplasm, and autoimmune disease. Participants will also gain an understanding of timely evaluation involving distinguishing benign, self-limited conditions from life-threatening etiologies such as cerebrovascular events, as well as facial nerve anatomy, red flags, and appropriate management, including eye protection, pharmacologic therapy, and specialist referral. This activity for healthcare professionals is designed to enhance the learner's competence in identifying facial paralysis, performing the recommended evaluation, and implementing an appropriate interprofessional approach when managing this condition, ultimately improving patient outcomes and reducing complications.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: New York State Infection Control
courses.description: Infection control refers to the policies and procedures implemented to control and minimize the spread of infections within hospitals and other healthcare settings, with the main goal of reducing infection rates. The primary purpose of infection control programs has been to focus on the surveillance of health care acquired infections and to understand the epidemiology of risk factors. In recent times, healthcare epidemiology has been characterized by consumer demands for greater transparency and accountability, increased scrutiny and regulation, and expectations for rapid reductions in health care acquired infection rates. The role of infection control is to prevent and reduce the risk of health care acquired infections by implementing infection control programs, including surveillance, isolation, outbreak management, environmental hygiene, employee health, education, and infection prevention policies and management. This activity reviews the New York State requirements for healthcare professional training regarding infection control, empowering healthcare professionals and their teams to apply up-to-date infection control practices within their practices.

courses.title: Ophthalmia Neonatorum (Neonatal Conjunctivitis)
courses.description: Ophthalmia neonatorum, or neonatal conjunctivitis, is a serious ocular condition affecting newborns within the first month of life, with global incidence ranging from less than 1% in high-resource areas to over 10% in underserved regions. Without timely intervention, this disease most notably associated with Neisseria gonorrhoeae and Chlamydia trachomatis can progress to corneal ulceration, scarring, and permanent blindness. This course equips clinicians with the knowledge to identify, prevent, and manage ophthalmia neonatorum through an evidence-based, interprofessional lens. Participants will explore updated United States Preventive Services Task Force and CDC guidelines on universal prophylaxis, the use of erythromycin or azithromycin, and prenatal screening strategies for sexually transmitted infections. The differential diagnosis based on onset, discharge type, and systemic symptoms, as well as on the integration of bedside diagnostics, molecular testing, and culture-based confirmation, is also reviewed. This activity for healthcare professionals is designed to enhance the learner's competence in identifying ophthalmia neonatorum, performing the recommended evaluation, and implementing an appropriate interprofessional approach when managing this condition to reduce transmission risk, enhance early recognition, and ensure vision-preserving care for neonates in diverse clinical settings.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Pythium Keratitis
courses.description: Pythium keratitis is a rapidly progressive, vision-threatening corneal infection caused by Pythium insidiosum, an aquatic oomycete commonly found in stagnant water and soil. The pathogen exhibits filamentous growth that closely resembles fungal hyphae, but its distinct lack of ergosterol renders conventional antifungal therapies largely ineffective. Infection typically follows corneal microtrauma, leading to aggressive stromal necrosis, multifocal infiltrates, and, in advanced stages, corneal perforation. The clinical presentation often mirrors fungal keratitis, with features such as feathery margins, satellite lesions, and reticular stromal spread, complicating early differentiation. Definitive diagnosis requires microbiologic culture, histopathological examination revealing sparsely septate hyphae, and adjunctive molecular techniques such as polymerase chain reaction. Management strategies emphasize early therapeutic keratoplasty and the use of topical antibacterial agents, notably linezolid and azithromycin. Prompt recognition and targeted intervention are critical to improving visual outcomes and minimizing the risk of enucleation. This activity for healthcare professionals is designed to enhance learners' competence in evaluating and managing Pythium keratitis. Participants will deepen their understanding of the condition's etiology, risk factors, pathophysiology, and clinical presentation. Current diagnostic and therapeutic recommendations will also be discussed. Improved skills will enable clinicians to collaborate within an interprofessional team caring for affected individuals.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Opioid Use Disorder: Evaluation and Management
courses.description: This activity focuses on the critical evaluation and management of opioid use disorder (OUD), a pervasive condition significantly diminishing patients' quality of life and contributing to a widespread epidemic in the United States. With over 16 million affected globally and 2.1 million in the United States, the course emphasizes the urgency of identifying and promptly treating persistent opioid use and misuse. Participants will review evidence-based treatment options, including methadone and buprenorphine, and examine their roles in both the acute phase for detoxification and long-term management. The program also discusses the Mainstreaming Addiction Treatment (MAT) Act, which empowers healthcare providers to prescribe buprenorphine without the previous X-Waiver limitations. Furthermore, the course explores the multidimensional approach to treatment, including behavioral therapy, peer support, and the integration of nonpharmacologic interventions, reinforcing the need for an interprofessional team in optimizing patient care. Overall, this activity will equip healthcare professionals with the knowledge and skills necessary to navigate the intricate landscape of OUD, emphasizing a patient-centered, evidence-based, and interdisciplinary approach to improve outcomes and address the ongoing opioid epidemic.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Electrophysiology Study and Ablation of Ventricular Tachycardia
courses.description: Electrophysiology study (EPS) and catheter ablation are essential diagnostic and therapeutic tools for managing ventricular tachycardia (VT), particularly in patients with structural heart disease or refractory arrhythmias. EPS identifies arrhythmogenic foci and abnormal conduction pathways, guiding targeted ablation to eliminate VT circuits. Catheter ablation has been shown to reduce VT burden, decrease implantable cardiac defibrillator shocks, improve quality of life, and lower hospitalization rates. While it is a complex procedure requiring specialized expertise, advancements in mapping technologies and ablation strategies have improved efficacy and safety, making it a cornerstone in VT management. Clinicians participating in this course gain comprehensive knowledge of VT pathophysiology, patient selection for EPS and ablation, procedural techniques, and post-ablation management. This course enhances clinician's ability to interpret electrophysiologic findings, optimize antiarrhythmic therapy, and recognize complications. By improving technical skills and interdisciplinary collaboration, clinicians are better equipped to deliver high-quality, patient-centered care, ultimately improving patient outcomes with ventricular arrhythmias.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Tuberculosis Overview
courses.description: Tuberculosis (TB) is a significant global health challenge; the World Health Organization has set an ambitious goal to reduce TB incidence by 90% between 2015 and 2035. However, TB diagnosis, treatment, and prevention present considerable difficulties. Before the COVID-19 pandemic, TB was the most prevalent infectious disease worldwide. Mycobacterium tuberculosis, the causative agent of TB, has plagued humanity for millennia. Diagnostic approaches include the Mantoux skin test and the interferon-gamma release assay, which have diagnostic and predictive limitations. Advances such as molecular nucleic acid amplification tests have improved diagnostic accuracy but remain inaccessible in many high-prevalence regions. The ongoing development and implementation of new diagnostic tests aim to enhance TB detection further. This activity introduces the epidemiology, pathophysiology, diagnostic approaches, treatments, and prevention of latent and active TB. The treatment of TB involves complex regimens that are challenging to administer. The primary anti-TB antibiotics, developed in the mid-20th century, are essential, but recent approvals of 2 new antibiotics mark a significant advancement. Effective TB prevention and management require a coordinated effort among public health officials, primary care clinicians, and specialists, emphasizing the need for robust public health infrastructure and interprofessional collaboration to achieve global TB control and elimination goals.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: HIV-Related Endocrinopathies
courses.description: HIV infection can affect virtually every endocrine organ system in the body. Endocrine dysfunction secondary to neoplastic and opportunistic infectious involvement of endocrine organs was pervasive during the early AIDS pandemic. However, the current widespread use of effective antiretroviral therapy permits individuals with HIV a lifespan approaching that of the general population. Consequently, individuals with chronic HIV infection develop endocrinopathies commonly seen within the general population. Still, HIV status and antiretroviral therapy appear to be independent risk factors for developing many endocrinological disorders. Inadequately managed hormonal dysfunction can adversely affect quality of life and increase overall morbidity and mortality. HIV status can present unique challenges in diagnosing and managing endocrinopathies. This activity reviews the epidemiology, etiology, presenting symptomatology, diagnostic evaluation, and management of endocrinopathies in individuals with HIV and highlights the role of the interprofessional team in improving outcomes for these patients.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Differentiating Pythium Keratitis From Fungal and Acanthamoeba Keratitis: A Practical Guide
courses.description: Microbial keratitis remains a leading cause of corneal blindness, and early differentiation among infectious etiologies is critical for vision preservation. Pythium keratitis, an emerging and frequently misdiagnosed infection, closely mimics fungal and Acanthamoeba keratitis, often leading to delayed treatment and poor outcomes. This activity provides a practical, clinically oriented approach to distinguishing these conditions by reviewing their epidemiology, pathophysiology, and key clinical features, with emphasis on slit-lamp findings, disease progression, and clinical red flags. Diagnostic strategies, including microbiologic techniques, imaging adjuncts, and common pitfalls, are also addressed, along with evidence-based management highlighting differences in medical therapy, surgical decision-making, and prognosis. An interprofessional approach involving ophthalmology, microbiology, pathology, nursing, and pharmacy enhances diagnostic accuracy, streamlines management, and improves patient outcomes.

courses.title: Thyroid Nodule Biopsy
courses.description: Fine needle aspiration (FNA) dates back to the 1930s when Martin and Ellis first described the procedure and its potential implications in the medical field. Over time the role of ultrasound-guided FNA evolved as an important tool in assessing thyroid nodules. This activity describes and outlines fine-needle aspiration of a thyroid nodule with ultrasound guidance. It also reviews the role of proper technique in the successful acquisition of thyroid cells for cytopathologic review.

courses.title: Codeine
courses.description: Codeine is a member of the opioid class of medications and is used to manage pain. Codeine is also used to treat cough. For mild-to-moderate pain, codeine is often used as a combined medication with acetaminophen or with an NSAID like ibuprofen. The drug is often available as a combination product with promethazine or an NSAID like salicylic acid for cough and cold. Codeine is often marketed in the form of tablets and syrups. While opioids are valuable agents for treating pain, they also carry a high risk of misuse, abuse, addiction, and increased mortality, as demonstrated by the current opioid epidemic and accompanying overdose deaths. This activity outlines the indications, mechanism of action, contraindications, adverse events, and other important aspects relating to the use of codeine in the clinical setting. The use of codeine by interprofessional team members relates to the potential for opioid misuse and the associated consequences, along with the appropriate indications.

courses.title: Parry-Romberg Syndrome
courses.description: Parry-Romberg syndrome, or progressive hemifacial atrophy, is a rare, chronic, and multifactorial disorder characterized by progressive unilateral atrophy of facial tissues, including skin, subcutaneous fat, muscle, cartilage, and bone. Typically manifesting during the first or second decade of life, Parry-Romberg syndrome progresses slowly over several years before stabilizing. This course reviews the neurological, ophthalmologic, dental, and dermatologic manifestations that frequently accompany the facial changes, reflecting the condition's multisystemic nature. The pathogenesis is not clearly proven. Various proposed mechanisms include autoimmune, neurogenic, and vascular causes, often with overlap syndromes such as localized scleroderma. Early recognition and interprofessional management are essential to optimize functional, aesthetic, and psychosocial outcomes. This course explores the pathophysiology, clinical manifestations, diagnostic evaluation, and evolving management strategies of Parry-Romberg syndrome. Participants will gain competence in differentiating Parry-Romberg syndrome from similar neurocutaneous and autoimmune disorders, applying appropriate diagnostic imaging and serologic assessments, and implementing evidence-based therapeutic and reconstructive interventions. This activity for healthcare professionals is designed to enhance the learner's competence in identifying Parry-Romberg syndrome, performing the recommended evaluation, and implementing an appropriate interprofessional approach when managing this condition to improve outcomes and quality of life.

courses.title: Opioid Withdrawal
courses.description: Opioid withdrawal syndrome is a life-threatening condition resulting from opioid dependence. Opioids are a group of drugs used to manage severe pain and include morphine, heroin, oxycontin, codeine, methadone, and hydromorphone. Opioids are sometimes misused, as they can assist with mental relaxation and pain relief and can produce a sense of euphoria. Chronic opioid use can lead to the development of potentially incapacitating dependence. This activity describes the evaluation and management of opioid withdrawal and highlights the interprofessional team's role in improving care for affected patients.

courses.title: Cytomegalovirus Corneal Endotheliitis
courses.description: Cytomegalovirus (CMV) corneal endotheliitis is an underrecognized cause of corneal endothelial dysfunction that can lead to progressive vision loss and secondary glaucoma. The condition typically arises in immunocompetent adults and is associated with reactivation of latent CMV within the anterior segment. Risk factors include prior intraocular surgery, corticosteroid use, and preexisting ocular inflammation. Viral replication induces localized endothelial injury, resulting in recurrent anterior uveitis, corneal edema, and characteristic coin-shaped or linear keratic precipitates. Clinical overlap with herpes simplex virus and varicella zoster virus endotheliitis complicates recognition, making polymerase chain reaction analysis of aqueous humor the diagnostic gold standard. Management requires prompt initiation of topical or systemic ganciclovir or valganciclovir, often combined with judicious corticosteroid use to control inflammation. Despite therapy, patients remain at risk for irreversible endothelial cell loss, persistent corneal edema, and refractory glaucoma. Long-term prognosis depends on early detection, appropriate antiviral treatment, and preservation of endothelial reserve. This educational activity for healthcare professionals is designed to strengthen learners' proficiency in evaluating and managing CMV corneal endotheliitis. Participants will broaden their grasp of the condition's etiology, risk factors, pathophysiology, and distinguishing clinical features. Improved skills will support accurate diagnosis, timely initiation of antiviral therapy, and effective prevention of complications such as endothelial cell loss and secondary glaucoma. By enhancing understanding in these areas, clinicians working within interprofessional teams will be better equipped to collaborate, apply evidence-based strategies, and optimize visual outcomes for patients affected by this vision-threatening condition.

courses.title: Dermatopathology Evaluation of Tumors
courses.description: The evaluation of cutaneous neoplasms requires expertise in both clinical dermatology and dermatopathology. Clinicians generate a differential diagnosis based on the tumor's clinical presentation, integrating knowledge of histopathology, biopsy techniques, and disease pathophysiology to guide diagnostic accuracy. Proper tissue sampling, orientation, and preservation are critical for ensuring high-quality histological assessment. A precise dermatopathologic diagnosis not only facilitates targeted treatment strategies but also improves patient outcomes. Cutaneous neoplasms encompass a diverse spectrum of lesions, including epidermal, adnexal, melanocytic, mesenchymal, and hematolymphoid tumors. The evaluation of these lesions relies on histopathologic examination supplemented by immunohistochemistry and molecular testing when necessary. Recognizing key histologic patterns, differentiating benign from malignant entities, and correlating findings with clinical features are essential skills in dermatopathology. Advances in diagnostic techniques continue to refine tumor classification and prognostication, enhancing clinical decision-making and patient care. This activity for healthcare professionals is designed to enhance learners' proficiency in evaluating skin tumors using clinical dermatology and dermatopathology techniques, as well as following a methodical approach to assessment and diagnosis. Participants will deepen their understanding of the classification, histopathologic features, and diagnostic evaluation of common and some rare skin tumors. The course also covers biopsy techniques, laboratory analyses, and advanced methods like immunohistochemistry and molecular studies to enhance clinicians' dermatopathology practices and improve their diagnostic accuracy. Improved skills will empower healthcare professionals to collaborate within an interprofessional team caring for individuals with cutaneous neoplasms, improving outcomes.

courses.title: Prostate Cancer
courses.description: Prostate cancer is the most commonly diagnosed malignancy worldwide and the sixth leading cause of cancer-related death in men. Diagnosis is primarily based on prostate-specific antigen testing, magnetic resonance imaging scans, and prostate tissue biopsies, although prostate-specific antigen testing for screening remains controversial. New diagnostic technologies are now available, including risk stratification bioassay tests, germline testing, and various positron emission tomography scans. When confined to the prostate, the disease is considered localized and potentially curable. If the disease has spread outside the prostate, bisphosphonates, rank ligand inhibitors, hormonal treatment, chemotherapy, radiopharmaceuticals, immunotherapy, focused radiation, and other targeted therapies can be used. This activity provides a comprehensive review of the current evaluation and management of prostate cancer, highlighting the role of the interprofessional team in improving care for affected patients.

courses.title: Interstitial Cystitis/Bladder Pain Syndrome
courses.description: Interstitial cystitis/bladder pain syndrome is a complex and chronic medical condition that primarily affects the urinary bladder, leading to a range of distressing symptoms. This disorder is characterized by the inflammation of the bladder's lining, resulting in recurring and often severe discomfort, urgency, and frequency of urination. Interstitial cystitis remains challenging to diagnose and manage, as its precise causes are not fully understood, and it can mimic other urinary tract disorders. Individuals living with interstitial cystitis face a significant impact on their quality of life, as the symptoms can be disruptive and emotionally taxing. Patients' responses to treatment are highly variable. This activity reviews the approach, investigation, and management of interstitial cystitis/bladder pain syndrome and highlights the role of the interprofessional team in evaluating and treating this challenging disorder.

courses.title: HIV and AIDS
courses.description: Clinical prevention of HIV and AIDS is the cornerstone of controlling the global HIV pandemic, which has claimed over 44.1 million lives worldwide since the pandemic was recognized. Although a cure remains out of reach, HIV is a chronic illness due to the effectiveness of antiretroviral therapy. Combined with significant advancements in prevention, the goal of halting the global HIV pandemic is now feasible. Current interventions acknowledge the complexity of clinical management, considering socio-economic factors, patient-centered care, continuous quality improvement, and the importance of social and regulatory environments to achieve optimal patient and population outcomes. This activity comprehensively reviews HIV transmission, pathophysiology, clinical presentations, evaluation, up-to-date treatment, reporting, and implementation considerations for specific population groups to prevent the diagnosis of AIDS. Clinicians increase their knowledge, skills, and competence in managing HIV, improving patient outcomes, reducing transmissions, and contributing to global efforts of disease eradication. The role of the interprofessional team is highlighted, emphasizing collaboration among clinical, public health, and interdisciplinary team members.

courses.title: Artificial Intelligence and Deep Learning in the Diagnosis of Pythium Keratitis
courses.description: Artificial intelligence (AI) and deep learning have emerged as transformative tools in ophthalmology, offering new possibilities for early, accurate, and rapid diagnosis of challenging infectious keratitis. Pythium keratitis, an aggressive and vision-threatening ocular infection, often clinically mimics fungal keratitis, leading to delayed diagnosis and suboptimal outcomes. This educational activity introduces learners to state-of-the-art AI-driven diagnostic strategies for enhancing Pythium detection through image-based algorithms, multimodal data integration, and automated pattern recognition. Participants will explore how deep learning models can analyze slit-lamp photographs, anterior segment optical coherence tomography characteristics, and confocal microscopy features to differentiate Pythium from fungal and bacterial etiologies with improved accuracy. The course also reviews current evidence, model performance metrics, workflow integration, and practical considerations for adapting AI tools into real-world clinical environments. By engaging with this content, healthcare professionals will gain an improved understanding of how AI technologies can support earlier diagnosis, guide timely therapeutic decisions, and potentially reduce the need for invasive interventions such as therapeutic keratoplasty. This activity emphasizes how collaboration among ophthalmologists, microbiologists, imaging specialists, and data scientists strengthens clinical competence and accelerates innovation. Ultimately, participants will learn how interprofessional teamwork and AI-enhanced decision support can improve patient outcomes in Pythium keratitis, one of the most rapidly progressive ocular surface infections.

courses.title: Opioid Therapy: Clinical Considerations
courses.description: Opioids. Pain medication. Pain management. Controlled substance prescribing. These words can be challenging for prescribers. Opiates are medications used to manage everything from pain to cough to diarrhea. "Opioid" is an umbrella term that represents all compounds that bind to opioid receptors, which includes compounds derived from poppy seeds, such as morphine and codeine, as well as synthetic opioids like fentanyl. Opioid receptors are found throughout the central and peripheral nervous systems and gastrointestinal tract, regulating many body functions: pain, mood, stress, reward, gastrointestinal functions, and respiration.[1][8][2][27] While opiates have a role in therapeutic decision-making, their use involves significant risks and adverse effects that healthcare providers need to be prepared to manage effectively. Among the spectrum of adverse effects, this course discussion mainly focuses on 3 significant categories: tolerance, dependency, and opioid-associated use disorder. Although these complications differ in their presentation and mechanisms, they highlight the critical need for a comprehensive understanding and careful monitoring to ensure both efficacy and patient safety. This activity explores the characteristics, causes, identification, management, and prevention of these adverse effects, equipping healthcare professionals with the knowledge and tools needed to deliver optimal care when prescribing opioid medications.

courses.title: Cranial Nerve Testing
courses.description: Cranial nerve testing is integral to the general neurologic exam to help identify and localize neurologic pathology. This testing is widely applicable to emergency and clinical situations and can be performed relatively quickly with equipment readily available in the hospital or ambulatory environment. Cranial nerve testing is helpful in monitoring for the progression or worsening of neurologic disease processes, particularly neurotrauma. However, patients suffering from strokes or other intracranial pathologies routinely require frequent monitoring for worsening function or condition. This activity describes cranial nerve testing and explains the role of the interprofessional team in utilizing this testing modality to evaluate and monitor patients for pathologic processes and disease progression.

courses.title: Comprehensive Review of Bioterrorism
courses.description: Bioterrorism involves the deliberate release of bioweapons to cause death or disease in humans, animals, or plants. Biological weapons may be developed or used as part of a government policy in biological warfare or by terrorist groups or criminals. Biological weapons can initiate large-scale epidemics with an unparalleled lethality, and nation-states and terrorist groups have used dangerous and destructive Biological weapons in the past. This activity reviews the types, evaluation, and treatment of different biological weapons that have been used and has the potential to be used in bioterrorism attacks and discusses the role of the inter-professional team in evaluating and treating catastrophic events associated with bioterrorism.

courses.title: Diffuse Toxic Goiter
courses.description: Goiter refers to enlargement of the thyroid gland and may arise from multiple etiologies, most commonly iodine deficiency worldwide and autoimmune disease in the United States. Diffuse toxic goiter represents a hyperfunctioning, diffusely enlarged thyroid that produces excess thyroid hormones and is most often associated with Graves disease, though nonautoimmune causes also exist. This course reviews the common presentations of diffuse toxic goiter, including weight loss, heat intolerance, tremor, palpitations, and neck swelling, with some developing Graves ophthalmopathy or dermopathy. Additionally, this activity reviews the pathophysiology, clinical features, diagnostic evaluation, and evidence-based management of diffuse toxic goiter. Diagnosis relies on thyroid function testing, targeted antibody assays, and imaging when indicated. Management options include antithyroid medications, radioactive iodine therapy, or surgery, each chosen based on patient characteristics, comorbidities, and disease severity. Participants will also gain an understanding of the varied presentations, interpretation of diagnostic findings, appropriate therapy selection, and patient counseling of risks. and long-term follow-up of diffuse toxic goiter. This activity for healthcare professionals is designed to enhance the learner's competence in identifying diffuse toxic goiter, performing the recommended evaluation, and implementing an appropriate interprofessional approach to manage this condition, thereby reducing complications through timely, individualized care and improving outcomes.

courses.title: Sympathetic Ophthalmia
courses.description: Sympathetic ophthalmia is a rare, devastating disease defined as bilateral uveitis following an eye injury. The condition may result in permanent bilateral vision loss in an otherwise healthy patient with no ocular morbidities. Initial symptoms and the timeline for the onset of symptoms after an injury are highly variable. Therefore, sympathetic ophthalmia must be considered within the differential for any presentation of bilateral uveitis. Managing this disease is challenging, requiring several immunosuppressants as part of treatment. Sympathetic ophthalmia is an uncommon, systemic uveitis that develops as a granulomatous inflammation in both eyes after an injury or invasive procedure. Typically emerging within the first 12 months post-injury, the onset can be postponed for several years. This condition is characterized by granulomatous inflammation with distinctive choroidal yellow-white nodules. Early treatment usually involves high doses of corticosteroids, which can elicit a prompt response; however, sustaining the remission often necessitates continuous immunomodulatory agents to curb further flare-ups. This topic equips clinicians with comprehensive knowledge of sympathetic ophthalmia, including its diverse clinical presentations and management strategies. Through collaborative learning, clinicians understand the importance of early diagnosis and tailored treatment plans to prevent irreversible vision impairment. Interprofessional teamwork enhances patient outcomes by facilitating holistic care and integrating ophthalmological expertise with immunological insights. By fostering effective communication and collaboration among specialists, the course empowers healthcare professionals to deliver timely interventions, optimize treatment regimens, and improve overall prognosis for patients with sympathetic ophthalmia.
