courses.title: Peyronie Disease
courses.description: Peyronie disease is a benign disorder causing pain and curvature of the penis during erections. This disease is a disorder of wound healing, scarring, and plaque formation of the penile tunica albuginea, which results in fibrosis and varying degrees of penile angulation when erect. The role of oral medications and supplements, traction therapy, vacuum erection devices, Clostridium histoliticum collagenase and other intralesional injections, iontophoresis, surgery, and various restorative therapies, such as platelet-rich plasma or stem cell penile injections and extracorporeal shockwave therapy, are reviewed. This activity reviews the etiology, pathophysiology, epidemiology, diagnosis, and treatment options for Peyronie disease, encompassing both surgical and nonsurgical approaches.The currently recommended evaluation and management strategies for this disorder are presented, highlighting the role of the interprofessional team in ensuring the best possible patient outcomes.

courses.title: Colon Cancer
courses.description: Colorectal cancer is an increasingly important public health problem in the United States and worldwide. Colorectal cancers have the highest incidence among malignancies after lung cancer, breast cancer in women, and prostate cancer in men. This condition is the second most common cause of cancer-related mortality in the United States. Despite sharing similar disease biology, colon and rectal cancers are considered separately, given the diagnostic technique and treatment differences. Colon cancer is often sporadic and related to risk factors such as age, race, diet, and the presence of inflammatory bowel disease. Hereditary colon malignancies are most commonly associated with Lynch syndrome and genetic polyposis syndromes. Screening colonoscopy is critical in identifying premalignant and early-stage lesions. Surgery is the mainstay of curative treatment, with chemotherapy being a necessary adjunct. Radiation plays an integral role in rectal cancer but is less commonly used to treat colon cancer. This activity for healthcare professionals enhances learners' competence in recognizing symptoms, providing a timely diagnosis, and using best practices when managing colorectal cancer. The course emphasizes the critical importance of screening, particularly colonoscopy, for early detection and prevention and the diagnostic and therapeutic strategies for managing localized and metastatic disease. Through evidence-based discussion, participants explore surgical techniques, the role of adjuvant and systemic therapies, and the integration of targeted biologic and immune checkpoint inhibitors into treatment plans. Special attention is given to interdisciplinary collaboration, tailored approaches for high-risk patient populations, and strategies to optimize patient outcomes while minimizing treatment-related complications. By enhancing diagnostic precision, treatment planning, and team-based care, this activity equips healthcare professionals with the confidence to address the...

courses.title: Complicated Urinary Tract Infections
courses.description: Urinary tract infections (UTIs) are a leading cause of sepsis in hospitalized patients and present a wide spectrum of severity, from simple UTIs that respond well to outpatient antibiotics to complicated UTIs that can escalate to life-threatening urosepsis. This activity provides an in-depth guide to the evaluation, diagnosis, and management of both simple and complicated UTIs. Participants gain insights into current guidelines, including the appropriate use of first-line antibiotics, risk factor assessment, imaging techniques, and the management of specific complications like pyonephrosis, emphysematous cystitis, and recurrent infections. Special emphasis is placed on addressing the practice gap in antibiotic selection, the overuse of broad-spectrum agents, and the challenges of managing UTIs in high-risk populations, including patients with catheters, renal failure, or posttransplantation. This course also highlights the importance of interprofessional collaboration, patient education, and the integration of emerging diagnostic tools and treatments, such as bacteriophages and advanced imaging. This activity equips clinicians to improve patient outcomes, minimize inappropriate antibiotic use, and effectively manage the complexities of UTIs in diverse clinical scenarios.

courses.title: Bell Palsy
courses.description: Bell palsy is the most common paralysis of the seventh cranial nerve, with an onset that is typically rapid and hemifacial. The condition affects 15 to 40 of every 100,000 people annually and recurs in approximately 10% of cases. In addition to unilateral facial paralysis, Bell palsy often also involves a prodrome of otalgia, and many patients additionally report ipsilateral xerophthalmia, epiphora, hyperacusis, nasal obstruction, and dysgeusia. The facial asymmetry accompanying Bell palsy may cause dysarthria, oral incompetence, and difficulty expressing emotions nonverbally, resulting in social isolation and emotional distress. Fortunately, 70% to 80% of patients will recover completely even without treatment, and over 95% recover with prompt pharmacological therapy. In rare cases, surgical intervention may be indicated to protect the eye or improve recovery of facial nerve function. Imaging and laboratory evaluation are unnecessary in most cases, but patients with severe paralysis may undergo electrodiagnostic testing for its prognostic value and to establish candidacy for facial nerve decompression surgery. For patients who do not fully recover from Bell palsy, spastic and dyscoordinated facial contractions (synkinesis) usually develop, necessitating long-term treatment with physiotherapy, botulinum toxin injections, and potential surgical interventions. This activity for healthcare professionals reviews key aspects of Bell palsy, including its etiology, clinical presentation, differential diagnosis, and current approaches to treatment and rehabilitation, from initial presentation to long-term management. The activity also highlights the role of an interprofessional team in improving outcomes for affected patients.

courses.title: Compressive Optic Neuropathy
courses.description: Compressive optic neuropathy (CON) results from intrinsic or extrinsic pressure on the optic nerve, leading to progressive visual dysfunction. Causes include orbital tumors, vascular lesions, inflammatory disease, trauma, and osseous abnormalities, with thyroid-associated orbitopathy and pituitary adenomas representing leading etiologies worldwide. This course reviews the clinical presentation of CON, typically characterized by painless, progressive vision loss, often accompanied by color desaturation, field defects, or changes in the optic disc, as well as the distinguishing features of CON from other optic neuropathies, which can be identified by careful clinical evaluation, detailed imaging, and interdisciplinary collaboration. Untreated disease can progress to irreversible blindness; therefore, timely diagnosis and intervention whether medical, surgical, or radiotherapeutic is essential to preserve or restore vision. This course explores the anatomy, pathophysiology, and clinical features of CON, alongside evidence-based strategies for diagnosis and management. Participants will also gain knowledge of key diagnostic tools such as MRI and perimetry, and recognition of red-flag symptoms. This activity for healthcare professionals is designed to enhance the learner's competence in identifying CON, performing the recommended evaluation, and implementing an appropriate interprofessional approach when managing this condition to prevent irreversible optic nerve damage.

courses.title: Superior Ophthalmic Vein Cannulation for Carotid Cavernous Fistula
courses.description: Superior ophthalmic vein (SOV) cannulation is a specialized endovascular technique used to access the cavernous sinus to treat carotid-cavernous fistulas (CCFs), particularly when traditional transvenous approaches are unsuccessful or contraindicated. The procedure requires detailed knowledge of orbital venous anatomy, advanced imaging interpretation, and precise technical execution to reduce the risk of complications, including hemorrhage, thrombosis, and neurovascular injury. This course reviews the indications, contraindications, anatomical considerations, procedural techniques, imaging guidance, and complication management associated with SOV cannulation. Participants learn to evaluate appropriate candidates, understand procedural planning, and apply strategies that improve safety and treatment effectiveness. Collaboration among clinicians, neurointerventional specialists, ophthalmologists, radiologists, anesthesiology professionals, nursing professionals, and other interprofessional team members promotes coordinated care, enhances procedural precision, reduces complications, and improves outcomes for patients undergoing treatment for CCFs.

courses.title: Antihypertensive Medications
courses.description: Hypertension remains one of the most prevalent and clinically significant modifiable risk factors for cardiovascular disease. This activity reviews contemporary hypertension management based on the 2025 American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association guideline, with emphasis on accurate evidence-based diagnosis, cardiovascular risk stratification, pharmacologic therapy selection, medication optimization, treatment adherence, and long-term longitudinal blood pressure monitoring to reduce morbidity and mortality. This activity addresses these challenges by integrating evidence from clinical trials, practical treatment algorithms, and patient-centered management strategies, including home and ambulatory blood pressure monitoring and team-based care models. In addition, this activity helps clinicians to develop skills in optimizing antihypertensive therapy, interpreting blood pressure monitoring data, managing medication-related adverse effects, and improving adherence through simplified treatment regimens. The activity also emphasizes interprofessional collaboration and the expanding role of digital health technologies in hypertension management, equipping clinicians to deliver coordinated, evidence-based care to reduce cardiovascular complications and improve long-term outcomes.

courses.title: Sleeve Gastrectomy
courses.description: In the United States, obesity has been increasing at an alarming rate over the past 50 years. In 2014, obesity and its comorbidities accounted for 14.3 percent of this country's healthcare expenditure. Weight loss surgery is considered a safe and durable treatment option for obesity. The techniques have been continuously evolving to yield better outcomes. This activity describes the indications, contraindications, and complications associated with sleeve gastrectomy and highlights the role of the interprofessional team in the management of patients with obesity

courses.title: Radiology Patient Safety and Communication
courses.description: In Western medicine and law, the move away from paternalism toward a patient-centered, patient autonomy first approach has made vital the communication of risks with patients to enable patients to make informed choices about their care, as reviewed elsewhere. This activity reviews risks associated with the performance of common diagnostic medical imaging exams, examines patient safety standards set by organizations tasked with preserving public safety, describes strategies to minimize patient safety risks from diagnostic medical imaging, and reviews how radiology exam risks can be communicated between healthcare providers and with patients so that the parties involved understand the risks and can make decisions based on the risks and their personal values, and also covers ethical, legal, other policy-based duties that healthcare providers have in disclosing risks patients may incur from medical imaging. Finally, it describes ways that healthcare providers can work in teams to promote patient safety and communication in medical imaging.

courses.title: Benign Essential Blepharospasm
courses.description: Benign essential blepharospasm is a persistent focal dystonia characterized by involuntary, repetitive contractions of the orbicularis oculi muscles, resulting in excessive blinking, episodic eyelid closure, and, in extreme instances, functional blindness. Although its etiology remains incompletely understood, several pathophysiological mechanisms have been proposed. Historically considered an isolated eyelid disorder, recent research has identified benign essential blepharospasm as a multifaceted neuro-ophthalmic condition characterized by abnormal sensorimotor integration, impaired blink reflex inhibition, and substantial interaction between central motor pathways and peripheral ocular surface physiology. Benign essential blepharospasm often advances incrementally, evolving from minor blinking irregularities to debilitating spasms that hinder driving, reading, mobility, and social engagement. The condition imposes significant psychosocial and functional burdens, with several individuals suffering from anxiety, sadness, sleep difficulties, and reduced quality of life. This course discussion offers an extensive examination of benign essential blepharospasm, encompassing its epidemiology, etiology, pathophysiology, clinical manifestation, diagnostic assessment, and related consequences. A comprehensive analysis of management techniques is provided, highlighting the pivotal role of botulinum toxin injections, ocular surface optimization, behavioral adjustments, and the interdisciplinary approach necessary for sustained care. The activity emphasizes critical differential diagnoses, including hemifacial spasm, reflex blepharospasm, myasthenia gravis, and apraxia of eyelid opening, thereby helping clinicians differentiate benign essential blepharospasm from other conditions that can cause irregular eyelid movements. This activity enhances healthcare professionals' understanding of the pathophysiology of benign essential blepharospasm, contemporary evidence-based...

courses.title: Vesicoureteral Reflux
courses.description: Vesicoureteral reflux (VUR) is characterized by the abnormal backward flow of urine from the urinary bladder into the upper urinary tract during voiding. This condition of retrograde urine flow is often caused by a short intramural ureter and is associated with recurrent urinary tract infections, renal cortical scarring, and renal failure in severe cases, including end-stage kidney disease. Voiding cystourethrogram is the preferred diagnostic tool for diagnosing VUR in children, necessitating collaboration among urologists, surgeons, and radiologists. After the procedure, an antibiotic regimen is customized based on the patient's clinical presentation, kidney anatomy, and treatment response. Surgical interventions are contemplated for recurrent or unresolved VUR. Patient education is crucial and includes treatment options while considering parental concerns and preferences, as VUR is typically diagnosed in children. This activity reviews the anatomy, pathophysiology, clinical presentation, diagnostic methods, and treatment options for VUR while emphasizing the importance of patient education in ensuring the long-term health of children with this condition. This activity highlights the crucial role of a collaborative interprofessional healthcare team, including urologists, surgeons, radiologists, nurses, pharmacists, and technologists, in delivering comprehensive care and assessing and enhancing treatment methods for patients with VUR.

courses.title: Marchiafava-Bignami Disease
courses.description: Marchiafava-Bignami disease (MBD) is a very rare disorder characterized by demyelination and necrosis of the corpus callosum. The adjacent subcortical white matter may also be involved. This activity describes the pathophysiology, etiology, presentation, and management of MBD. Although clinical features may be quite variable and nonspecific, Marchiafava-Bignami Disease should be considered in patients with chronic alcohol use or malnutrition who present with certain neurological symptoms. These symptoms include dementia, altered mental status, spasticity, dysarthria, ataxia, gait abnormalities, and seizures. Other reported clinical findings include desynchronization of bilateral symmetric movements and unilateral signs of agraphia, apraxia, dyspraxia, and anomia. This activity illustrates the evaluation and management of Marchiafava-Bignami Disease and reviews the role of the interprofessional team in improving care for patients with this condition.

courses.title: Perinephric Abscess
courses.description: A perinephric abscess is usually a complication of urologic infection which results from fat necrosis. Before the era of antibiotics, perinephric abscesses were due to prolonged bacteremia. More than 3/4 of perinephric abscesses are now due to complications of urinary tract infections

courses.title: Epilepsia Partialis Continua
courses.description: Epilepsia partialis continua (EPC) is a rare condition involving recurrent and sometimes intractable focal onset seizures associated with retained awareness. EPC seizures can occur over hours, days, or even years. The disease can manifest in a variety of ways, a few of which include myoclonic epilepsy, localized myoclonus, Jacksonian epilepsy, or sensorimotor clonic seizures. The localized nature of the seizures along with preserved consciousness and postictal confusion and weakness (Todd paralysis) are characteristic of the disorder but not pathognomonic. Treatment is centered on a combination of anti-epileptics coupled with identification and resolution of the underlying cause. This activity reviews when epilepsia partialis continua should be considered, how to properly evaluate for it, and the role of the interprofessional team in caring for patients with this condition.

courses.title: Asthma: Allergic, Nonallergic, and Environmental Phenotypes
courses.description: Asthma is a heterogeneous chronic inflammatory airway disease that can cause preventable exacerbations, hospitalizations, respiratory failure, and death when diagnosis and treatment are delayed or incomplete. This continuing medical education activity reviews evidence-based evaluation, phenotype-guided treatment, risk stratification, care for acute exacerbations, patient education, and referral criteria. The activity addresses the gap between guideline-recommended asthma care and inconsistent clinical practice, including overreliance on short-acting bronchodilator therapy, incomplete assessment of inflammatory phenotype, inadequate inhaler education, and delayed specialist referral. Participants will strengthen diagnostic reasoning, select appropriate controller and biologic therapies, recognize high-risk findings such as silent chest, reduce preventable complications, and coordinate care across the interprofessional healthcare team to improve patient-centered outcomes.

courses.title: Optic Neuritis
courses.description: Optic neuritis is a vision-threatening disorder and often the first symptom of demyelinating diseases such as multiple sclerosis. Infections, autoimmune diseases, and certain medications may also trigger this condition. Symptoms typically include sudden vision loss, eye pain (especially with eye movement), and changes in color perception. Some individuals may also experience the Marcus Gunn pupil, an abnormal response to light. Diagnosis involves a thorough clinical evaluation and the use of advanced imaging modalities, particularly optical coherence tomography and magnetic resonance imaging. Blood tests may be taken to exclude other conditions. Management often starts with high-dose intravenous corticosteroids to reduce inflammation and accelerate recovery. For individuals with underlying conditions like multiple sclerosis, disease-modifying therapies may be introduced to help prevent future episodes. The prognosis is generally positive, with most people experiencing partial or full recovery of vision within weeks to months. However, some may face persistent visual impairment, and the risk of recurrence or developing multiple sclerosis varies based on individual factors. This activity for healthcare professionals is designed to enhance learners' proficiency in evaluating and managing optic neuritis. Participants gain deeper insights into the condition's etiology, risk factors, pathophysiology, symptomatology, and best diagnostic and therapeutic practices. Clinicians will learn how to differentiate optic neuritis from other causes of vision loss and explore the relationship between this condition and systemic diseases. Increased competence enables healthcare practitioners to collaborate effectively within an interprofessional team caring for affected individuals, improving outcomes.

courses.description: The management of hormone receptor positive (HR-positive), human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 negative (HER2-negative) metastatic breast cancer (mBC) is undergoing rapid transformation, largely driven by the imperative to overcome acquired endocrine resistance, frequently mediated by somatic estrogen receptor 1 (ESR1) mutations. To address these gaps in testing and treatment, and ensure that clinicians can effectively evaluate the mechanisms of action and efficacy data of new and emerging next-generation SERDs, this educational activity utilizes the RE-AIM training and implementation model to 1) facilitate peer-to-peer learning at the point of care around novel and emerging oral SERDs and oral SERD combinations; and 2) build the appropriate infrastructure, clinical capacity, and training in oncology practices to optimally adopt these novel therapies in patients with estrogen receptor-positive/HER2-negative mBC.

courses.title: Batten Disease (Juvenile Neuronal Ceroid Lipofuscinosis)
courses.description: Neuronal ceroid lipofuscinoses (NCLs), or Batten disease, are a group of devastating and lethal neurodegenerative lysosomal storage diseases that typically affect children. The disease is known to have 14 forms, each resulting from mutations in a distinct gene. Juvenile neuronal ceroid-lipofuscinosis (JNCL), also called Spielmeyer-Vogt-Sjögren disease or CLN3, is the most common inherited, autosomal recessive, neurodegenerative disorder. It is characterized by progressive loss of vision, seizures, and loss of cognitive and motor functions, leading to premature demise. JNCL is caused by mutations of CLN3, a gene that encodes a hydrophobic transmembrane protein, which localizes to membrane lipid rafts in lysosomes, endosomes, synaptosomes, and cell membranes. The absence of the CLN3 protein affects numerous cellular functions, including pH regulation, arginine transport, membrane trafficking, and apoptosis. CLN3 disease is a rare neurodegenerative disease causing not only vision loss and decline in cognitive and motor skills but also altered behavior and emotions. Declines in physical and cognitive skills give rise to certain emotions and behaviors that differ for each individual, although general characteristics can be found. This activity describes the epidemiology, genetics, clinical presentation, and management of JNCL, providing healthcare professionals with the knowledge and tools to improve patient care for this complex and prevalent condition. This activity highlights the role of an interprofessional healthcare team in supporting and managing patients with this complex condition.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Nerve Conduction Studies and Electromyography
courses.description: Electrodiagnostic tests are electrophysiological techniques used to evaluate the function and integrity of peripheral nerves, nerve roots, plexuses, the neuromuscular junction (NMJ), and muscles. Electrodiagnostic tests are classified into 2 main types needle electromyography (EMG) and nerve conduction studies (NCS), which also include repetitive nerve stimulation. NCS and EMG are performed as extensions of the physical examination, providing valuable information on abnormalities affecting the nerves, muscles, or both. Electrodiagnostic studies are crucial in neuromuscular diagnosis, and they help localize lesions, differentiate between sensory and motor involvement, distinguish axonal from demyelinating patterns, and determine the condition's progression. NCS evaluates nerve conduction velocity and amplitude, whereas EMG assesses muscle activity, including spontaneous activity, motor unit action potentials, and recruitment patterns. These tests aid in diagnosing conditions such as neuropathies, radiculopathies, plexopathies, and NMJ disorders. Although these tests are generally considered safe, potential complications include infection, bleeding, and tissue injury. This activity reviews the indications and importance of NCS and EMG in evaluating peripheral nerve, the NMJ, and muscle physiology and diseases, as well as diagnosing related disorders. This activity assesses disease severity, identifies the level of injury, predicts prognosis, and guides follow-up. This activity also emphasizes the importance of collaboration among interprofessional healthcare providers to ensure effective patient care and improve treatment outcomes.

courses.title: Doppler Abdominal Aorta Assessment, Protocols, and Interpretation
courses.description: Doppler ultrasound is a vital, noninvasive imaging tool for evaluating the abdominal aorta, providing critical insights into vascular structure and hemodynamics without the risks of contrast exposure or ionizing radiation. Whether used in radiology suites or as point-of-care ultrasound in emergency and resource-limited settings, mastering Doppler ultrasound of the abdominal aorta is essential for timely diagnosis, risk stratification, and management of vascular diseases.

courses.title: Spontaneous Intestinal Perforation of the Newborn
courses.description: Spontaneous intestinal perforation in the newborn is defined as a single bowel wall perforation typically occurring in the terminal ileum. It is a life-threatening condition that affects very low birth weight infants (birth weight of less than 1500 g) and extremely low birth weight (birth weight of less than 1000 g) infants. The exact pathophysiology of spontaneous intestinal perforation is a subject of debate. Prematurity and low birth weight are significant risk factors. Diagnosis relies on the typical radiographic finding of pneumoperitoneum. Spontaneous intestinal perforation is associated with significant morbidity and mortality. Timely diagnosis, prompt surgical consultation, and management are of utmost importance. This activity reviews the incidence, pathophysiology, and role of the interprofessional team in managing spontaneous intestinal perforation.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Clinical Significance of Volume of Distribution in Pharmacotherapy
courses.description: The volume of distribution (Vd) is a key pharmacokinetic parameter that influences drug dosing, half-life, and the relationship between plasma drug concentration and total body drug exposure. Although Vd is a theoretical construct, changes in physiological and clinical conditions, such as obesity, critical illness, hypoalbuminemia, and drug-drug interactions, can significantly alter drug distribution. These changes may affect measured drug concentrations and therapeutic response. Failure to recognize such alterations can lead to inappropriate dose selection or misinterpretation of therapeutic drug monitoring results. This activity focuses on the clinical interpretation of Vd across diverse patient populations and physiological states. This activity reviews the fundamental principles of Vd, including its relationship with clearance and bioavailability, as well as factors influencing drug distribution, such as plasma protein binding, tissue sequestration, and transporter- or enzyme-mediated drug interactions. This activity also emphasizes how patient-specific variables can modify pharmacokinetic behavior and affect dosing strategies. In addition, this activity highlights the important role of the multidisciplinary healthcare team in applying pharmacokinetic principles to medication management. Through interprofessional collaboration in prescribing, dispensing, administering, and monitoring medications, healthcare professionals can integrate pharmacokinetic reasoning into routine clinical practice. By applying evidence-based principles of drug distribution and dose optimization, this activity aims to support safer prescribing practices, improve therapeutic outcomes, and enhance individualized patient care through rational dose optimization and vigilant monitoring.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Mohs Micrographic Surgery: Evaluation and Treatment of Nonmelanoma Skin Cancer
courses.description: Nonmelanoma skin cancers (NMSC), including basal cell carcinoma (BCC) and squamous cell carcinoma (SCC), represent the most prevalent skin malignancies in the United States. Despite their typically slow-growing and locally invasive nature, both forms demand prompt recognition and thoughtful management due to the potential for significant tissue destruction and, in the case of SCC, metastatic risk. Chronic ultraviolet (UV) radiation exposure is the primary etiologic factor, with genetic mutations contributing to the pathogenesis of the condition. Additional risk factors include immunosuppression, lighter Fitzpatrick skin types, environmental carcinogens, and occupational hazards. Mohs micrographic surgery is a tissue-sparing surgical technique employed by Mohs surgeons in dermatology practices worldwide and remains the gold standard for treating NMSC, providing patients with very high cure rates and cosmetically pleasing outcomes. However, Mohs micrographic surgery is not used for every NMSC, and thus, specific criteria guide physicians in determining when this procedure is indicated. This course explores NMSC diagnosis and treatment, including identifying high-risk features, recognizing early clinical signs, and selecting appropriate management strategies based on lesion subtype and patient characteristics. Special emphasis will be placed on the use of Mohs micrographic surgery, which offers superior cure rates and maximal tissue preservation for NMSC, particularly in cosmetically sensitive areas. Participants will also explore diagnostic enhancements with dermoscopy, biopsy strategies, and multidisciplinary approaches for advanced or nonsurgical cases. This activity for healthcare professionals is designed to enhance the learner's competence in implementing evidence-based insights into prevention, risk stratification, and treatment planning for patients with NMSC utilizing an appropriate interprofessional approach, improving outcomes through precision in...

courses.title: Robotic Radical Cystectomy of the Bladder
courses.description: Robotic radical cystectomy is a surgical technique for managing muscle-invasive bladder cancer and high-risk non-muscle invasive bladder cancer. Historically, open radical cystectomy with bilateral pelvic lymph node dissection and urinary diversion was the gold standard. However, the rise of minimally invasive surgery in urology has led to the widespread adoption of robotic cystectomy, including intracorporeal urinary diversion surgery. Typically, this surgery for urothelial cancer is preceded by neoadjuvant cisplatin-based chemotherapy and is now common in tertiary care centers for invasive bladder cancer. Despite its technical challenges, long learning curve, longer operative times, higher costs, high complication rate, and significant morbidity similar to the open approach, robotic radical cystectomy has gained popularity. This procedure has demonstrated various perioperative benefits, including less intraoperative blood loss, reduced transfusion rates, better rates of positive margins, more lymph nodes recovered, and shorter hospital stays while maintaining similar oncologic outcomes compared to open surgery. Therefore, perioperative protocols are essential to reduce the risk of postoperative complications and promote enhanced recovery. This activity focuses on surgical indications, operative techniques, complications, and multidisciplinary care involved with robotic radical cystectomy, primarily focusing on robotic radical cystectomy rather than partial cystectomy. This activity also provides clinicians with a comprehensive understanding of the latest techniques and technologies, including patient selection, preoperative planning, intraoperative strategies, and postoperative care. In addition, this activity emphasizes the role of multidisciplinary healthcare professionals in the care of patients undergoing robotic radical cystectomy with bilateral pelvic lymph node dissection and urinary diversion surgery.

Healthcare professionals must understand how to identify suitable candidates, establish realistic treatment goals, and select appropriate administration methods for deucravacitinib therapy. courses.title: Paraphenylenediamine Toxicity
courses.description: Paraphenylenediamine toxicity is an emerging public health concern in developing countries due to both intentional self-harm and accidental poisoning. Paraphenylenediamine is a common agent in hair dyes, and its concentration in these products is largely unregulated. Potential clinical manifestations may range from local toxicity, primarily with dermatologic presentations, to systemic toxicity, which could present as multiorgan failure and possibly death. Despite the potential for significant morbidity and mortality, clinician awareness remains largely low in developed countries. As there is currently no antidote for paraphenylenediamine, the mainstay of management is to have a high index of suspicion and to ensure early intervention and clinical support. As reported cases of toxicity rise, it becomes vital that healthcare professionals are educated regarding the potential dangers of this toxin. This activity aims to illuminate the etiology, epidemiology, clinical presentations, and underlying pathophysiology of paraphenylenediamine toxicology and also reviews the related management and preventive strategies. Participants are empowered with the necessary tools and expertise to ensure optimal patient care and to improve patient outcomes.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Calcium Deposition and Other Renal Crystal Diseases
courses.description: Renal crystallopathies are a group of underdiagnosed and underrecognized disorders associated with the accumulation of crystalline particles in the renal tubules and interstitium, causing acute kidney injury and progressive chronic kidney disease. This discusses the four main types of crystalline deposition, the pathologic findings and clinical manifestations. Genetic causes, acquired causes, their pathogenesis, histological features, diagnosis, and treatment options will also be addressed. While rare many of these conditions can lead to end-stage renal disease, especially in the pediatric population. There are many therapeutic interventions that can be made to improve renal outcomes. Early recognition and treatment are key to preventing reversible kidney disease.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Obesity and Type 2 Diabetes
courses.description: Obesity is a major global health concern and a leading contributor to the development and progression of type 2 diabetes (T2D). Since 1990, adult obesity has more than doubled, and childhood obesity has quadrupled. As of 2022, 1 in 8 people worldwide was living with obesity. Excess body weight increases the lifetime risk of T2D, from 7% to 70% in men and 12% to 74% in women, as body mass index (BMI) increases. Effective management of obesity is crucial for the prevention and treatment of T2D. Lifestyle interventions, pharmacological therapies, and bariatric surgery have all been shown to reduce the incidence of diabetes and improve glycemic control. Even modest weight loss (5% 10%) can lead to significant metabolic improvements and, in some cases, diabetes remission. Clinicians should screen all patients with obesity for T2D and follow evidence-based guidelines to tailor treatment. BMI remains the primary metric for classifying weight status, with lower thresholds recommended for Asian populations due to higher diabetes risk at lower BMI levels. Although the World Health Organization classifies obesity as a chronic disease (code 5B81), its designation remains debated due to lacking a universal clinical definition. Regardless, early identification and comprehensive, individualized treatment are essential for reducing the global burden of diabetes. This activity reviews the treatment of patients with obesity and diabetes, including lifestyle modification, pharmacological therapy, and metabolic and bariatric surgery. This activity also underscores the importance of interprofessional collaboration in implementing evidence-based strategies and achieving optimal outcomes in preventing and managing these interrelated conditions.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Ureterocele
courses.description: A ureterocele is a congenital anomaly affecting the distal intramural part of the ureter. A ureterocele is commonly associated with a duplex urinary system that adheres to the Meyer-Weigert rule, which predicts the drainage pattern of duplicated kidneys. Detecting ureteroceles directly on antenatal scans can be challenging. However, they can often be identified through the presence of fetal hydronephrosis or duplicated renal systems on these scans. Early detection of this condition is crucial, as it can prevent significant morbidities, including infection, bladder-neck obstruction, and, most importantly, loss of function of the upper renal moiety. This activity reviews the pivotal role of interdisciplinary collaboration in improving care for patients with ureteroceles by giving the learner a comprehensive understanding of the diagnosis and management of ureteroceles and associated congenital anomalies in the fetal urinary system. Collaboration and expertise across disciplines are essential in providing the best care for affected individuals.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Trisomy X Syndrome
courses.description: Trisomy X syndrome is the most common female sex chromosomal aneuploidy, with an extra X chromosome occurring in 1 per 1000 females. Despite this prevalence, only about 10% of affected individuals receive a diagnosis; however, detection rates are expected to increase with the expansion of prenatal screening. This condition presents with variable phenotypes of varying severity, requiring a high index of suspicion for diagnosis. In this activity, the etiology and clinical presentations of trisomy X syndrome are discussed. Specifically, learners identify variable patient phenotypes and associations between this condition and behavioral health disorders. Evidence suggests that early diagnosis and behavioral modifications may improve long-term outcomes for patients and their caregivers. In addition, women with this condition can experience primary ovarian insufficiency, impacting fertility and necessitating intervention in patients who desire to have children. Upon completion of this activity, learners should be able to support individuals with trisomy X as members of an interprofessional team and recognize current gaps in the evidence regarding the natural history and management of this condition.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Prostatic Urethral Lift
courses.description: The prostatic urethral lift (PUL) is a minimally invasive procedure to alleviate urinary symptoms in patients with benign prostatic hyperplasia. This procedure involves placing small implants to hold the enlarged prostate tissue away from the urethra, thereby reducing obstruction without cutting, heating, or removing tissue. PUL is typically performed under local, spinal, or general anesthesia and offers a shorter recovery time compared to traditional surgical methods like transurethral resection of the prostate. Patients often experience immediate symptom relief and a quicker return to normal activities. Clinicians participating in this course gain comprehensive knowledge about the indications, procedural techniques, and postoperative care associated with the PUL. The course covers patient selection criteria, preoperative evaluations, and the technical aspects of implant placement. Additionally, the course addresses potential complications, postoperative management strategies, and the importance of interprofessional communication and care coordination to optimize patient outcomes.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Urinary Crystals Identification and Analysis
courses.description: Urinary crystal formation is a marker of urinary supersaturation with different substances and can occur secondary to inherited diseases, metabolic disorders, or drugs. Urine sediment examination by microscopy is an excellent tool for clinicians to understand underlying pathology, although it is often not performed. Different crystals have recognizable appearances and patterns. The presence of crystals can be a clue to underlying disease pathologies. Commonly associated conditions include hyperoxaluria, hypercalciuria, hyperuricemia, metabolic syndrome, and drug-related crystalluria. Proper identification of urinary crystals can aid in selecting therapeutic interventions, from dietary changes to prescribing or discontinuing medications. Given the significant prevalence of nephrolithiasis, proper diagnosis and treatment of risk factors can decrease patient morbidity. This activity reviews the methods used in urine sediment examination and the appropriate identification of various urinary crystals. Participants learn to recognize different types of urine crystals, understand their clinical significance, and apply this knowledge to improve patient outcomes. This activity also highlights the role of the interprofessional team in identifying and interpreting urine crystals, leading to more accurate diagnoses and targeted and effective treatment plans for patients with nephrolithiasis and other urinary crystal associated diseases.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: CART Cell Therapy Toxicity
courses.description: Chimeric antigen receptor-T (CAR-T) cell therapy is an evolving treatment entity used to treat relapsed/refractory cancers. It involves genetically modifying autologous or allogeneic T cells to express Chimeric Antigen Receptor (CAR) proteins that target specific cancer cells. Despite promising outcomes, these cells attack normal tissue cells expressing similar proteins on their surfaces. This cross-reactivity results in adverse events (AEs), leading to substantial mortality and morbidity. This activity reviews the evaluation and treatment of CAR-T toxicity and highlights the role of interprofessional teams in evaluating and treating patients with these AEs.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Double Outlet Right Ventricle
courses.description: Double outlet right ventricle, in which at least 50% of both great arteries arise from the morphologic right ventricle, represents 8% to 9% of all conotruncal anomalies. Double-outlet right ventricle is a highly complex and heterogeneous group of anatomic conditions, with a spectrum ranging from tetralogy of Fallot to transposition of the great arteries. Many classification schemes have been proposed during the past 50 years and continue to be debated. The treatment of this group of conditions continues to evolve, and surgical techniques range from biventricular repair with an intraventricular baffle to univentricular staged palliation, including ventricular septal defect (VSD) closure, Rastelli procedure, arterial switch operation, and double root translocation. The physiology and appropriate surgical treatment require a firm understanding of the relationship between the great vessels and the location of the VSD, which is itself determined by the spiraling septation of the primitive truncus. This activity reviews the embryology, anatomy, epidemiology, pathophysiology, diagnosis, and surgical treatment of this group of lesions. This activity provides healthcare professionals with the knowledge and tools to effectively care for this highly complex patient population in an era in which best surgical practices continue to evolve.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Immune-Mediated Oral Mucosal Diseases
courses.description: Mucosal lesions of the oral cavity are common and encompass a broad range of conditions. Many of these disease processes are immune-mediated or represent an oral manifestation of a systemic immunologic disease. Oral mucosal lesions related to immune dysfunction or presumed autoimmune etiologies may be symptomatic, seriously affecting quality of life, and serve as an associated comorbidity in high-risk patient populations. The clinical presentations of these lesions are often nonspecific, subtle, and ever-changing in appearance; typically, they require detailed evaluation of patient histories, histopathologic studies, and multidisciplinary consultation for definitive diagnosis. Management varies from simple observation to complex systemic therapies. Patients may find treatments to provide unsatisfactory or inconsistent results but may also be content with simple, noninvasive therapies. This activity reviews the etiology, evaluation, identification, and management of the commonly discussed immune-mediated mucosal lesions of the oral cavity. The role of the multidisciplinary healthcare team involved in treating patients with these conditions is discussed.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Blepharophimosis Syndrome
courses.description: Blepharophimosis syndrome (BPES), which stands for blepharophimosis, ptosis, epicanthus inverse syndrome, is a rare genetic disorder primarily affecting eyelid development, resulting in a distinct facial appearance. The syndrome is characterized by: Telecanthus: Increased distance between the inner corners of the eyes Ptosis: Drooping of the upper eyelid Epicanthus inversus: Upward fold of skin near the inner corner of the eye These features define BPES. The disruption of the development of the eyelid and associated tissues during embryogenesis is the cause of the structural abnormalities observed in BPES. The severity and subtype of BPES can vary, with some individuals experiencing significant visual impairment from ptosis, whereas others may have cosmetic concerns. The condition is restricted to the structural flaws that are present from birth and does not tend to spread. However, ptosis can lead to other issues, including amblyopia, if left untreated, which emphasizes the need for early detection and surgery. BPES is classified into 2 types. The 4 traditional clinical signs telecanthus, epicanthus inversus, ptosis, and blepharophimosis are present in every form. Type I is linked to early ovarian failure. Only the traditional facial traits define type II. If left untreated, these characteristics are linked to a high risk of amblyopia. Early surgical intervention is necessary for both types to ensure normal development of eyesight. This activity reviews the clinical presentation, assessment, treatment, and management of BPES, emphasizing the role of an interprofessional healthcare team including endocrinologists, genetic counselors, and other medical professionals in optimizing patient care and outcomes.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Dermatopathology of Metabolic and Storage Diseases
courses.description: Systemic metabolic and storage disorders often present with subtle, nonspecific skin changes that can be key indicators of underlying disease. Accurate diagnosis requires strong clinicopathologic correlation, with histopathologic evaluation playing a critical role. However, interpreting these findings can be challenging, even for experienced dermatopathologists, due to the rarity of these conditions and their dermatologic manifestations. This activity reviews the clinical and histopathologic features of metabolic and storage disorders, including vitamin disturbances, necrolytic erythemas, lysosomal storage diseases, mucinoses, amyloidosis, and others. Participants gain the skills required to identify subtle histologic clues, improve diagnostic accuracy, and enhance patient care.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Anthracycline Toxicity
courses.description: Toxicity complicates the administration of anthracycline chemotherapy agents in treating cancer in high-risk patients in a dose-dependent manner. Anthracycline-induced cardiotoxicity stands as a serious complication, often manifesting as severe, irreversible cardiac failure, posing life-threatening risks. Effective evaluation protocols before, during, and after anthracycline administration are crucial in early detection, prevention, and timely intervention against this disorder. This activity reviews assessment strategies, including advanced cardiac monitoring and imaging techniques, to enable early identification of cardiac issues associated with anthracycline treatment and explores preventive management and treatment modalities critical in mitigating the impact of cardiotoxicity on patients' health outcomes. The activity also highlights the role of the interprofessional, multidisciplinary team in caring for patients susceptible to or affected by anthracycline toxicity while emphasizing timely intervention and comprehensive evidence-based management strategies to improve clinical outcomes.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Thin Basement Membrane Nephropathy
courses.description: Thin basement membrane nephropathy (TBMN), also known as thin basement membrane disease, is a genetic disorder that affects the glomerular basement membrane (GBM). TBMN is characterized by microscopic hematuria, typically with normal kidney function and the absence of proteinuria. TBMN results from mutations in genes encoding type IV collagen, leading to widespread and uniform thinning of the GBM. TBMN usually presents as isolated microscopic hematuria, which may be dysmorphic, without significant proteinuria, renal dysfunction, or hypertension. Although TBMN shares some overlapping features with Alport syndrome, such as its genetic basis and involvement of type IV collagen, the course and prognosis of these 2 diseases differ significantly, requiring distinct management strategies. Unlike Alport syndrome, TBMN generally does not involve extrarenal symptoms and follows a more benign clinical course. The diagnosis of TBMN is often based on clinical presentation and family history, with renal biopsy showing diffuse thinning of the GBM. A family history of progressive renal disease is usually absent, and in such cases, a renal biopsy may not be necessary for a definitive diagnosis. Management is typically conservative, as most patients do not require specific treatment due to the benign nature of the disease. This activity reviews the pathogenesis, evaluation, and management of TBMN and also highlights the critical roles of the interprofessional healthcare team in evaluating and treating patients with this condition.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Laboratory Evaluation of Hereditary Hemochromatosis
courses.description: Hereditary hemochromatosis is a common inherited disorder of iron metabolism characterized by excessive intestinal iron absorption and progressive iron accumulation in body tissues. Although hereditary hemochromatosis has a high prevalence in populations of Northern European ancestry and occurs with similar frequency in the United States, Europe, and Australia, many affected individuals remain asymptomatic for years, leading to delayed or incidental diagnosis. When left unrecognized or untreated, iron overload can result in significant organ damage involving the liver, pancreas, heart, pituitary gland, and other endocrine organs, with a markedly increased risk of hepatocellular carcinoma. This educational activity provides a comprehensive overview of hereditary hemochromatosis, focusing on its pathophysiology, clinical presentation, and natural history. Learners gain insight into evidence-based diagnostic strategies, including the appropriate use of iron studies and genetic testing, as well as approaches to disease monitoring and long-term management. Emphasis is placed on early detection and timely intervention to prevent irreversible complications. Participation in this activity highlights the critical role of the interprofessional healthcare team, including pathologists, laboratory professionals, primary care providers, hepatologists, and nurses, in improving diagnostic accuracy, coordinating care, and optimizing patient outcomes. Through collaborative practice and informed clinical decision-making, healthcare professionals can significantly reduce morbidity and enhance the quality of care for patients with hereditary hemochromatosis.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

practice_areas: Advanced Heart Failure and Transplant Cardiology

courses.title: Urinary Tract Infections In Children
courses.description: Urinary tract infection remains a significant source of morbidity in children, specifically uncircumcised males in the first year of life and females throughout their lives. To avoid morbidity and long-term complications, urinary tract infections in children must be promptly diagnosed and treated. Optimized urine collection techniques are essential to reduce false positive test results and unnecessary antibiotic treatments. Appropriate imaging studies are equally critical for accurate diagnosis. The American Academy of Pediatrics offers clear guidelines on antibiotic prophylaxis and treatment, focusing on tailoring testing and treatment to improve outcomes and ultimately enhance the quality of life for pediatric patients and their families. Healthcare professionals can expect to gain a comprehensive understanding of urinary tract infection diagnosis and management, from reviewing diagnostic tools to emphasizing the role of infection prevention and antibiotics stewardship. Clinicians will also understand the need for collaborative efforts among multiple subspecialists in pediatrics and the importance of an interprofessional team in optimizing care for children with urinary tract infections.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Familial Atypical Multiple Mole and Melanoma Syndrome
courses.description: Familial atypical multiple mole melanoma (FAMMM) syndrome is a hereditary condition that significantly increases the lifetime risk of cutaneous melanoma and, in some cases, pancreatic cancer. Characterized by the presence of numerous clinically atypical nevi with irregular borders, variable pigmentation, and a tendency for recurrence, FAMMM requires early recognition and lifelong dermatologic surveillance to reduce morbidity and mortality associated with melanoma. This educational activity provides an in-depth review of the epidemiology, molecular genetics, pathophysiology, clinical presentation, diagnostic criteria, and management of FAMMM syndrome. Clinicians will gain tools to distinguish FAMMM from other dysplastic nevus syndromes and to implement effective screening and risk-reduction strategies for high-risk individuals. Special attention is given to the role of genetic counseling, including indications for CDKN2A mutation testing and implications for family members. By engaging in this activity, learners will enhance their competence in early detection and management, ultimately improving outcomes through timely interventions. The activity emphasizes the critical contributions of dermatologists, oncologists, genetic counselors, primary care providers, and nurses in delivering coordinated, patient-centered care. This interprofessional approach fosters better risk communication, more effective surveillance, and improved adherence to prevention guidelines, reinforcing the importance of a team-based strategy in managing hereditary melanoma syndromes.

courses.title: Stroke Imaging
courses.description: Diagnostic neuroimaging is recommended for all suspected stroke cases, progressing from noncontrast computed tomography to advanced vessel and perfusion modalities to optimize the timely diagnosis and hyperacute management of stroke. This course reviews the distribution of cerebral arteries, which is fundamental to accurate diagnosis and management of acute ischemic stroke, including the anterior and posterior circulations, interconnected by the circle of Willis, that supply distinct brain territories, and the associated characteristic clinical deficits that occur when these areas are compromised. Participants will gain an understanding of neurovascular clinical-radiological correlation, early CT ischemic signs (including ASPECTS scoring), multiphase vessel imaging, and the identification of vessel occlusion and salvageable tissue. Advanced imaging workflows, including CT perfusion, multiphase CT angiography, and MRI mismatch are emphasized to guide eligibility for extended-window thrombolysis and endovascular thrombectomy in early, extended, and large ischemic core presentations. This activity for healthcare professionals is designed to enhance learners' competence in applying diagnostic neuroimaging principles, following recommended stroke imaging algorithms, interpreting complex imaging findings, and implementing an appropriate approach to managing stroke.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Cryoglobulinemic Glomerulonephritis
courses.description: Cryoglobulinemia is a disorder characterized by the precipitation of immunoglobulins, known as cryoglobulins, at temperatures below 37 C. Cryoglobulinemia results from abnormal B-cell proliferation and is often associated with B-cell lymphoproliferative disorders, autoimmune diseases, or chronic infections such as hepatitis C virus. This condition is defined by the presence of these cryoglobulins, and when clinical symptoms occur, cryoglobulinemic vasculitis is diagnosed. The cryoglobulins can precipitate and obstruct small vessels, causing ischemia, or they can deposit in the vasculature and cause leukocytoclastic vasculitis. Cryoglobulinemia can lead to end-organ damage due to systemic vasculitis, including glomerulonephritis, and is associated with an increased risk of cardiovascular disease, significantly contributing to morbidity and mortality. Three main types of cryoglobulinemia exist, and identification and classification of these types aid in selecting appropriate therapeutic interventions. This activity reviews cryoglobulinemia and cryoglobulinemic glomerulonephritis, emphasizing their classification, pathophysiology, histology, diagnostic challenges, renal histopathology, and management strategies.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Fluvoxamine
courses.description: Fluvoxamine is a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor that received US Food and Drug Administration approval in 1994 for the treatment of obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) in adults and pediatric patients aged 8 years and older. Obsessive-compulsive disorder is a mental health disorder characterized by persistent, unwanted thoughts (obsessions) and repetitive behaviors (compulsions) that cause significant distress and impair daily functioning. Fluvoxamine enhances the action of serotonin by blocking its reuptake at the neuronal membrane. This medication has a uniquely high affinity for the sigma-1 receptor compared to other SSRIs, which may contribute to its therapeutic effects. This activity provides a comprehensive review of fluvoxamine's clinical pharmacology, therapeutic uses, dosing strategies, contraindications, adverse effects profile, and key drug-drug interactions. Special attention is given to safety considerations in pediatric and older adults, as well as its role in managing treatment-resistant obsessive-compulsive disorder and off-label applications. Interprofessional knowledge of fluvoxamine's properties enables clinicians, pharmacists, and mental healthcare professionals to optimize treatment plans, enhance medication adherence, and improve patient outcomes. This activity is designed to support informed decision-making and promote collaborative care in the management of obsessive-compulsive disorder and related disorders.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Mohs Micrographic Surgery Section of Specimens Using Cryostat, Stain, and Immunostain
courses.description: Mohs micrographic surgery (MMS) is a highly effective, gold-standard treatment for managing many cutaneous malignancies due to its high cure rates and tissue-conserving nature. In MMS, unlike other surgical techniques, the surgeon also serves as the pathologist, ensuring complete histological clearance of the tumor. Specialized processing techniques are used to prepare, section, and stain tissue, allowing thorough examination of both peripheral and deep margins. The tissue is prepared using a cryostat to create frozen sections, which are stained with hematoxylin and eosin stains or immunostains, such as MART-1 for melanoma. Proper specimen processing, including the use of a cryostat and various staining methods (such as immunostaining), is crucial for the accurate interpretation of fresh-frozen sections and successful MMS outcomes. High-quality slides allow the surgeon to thoroughly evaluate tumor margins and characteristics, minimize complications, and achieve high cure rates. As tissue conservation is a key aspect of MMS, well-prepared specimens help prevent false-positive margins and processing artifacts, avoiding unnecessary removal of additional skin and reducing patient harm. This activity reviews techniques for preparing and sectioning specimens using a cryostat, staining, and immunostaining, providing surgeons with the essential knowledge to properly process tissue, identify and troubleshoot common processing errors, and enhance patient care.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Electrophysiology Study and Ablation of Atrioventricular Nodal Reentrant Tachycardia
courses.description: Atrioventricular nodal reentrant tachycardia (AVNRT) is the most common regular, sustained paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia. AVNRT affects mainly young and middle-aged otherwise healthy adults. An electrophysiology study is mandatory to definitively diagnose and differentiate this arrhythmia from other supraventricular tachycardias with similar electrocardiographic features. Catheter ablation is currently the best therapeutic option for symptomatic patients, and while not without risk, it is generally very well-tolerated. This activity reviews the role of electrophysiology study and catheter ablation in the diagnosis and treatment of AVNRT and highlights the role of the healthcare team in the management of patients with this arrhythmia.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

practice_areas: Advanced Heart Failure and Transplant Cardiology

courses.title: Retroperitoneal Liposarcoma
courses.description: Retroperitoneal liposarcoma is a rare and challenging malignancy that arises in the retroperitoneal space, constituting a significant subset of soft tissue sarcomas. Characterized by the proliferation of malignant adipocytes, this tumor presents a unique diagnostic and therapeutic challenge due to its insidious onset and deep-seated location. Because retroperitoneal liposarcomas can grow to substantial sizes before detection, patients often receive a late-stage diagnosis, complicating surgical resection. Imaging studies typically suggest the diagnosis, but a needle biopsy is usually required for confirmation, histological classification, and tumor grading. Complete surgical resection remains the cornerstone of curative therapy, as achieving negative margins significantly impacts prognosis. Although metastases are less common than in other soft tissue sarcomas, they can occur and necessitate vigilant surveillance and timely intervention. Despite its rarity, retroperitoneal liposarcoma has considerable morbidity and mortality, requiring a high index of suspicion for early diagnosis and a multidisciplinary approach for optimal management. This activity reviews the etiology, epidemiology, pathology, clinical presentation, and management of retroperitoneal liposarcoma. In addition, this activity explores key aspects of retroperitoneal liposarcoma, including its epidemiology, histology, diagnostic modalities, differential diagnoses, and treatment approaches. This activity also provides healthcare professionals with the knowledge and tools necessary to enhance patient care for this complex malignancy.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Familial Combined Hyperlipidemia
courses.description: Familial combined hyperlipidemia (FCH) is a hereditary metabolic disorder characterized by elevated levels of total cholesterol, triglycerides, low-density lipoprotein (LDL) cholesterol, and decreased levels of high-density lipoprotein (HDL) cholesterol. FCH is one of the most common hereditary lipid disorders. In addition, this disease is associated with an increased risk of developing cardiovascular disease, including atherosclerosis and coronary heart disease. Despite its prevalence and potential health consequences, FCH is often underdiagnosed and undertreated, making it a topic of ongoing research to understand its underlying genetic and metabolic mechanisms better and develop effective treatment strategies. This activity reviews the etiology, pathophysiology, evaluation, and management of familial combined hyperlipidemia. It also examines the role of the interprofessional team in improving care for patients with this condition.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: n-hexane Toxicity
courses.description: n-Hexane toxicity is a critical topic for healthcare professionals, especially those involved in occupational health, medical toxicology, and neurology. This condition primarily arises from workplace exposure, especially in industries requiring solvent use, such as paint, varnish, and glue manufacturing. Risk factors include prolonged or excessive exposure to n-hexane, lack of adequate ventilation, failure to use proper protection when working with the chemical, and a lack of occupational safety protocols. Individuals with preexisting neurological conditions are at greater risk. The pathogenesis involves n-hexane's metabolism into toxic byproducts, particularly 2,5-hexanedione, which can lead to neuronal damage, especially in peripheral nerves. The toxic effects manifest through various symptoms, including peripheral neuropathy, weakness, numbness, and motor coordination difficulties. Chronic exposure may lead to more severe neurological deficits. Diagnosis relies on clinical assessment, patient history, and sometimes electromyography and nerve conduction studies to evaluate nerve function. Management focuses on eliminating further exposure and initiating symptomatic treatment. Supportive therapies, such as physical rehabilitation, may aid recovery in affected individuals. Prognosis varies based on the duration and severity of exposure; some may experience significant recovery, while others may have lasting neurological deficits. Early intervention improves outcomes, emphasizing the importance of monitoring and minimizing exposure in at-risk populations. This activity for healthcare professionals is designed to enhance learners' proficiency in evaluating and diagnosing n-hexane toxicity. Trainees gain deeper insights into the condition's pathophysiology, epidemiology, diagnosis, prevention, and management, focusing on how metabolites like 2,5-hexanedione disrupt nerve function. Greater competence enables clinicians to work within an interprofessional team caring...
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Electrophysiology Study and Ablation of Atrial Flutter
courses.description: Catheter radiofrequency ablation is an evolving field that offers a viable solution for patients with recurrent arrhythmias. While the procedure boasts a high success rate for various atrial arrhythmias, especially atrial flutter, it has significant risks. Diagnosing and managing atrial flutter can vary significantly depending on the flutter type and circuit direction. Therefore, it is crucial to thoroughly understand proper anatomy, techniques, and risks associated with the procedure. Additionally, informing patients about these potential risks before intervention is prudent. This ensures that patients clearly understand the possible complications and can make informed decisions regarding their treatment. This activity focuses on the indications, contraindications, and procedural techniques involved in atrial flutter ablation, highlighting the importance of an interprofessional team in delivering comprehensive care to patients undergoing this procedure.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

practice_areas: Advanced Heart Failure and Transplant Cardiology

courses.title: Mohs Micrographic Surgery of Uncommon Tumors (Angiosarcoma, Eccrine, Paget, and Merkel Cell)
courses.description: Mohs micrographic surgery (MMS) is widely used to treat common cutaneous malignancies such as squamous and basal cell carcinomas. Due to its high cure rates and tissue preservation, MMS is warranted as an alternative for treating rare tumors. In recent years, several international research groups have studied and reported on the efficacy and outcomes of MMS in treating uncommon cutaneous malignancies (UCMs), such as angiosarcoma, Merkel cell carcinoma, eccrine malignant tumors, and Paget disease. Although UCMs generally have poorer prognoses compared to common cutaneous malignancies, MMS shows promise for their treatment. Many UCMs lack distinctive clinical features, making early diagnosis challenging when based solely on clinical characteristics. Typically, UCMs are treated with wide local excisions, but MMS has been increasingly used as an alternative, supported by case reports and series demonstrating its benefits. However, the use of MMS is debated due to the high metastatic potential of some tumors, such as angiosarcoma and Merkel cell carcinoma. This activity explores the role of MMS in UCM treatment, discussing the epidemiology, etiology, clinical presentation, and histological findings of various UCMs, where MMS has shown increasing relevance in recent literature. Additionally, this activity highlights the advantages and disadvantages of using MMS as an alternative treatment for the above-mentioned UCMs. This activity provides interprofessional healthcare providers with the knowledge and tools to enhance decision-making when evaluating treatment options for patients with UCMs, ensuring the highest standard of care for affected patients.

courses.title: Electrophysiology Study and Ablation of Atrial Tachycardia
courses.description: Electrophysiology study and ablation of atrial tachycardia (AT) involve mapping the heart's electrical activity to identify and treat abnormal focal sites responsible for the arrhythmia. Focal ATs arise from specific areas of the atria, most commonly within the right atrium, and are characterized by regular atrial activation independent of the sinus and atrioventricular nodes. Ablation targets these foci to restore normal rhythm, using techniques guided by electroanatomical mapping and intracardiac signals. This approach is highly effective for unifocal AT, with catheter ablation offering low complication rates and durable outcomes for most patients. Clinicians participating in this course will gain in-depth knowledge of atrial tachycardia anatomy, pathophysiology, and mechanisms. The course will equip healthcare professionals with the skills to diagnose ATs accurately, interpret complex electrophysiology study results, and implement state-of-the-art ablation techniques. Through case-based learning and expert guidance, participants will also enhance their ability to manage challenging AT cases, optimize patient outcomes, and improve procedural safety.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Oral Health Considerations for Patients With Systemic Disease
courses.description: Due to demographic and population changes, advances in the medical and surgical management of systemic diseases, and improvements in population oral health, there are increasing interactions between oral healthcare providers and medical providers. These interactions are often aimed at supporting patient care and dental management in the context of systemic disease and its associated management and therapy. This educational activity reviews the role of clinicians and dentists in detecting, diagnosing, evaluating, and managing patients with common systemic diseases. This activity explores the impact of systemic disease on dental treatment options and the potential effects of dental treatments on systemic disease management. The bidirectional relationship between oral and systemic health and therapy facilitates the exploration of the role of interdisciplinary teams in delivering care to individuals with systemic diseases and oral health needs. The increasing evidence for the role of the oral cavity in overall health, as well as the impact of overall health on the oral cavity, is also explored and discussed. By increasing the knowledge base of oral healthcare providers and medical providers regarding dental management considerations for patients with systemic diseases, this educational activity helps decrease barriers to understanding and increase the potential for meaningful interactions and collaboration across healthcare settings, ultimately benefiting patients.
