courses.title: Ambulatory ECG Monitoring
courses.description: This activity provides clinicians with a comprehensive review of ambulatory electrocardiogram monitoring, with emphasis on device selection, clinical indications, and interpretation of findings across a range of cardiac conditions. Despite the availability of evidence-based guidelines and an expanding array of monitoring technologies, a significant practice gap exists in the consistent application of appropriate monitoring strategies for conditions such as cryptogenic stroke, syncope, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, and atrial fibrillation. This activity addresses that gap by equipping clinicians with updated knowledge of monitoring modalities, including Holter monitors, patch recorders, mobile cardiac outpatient telemetry, and implantable loop recorders. Participants are expected to gain improved diagnostic accuracy, enhanced risk stratification skills, and the ability to select monitoring strategies tailored to individual patient presentations, ultimately supporting better patient outcomes and more informed clinical decision-making.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Laboratory Assessment of Thyroid Function
courses.description: Laboratory assessment of thyroid function is essential for diagnosing and monitoring thyroid diseases, which are common and often present with nonspecific symptoms. Thyroid disorders can arise from primary thyroid gland disease or secondary hypothalamic-pituitary dysfunction, leading to either the overproduction (hyperthyroidism) or underproduction (hypothyroidism) of thyroid hormones. In addition, thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) resistance, caused by genetic mutations in the TSH receptor, drug-induced thyroid disorders, pregnancy-related thyroid conditions, and nonthyroidal illnesses (such as those following acute or chronic diseases, including acute psychiatric disorders), may also occur. Thyroid function tests (TFTs) measure TSH, T3, and T4 levels, aiding in the diagnosis of conditions such as hypothyroidism, hyperthyroidism, and other thyroid dysfunctions. TFTs are widely utilized due to their high sensitivity and specificity. The thyroid gland regulates metabolism and mood through T4 and T3 hormones, which are controlled by the hypothalamic-pituitary-thyroid axis. Certain tests, such as TSH, T3, and T4, along with additional markers, support accurate diagnosis. However, TSH testing has limitations in cases of central hypothyroidism, subclinical disease, and medication interference, necessitating careful interpretation. This activity outlines the etiology of thyroid disease and TFTs, including sample requirements, analytical methods, interpretation, interferences, clinical significance, and further testing. This activity also highlights the importance of collaboration among healthcare providers to ensure accurate diagnosis and comprehensive patient care throughout the evaluation and management of thyroid disorders.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Treatment of Cutaneous Malignancies With Topical, Oral, and Injectable Medication
courses.description: Skin cancer is one of the most common malignancies globally, with rising incidence rates, particularly in the United States, where approximately 1 in 5 individuals is expected to develop the disease by age 70. The primary types basal cell carcinoma, squamous cell carcinoma, and melanoma pose unique treatment challenges. Nonsurgical treatment options, including topical, oral, and injectable agents, are increasingly used to manage tumors while preserving function and cosmetic outcomes. The therapeutic landscape for cutaneous malignancies is diverse, with treatments tailored to the cancer type and stage. Standard interventions include surgical excision and Mohs micrographic surgery, which precisely removes cancerous tissue while sparing healthy surrounding skin. Radiation therapy offers a noninvasive alternative by using high-energy beams to target and destroy tumor cells. For advanced or difficult-to-treat cases, systemic treatments such as chemotherapy, immunotherapy, and targeted biologics have become critical components of care. This activity explores commonly used topical therapies, oral chemotherapeutic agents, and biologics in the management of cutaneous malignancies. This activity also aims to equip healthcare providers with the knowledge and skills necessary to effectively use topical, oral, and injectable medications to treat skin cancers. In addition, this activity underscores the importance of interprofessional collaboration among healthcare providers in understanding the therapeutic efficacy, potential adverse effects, and clinical implications of these treatments, as well as in implementing a coordinated care approach for optimal patient outcomes.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Menstrual Suppression
courses.description: Medication-induced secondary amenorrhea involves the intentional use of hormonal contraceptive medications to suppress menstruation or induce amenorrhea. Patients or their caregivers may opt for menstrual suppression for various reasons, such as alleviating menstrual-related symptoms, managing specific health conditions, or enhancing overall quality of life. This practice is particularly pertinent for certain demographics, including adolescents, individuals with disabilities, military personnel, athletes, and those undergoing cancer treatment. Hormonal agents like combined hormonal contraceptives, progestin-only contraceptives, long-acting reversible contraceptives, gonadotropin-releasing hormone agonists, or testosterone can be utilized based on individual preferences and health requirements. Participants in this course gain a thorough understanding of the indications and methodologies of menstrual suppression, tailored to the diverse needs of various patient groups. They learn to navigate the nuanced considerations involved in recommending and managing menstrual suppression, particularly for special populations like adolescents and individuals with disabilities. Moreover, the course emphasizes the significance of collaboration within an interprofessional team to optimize patient outcomes. By working together, healthcare professionals can pool their expertise and perspectives to develop tailored care plans that address each patient's unique needs and preferences. This collaborative approach enhances the quality of care and fosters a holistic understanding of the patient's health and well-being beyond mere symptom management.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Renal Abscess
courses.description: Renal abscesses are rare but severe infections that arise from complicated urinary tract infections or bacteremia, often due to untreated pyelonephritis or hematogenous spread. These infections lead to localized collections of pus within the renal parenchyma or perinephric space, predominantly affecting patients with diabetes, immunosuppression, or urinary tract abnormalities. Accurate diagnosis relies on imaging, with contrast-enhanced computed tomography scans regarded as the gold standard. Ultrasound and magnetic resonance imaging are valuable alternatives for certain populations. Managing renal abscesses represents a critical intersection of infectious disease, nephrology, and interventional radiology. This activity unravels the complexities of renal abscesses, tracing their progression from subtle infections to potentially life-threatening emergencies. This activity examines treatment pathways by comparing conservative medical management with the nuanced criteria for surgical intervention. This activity also provides interprofessional healthcare providers with the knowledge and tools to effectively manage renal abscesses, promote patient safety, and optimize outcomes while emphasizing their role in developing a cohesive management plan that prioritizes early detection, prompt imaging, timely pharmacological intervention, and image-guided procedures. In addition, this activity fosters a collaborative approach among interprofessional healthcare providers, reinforcing the significance of each team member in the continuum of care from initial suspicion to treatment and follow-up empowering them to excel in managing renal abscesses.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Sebaceous Carcinoma
courses.description: Sebaceous carcinoma is a rare, aggressive malignancy originating from the sebaceous glands, with an estimated incidence rate of approximately 2 cases per million people per year. The condition is classified based on location, whether periocular or extraocular, with the former type having greater metastatic potential. This tumor is associated with Muir-Torre syndrome, a subtype of hereditary nonpolyposis colorectal cancer (Lynch syndrome), presenting with cutaneous sebaceous tumors and internal malignancies due to DNA microsatellite instabilities. The 5-year overall survival rate is 78% for localized disease and 50% for metastatic cases. However, the survival rate continues to improve with increased disease awareness and advanced excision procedures, such as Mohs micrographic surgery. This activity for healthcare professionals is designed to enhance learners' proficiency in evaluating and managing sebaceous carcinoma, with particular emphasis on the therapeutic role of Mohs micrographic surgery. Participants gain a deeper understanding of the condition's epidemiology, clinical presentation, diagnostic modalities, and treatment strategies, equipping them with the expertise needed for accurate diagnosis and effective patient care. Greater competence enables clinicians to collaborate within an interprofessional team caring for individuals with sebaceous carcinoma, improving outcomes.

courses.title: Xylazine Toxicity
courses.description: Xylazine toxicity is a critical and emerging public health concern associated with severe respiratory and central nervous system depression, significant cardiovascular effects, and potentially disfiguring and life-threatening skin ulcers. The increasing prevalence of xylazine as an adulterant in the opioid and nonopioid supply for patients with substance use disorder is a public health emergency. The heightened risk of death due to xylazine toxicity and lack of a specific antidote underscores the dire need for prompt identification, comprehensive evaluation, and appropriate management. This activity outlines the identification, evaluation, and management of xylazine toxicity, reviews the array of presenting symptoms and potential complications, including distinctive skin ulcers, and highlights the role of interprofessional healthcare team efforts in improving care for patients affected by xylazine toxicity, emphasizing the significance of collaborative efforts spanning from acute management to preventive and rehabilitative measures for people suffering from xylazine toxicity.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Kabuki Syndrome
courses.description: Kabuki syndrome is a rare inherited genetic syndrome caused by mutations in either the KMT2D or KDM6A gene. These mutations affect methylation, leading to abnormal growth and development. Kabuki syndrome is often recognized by the characteristic facial features that are thought to resemble traditional Japanese Kabuki theatre actors. The condition has a heterogeneous phenotype and affects multiple body systems, leading to craniofacial abnormalities, hearing loss, vision problems, congenital heart defects, feeding difficulties, immune dysfunction, poor growth, skeletal and dermatoglyphic abnormalities, and difficulties with cognition and development. There is no treatment other than symptomatic management and prevention of complications. This activity reviews the genetic basis for Kabuki syndrome, its clinical manifestations, diagnostic considerations, and management. By participating in this activity, healthcare professionals enhance their knowledge of diagnostic accuracy, improve patient care, and stay current with evolving practices when managing Kabuki syndrome. This course also highlights the importance of an interprofessional healthcare team in providing comprehensive, individualized care for patients with this rare syndrome.

courses.title: Enteropathic Arthritis
courses.description: Arthritis is a recognized manifestation associated with several medical conditions, including inflammatory bowel disease, bacterial gut infections, gluten-sensitive enteropathy, parasitic infections, pseudomembranous colitis, Whipple disease, and following intestinal bypass surgery. Studies reveal connections between alterations in gut microflora and joint inflammation, particularly with enteropathic arthritis. Enteropathic arthritis can manifest as peripheral, axial, or a combination of both, ranging from subclinical inflammation on imaging to severe symptoms with functional limitations. Effective treatment should address both arthritic and bowel manifestations, with options such as nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, glucocorticoids, disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs, and biological agents. The advent of biological therapies has significantly improved outcomes for inflammatory bowel disease and associated arthropathies. Within this activity, participants explore the etiology, pathophysiology, evaluation, and management of enteropathic arthritis, gaining essential knowledge and tools to enhance patient care and overall outcomes while navigating this complex condition. By engaging with the course content, learners deepen their understanding of the relationship between gut health and joint inflammation, as well as refine their skills in diagnosing and treating enteropathic arthritis effectively. Moreover, participation in this course fosters interprofessional collaboration and communication among healthcare teams, facilitating a holistic approach to patient care and optimizing treatment strategies through shared expertise and perspectives.

courses.title: Bariatric Surgery Malnutrition Complications
courses.description: The emergence of bariatric surgeries and their significant impact on the management of morbid obesity have brought about numerous healthcare and economic benefits through surgical interventions. However, it is essential to acknowledge that post-surgical complications, particularly those related to malnutrition, are widespread and often prone to misdiagnosis or inadequate treatment. Recent evidence suggests a rise in malnutrition-related complications, while patient adherence to supplementation and post-operative monitoring fails to match this upward trend. Given the increasing popularity of bariatric surgery as an obesity treatment, it becomes essential to recognize and understand these complications and their associated symptoms of nutritional deficiencies. This undertaking aims to examine the malnutrition complications following bariatric surgery, emphasizing the crucial role of the interprofessional team in evaluating and addressing these issues in patients.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Point-of-Care Testing
courses.description: Point-of-care testing is clinical laboratory testing performed at or near the site where patient care is delivered. Unlike traditional laboratory testing, which may involve delays in sample transport and result reporting, point-of-care testing offers rapid turnaround times that support timely clinical decision-making. Advances in technology, including miniaturized electronics and improved instrumentation, have enabled devices to become smaller, more accurate, and more accessible across various healthcare settings. This development allows a broad range of healthcare professionals, and in some cases even patients, to perform testing that informs immediate treatment decisions. The rapid availability of results has the potential to improve both clinical and economic outcomes by streamlining care, preventing delays in therapy, and enhancing patient satisfaction. Through this activity, participants develop competence in evaluating the methodology, benefits, and limitations of point-of-care testing while enhancing skills in interpreting and applying results to patient care. The activity emphasizes strategies for integrating testing into care workflows, identifying factors that may compromise accuracy, and selecting the most suitable test for the clinical situation. Collaboration among clinicians, pharmacists, and laboratory professionals is crucial to ensure accurate test utilization, prevent misinterpretation, and align treatment decisions with patient safety goals. By strengthening interprofessional communication, participants learn to support effective care coordination, improve diagnostic precision, and reduce the risk of unnecessary delays or adverse outcomes. Ultimately, this activity equips the healthcare team to deliver high-quality, patient-centered care while improving efficiency and overall outcomes.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Desmoplastic Trichoepithelioma
courses.description: Desmoplastic trichoepithelioma (DTE) is a rare, benign skin tumor that arises from hair follicles. DTE typically presents as a small, firm, and asymptomatic nodule, often located on the face, particularly in women during middle age. Characterized by a slow-growing, indolent nature, DTE can resemble other skin lesions, including basal cell carcinoma (BCC), necessitating a careful histopathological examination for accurate diagnosis. The tumor's distinguishing features include nests of basaloid cells surrounded by a dense, desmoplastic stroma, mimicking the fibrous tissue commonly seen in scar formation. Although benign, DTE is often excised to prevent misdiagnosis and for cosmetic reasons. This activity provides an in-depth review of DTE's clinical presentation, histopathological features, and differential diagnosis, particularly its resemblance to BCC. Participants learn about current best practices in diagnostic techniques, including dermatoscopy, histological examination, and treatment approaches, emphasizing when surgical intervention is necessary. The activity highlights the role of an interprofessional team in managing this rare condition, ensuring better patient outcomes, and reducing unnecessary treatments.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Myocardial Viability
courses.description: Myocardial viability refers to dysfunctional myocardium that, despite acute or chronic ischemia, retains the capacity to recover systolic function following revascularization. Ischemic injury produces both irreversible damage and adaptive states such as hibernating or stunned myocardium, in which contractile dysfunction persists in a low-perfusion environment yet remains potentially reversible. Assessment of myocardial viability is critical in chronic ischemic cardiomyopathy, chronic total coronary occlusion, and late-presenting ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction to guide revascularization decisions. Left ventricular ejection fraction serves as a key prognostic indicator in this population. This activity equips the participant with foundational knowledge of viability assessment techniques, interpretation of imaging findings, and clinical decision-making to optimize outcomes. Collaboration among an interprofessional team, including cardiology, radiology, and nursing, enhances diagnostic accuracy, coordinates timely interventions, and improves functional recovery and survival.

courses.title: Acute Rheumatic Fever
courses.description: Acute rheumatic fever (ARF) is an abnormal immunologic response to group A Streptococcus (GAS) infections, most commonly tonsillopharyngitis. ARF affects multiple organ systems and may have cardiac, neurologic, musculoskeletal, or dermatological manifestations. While ARF most commonly occurs in children, it can affect people of any age. The recurrence rate of ARF is very high, particularly in patients with limited access to healthcare. Severe or recurrent bouts of ARF can result in significant morbidity and mortality and the development of rheumatic heart disease (RHD). The mainstay of ARF treatment includes GAS eradication therapy, management of symptoms, and secondary prophylaxis against recurrence. Prompt diagnosis and treatment of ARF are essential in preventing complications and consequences of the disease. This course explores the complexities surrounding ARF pathogenesis, presenting symptoms and signs, complications, evaluation, and short- and long-term management. This activity for healthcare professionals is designed to enhance the learner's competence in identifying the clinical features of ARF, performing the recommended evaluation, and implementing an appropriate interprofessional approach when managing this condition to optimize patient outcomes.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Epidermolysis Bullosa
courses.description: Epidermolysis bullosa (EB) defines a group of rare, inherited dermatoses that present with repeated blistering, erosions, and ulceration in response to seemingly disproportionate mechanical trauma. This occurs due to genetically-mediated skin fragility defects within the dermo-epidermal junction. An extensive phenotypic range is described. Some forms of epidermolysis bullosa place patients at an increased risk of infection, disabling deformities secondary to heavy scarring, and aggressive cutaneous malignancy, often causing early fatality. A broad range of extra-cutaneous manifestations can lead to significant morbidity and premature mortality. In the absence of curative treatment, the current focus of care prioritizes preventing and relieving symptoms and their complications. More recently, novel therapeutics, including topical gene therapies, have gained approval for increased symptomatic improvement of this otherwise intractable group of conditions. This activity outlines the presentation, pathophysiology, evaluation, and management of epidermolysis bullosa, and describes the vital role of the interdisciplinary team in treating extra-cutaneous complications. Areas of research are highlighted pertaining to preventative and abortive clinical strategies, emphasizing the use of gene replacement therapy.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Laboratory Evaluation of Acute Leukemia
courses.description: Acute leukemia, encompassing acute lymphoblastic leukemia and acute myeloid leukemia, is a complex condition resulting from the malignant transformation of hematopoietic progenitor cells, leading to immature blast accumulation in the bone marrow and disruption of normal hematopoiesis. Hematologists utilize a range of laboratory tests to comprehensively evaluate acute leukemia, which is critical for diagnosis, classification, and treatment planning. Complete blood count and peripheral blood smear are essential tests to assess the quantity and morphology of blood cells while identifying abnormalities indicative of leukemia. Bone marrow aspiration and biopsy are crucial procedures for evaluating bone marrow cellularity, blast percentage, and hematopoietic cell maturation. Flow cytometry is used to identify cell surface markers, aiding in the classification of leukemia subtypes and the assessment of minimal residual disease. Cytogenetic analysis, including karyotyping and fluorescence in situ hybridization, detects chromosomal abnormalities essential for diagnosis and prognosis. Molecular studies, such as polymerase chain reaction and next-generation sequencing, identify specific gene mutations and translocations, providing detailed insights into the disease s genetic and molecular profile. This activity provides hematologists with the necessary skills to classify leukemia subtypes accurately, stratify patients into appropriate risk groups, and develop personalized treatment plans. This activity also facilitates the use of targeted therapies that address the specific genetic and molecular characteristics of each patient s leukemia, ultimately improving patient outcomes. In addition, this activity further emphasizes the importance of effective collaboration among healthcare professionals to ensure precise diagnoses and optimal management strategies.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Thrombopoietin Receptor Agonists
courses.description: Thrombopoietin receptor agonists (TPO-RAs) are hematopoietic growth factors that bind to the thrombopoietin receptors on megakaryocytes and hematopoietic stem cells, inducing the activation of Janus kinase/signal transducer and activator of transcription (JAK-STAT), mitogen-activated protein kinase pathway (MAPK), and phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K-AKT) pathways. Scientists have developed second-generation non-immunogenic thrombopoietic agents, including eltrombopag, lusutrombopag, avatrombopag, and romiplostim, for treating thrombocytopenia caused by different factors that may increase the risk of hemorrhage. TPO-RAs have diverse clinical uses, such as treating severe aplastic anemia, managing medical conditions in adults suffering from chronic immune thrombocytopenia refractory to prior treatments, helping with periprocedural thrombocytopenia in individuals with chronic liver disease, and controlling thrombocytopenia that occurs due to interferon-based therapy for hepatitis C. These agents are classified as megakaryocyte growth factors and work by stimulating megakaryocyte activation, proliferation, and maturation, thereby leading to increased circulating platelets, much like thrombopoietin's effect on its receptor. This activity focuses on the indications, mechanism of action, administration, and box warnings associated with TPO-RAs. In addition, this activity reviews off-label uses, pharmacokinetics, drug interactions, toxicity, and other relevant clinical details concerning TPO-RAs to help interprofessional healthcare team members effectively address thrombocytopenia caused by hematologic and hepatic conditions to enhance patient outcomes.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Benign and Malignant Iris Tumors
courses.description: Iris tumors comprise a rare yet significant category of pathological ocular conditions. Iris tumors may be benign or malignant, either of which has the capacity to compromise vision via various mechanisms. There is significant overlap in the clinical presentation of iris tumors, and a comprehensive understanding of critical differentiators facilitates early, accurate diagnosis and implementation of appropriate therapeutic interventions to preserve vision and reduce associated morbidity and, in the case of malignant tumors, mortality. This activity reviews the etiology, epidemiology, pathogenesis, histopathology, clinical characteristics, evaluation, management, and prognosis of various benign and malignant iris tumors. The activity also highlights the role of the interprofessional team in the evaluation and long-term management of iris tumors to improve outcomes for patients with these ocular conditions.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Laboratory Evaluation of Infertility
courses.description: Infertility is increasingly prevalent, affecting an estimated 15% of couples. A comprehensive workup of infertility is critical to diagnose the infertile couple. Laboratory and radiographic evaluations include pituitary, ovarian, tubal, and uterine testing and semen analysis. Upon diagnosis, appropriate treatment options can be presented and discussed with patients. This dialogue allows patients to make informed treatment decisions regarding their diagnosis and what interventions best suit their individual situation. Assisted reproductive technology has helped millions of couples conceive. This activity reviews the laboratory evaluation of infertile couples and highlights the role of the interprofessional team in assessing and treating patients with infertility. This course reviews the basic laboratory workup for laboratory personnel and clinicians and focuses on the etiology, epidemiology, pathophysiology, and diagnostic tests used in infertility evaluations.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Multiple Birth Delivery
courses.description: Unlike singleton pregnancies, the mode and timing of delivery for multifetal gestation is based on the type of twins or higher order multiples, with an evaluation of maternal and fetal complications. There are no clear guidelines on the best mode of delivery for all types of multiples. Techniques for vaginal delivery of twins include internal podalic version as well as breech extraction of twin B. Multifetal gestations, regardless of the mode of delivery, are associated with increased maternal and neonatal morbidity. To avoid the high morbidity associated with multifetal gestation, a multidisciplinary team must be available to provide adequate care to both the mother and her infants. This activity reviews multiple birth delivery and highlights the role of the healthcare team in managing and improving care for patients with multifetal gestation who undergo either vaginal or cesarean delivery. Clinicians can expect to gain a comprehensive understanding of the complexities and challenges associated with delivering twins or higher-order multiples. Unlike singleton pregnancies, multifetal gestations involve a nuanced evaluation of maternal and fetal complications to determine the most appropriate mode and timing of delivery. Participants will become knowledgeable on the criteria for determining whether a patient with multifetal gestation is a suitable candidate for vaginal delivery, empowering the patient to make informed decisions while providing optimal care for both mother and infants.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Osteomyelitis Imaging
courses.description: Osteomyelitis is the inflammation of bone and marrow, most typically due to an infectious process. Osteomyelitis may occur in patients of any age. Osteomyelitis is a disease with significant morbidity that can be challenging to diagnose. In addition to clinical assessments and laboratory studies, imaging results play a significant role in evaluating patients with suspected osteomyelitis. Plain radiography is the typical first step in the radiologic evaluation of patients with osteomyelitis. While plain films can identify bone changes, ultrasound has limited sensitivity for bone involvement. Computed tomography provides detailed cross-sectional images, but magnetic resonance imaging offers superior soft tissue resolution and sensitivity for early bone marrow changes. Nuclear medicine techniques aid in detecting infectious processes within the bone but lack specificity. Osteomyelitis needs to be diagnosed accurately and early to implement effective management. This activity reviews the strategic use, role, and limitations of plain radiography, computed tomography, magnetic resonance imaging, and nuclear medicine in diagnosing acute, subacute, and chronic osteomyelitis.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Acute Acoustic Trauma
courses.description: Acute acoustic trauma (AAT) is characterized by sudden sensorineural hearing loss caused by exposure to intense impulse noise, such as blasts or gunshots, typically exceeding 140 dB for less than 0.2 seconds. Hearing loss from AAT results from the blast s impact and the rapid expansion of gases. AAT often results from mechanical and metabolic injuries to the auditory system, causing symptoms such as hearing loss, tinnitus, otalgia, vertigo, and hyperacusis. AAT is distinct from noise-induced hearing loss, which develops gradually due to prolonged exposure to noise levels of 100 to 120 dBA, often found in workplaces or combat zones. Although AAT is prevalent among military personnel, it is frequently underdiagnosed in civilians due to underreporting. Healthcare providers face challenges in effectively diagnosing and managing AAT. The management strategy begins with advanced hearing protection devices; audiometric evaluations are essential before and after exposure. Prompt intervention can often prevent permanent hearing loss from hazardous noise exposure. Accurate diagnosis relies on audiometric evaluation and timely otolaryngology referral, especially for complications such as tympanic membrane perforation or facial nerve involvement. Treatment emphasizes hearing protection and managing ear trauma, while noise safety education and regular audiometric evaluations are essential for preventing permanent hearing loss. This activity reviews the characteristics, causes, diagnosis, management, and prevention of loud noise-induced injuries. This activity provides healthcare professionals with the knowledge and tools to deliver optimal patient care, including insights into the psychoacoustics of loudness, active and passive hearing protection methods, and the role of medical and surgical interventions in treating AAT.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Preventing Cervical Cancer: Best Practices in Pap and HPV Testing
courses.description: Cervical cancer remains a major global health concern, disproportionately affecting women in regions without effective screening programs. In the United States, the widespread implementation of Papanicolaou testing and human papillomavirus vaccination has significantly reduced the incidence and mortality of cervical cancer. This activity reviews the etiology, epidemiology, and pathophysiology of cervical cancer, emphasizing the role of high-risk human papillomavirus infection and the progression through cervical dysplasia. This activity highlights evidence-based screening recommendations, Papanicolaou cytology techniques, human papillomavirus co-testing, and updated guidelines from major organizations, including the United States Preventive Services Task Force, the American Cancer Society, the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists, and the American Society for Colposcopy and Cervical Pathology. Clinicians learn to identify appropriate screening intervals, interpret Bethesda System results, and manage abnormal findings across diverse populations. This activity also addresses specimen collection techniques; the evolution of cytopathology; diagnostic procedures, such as colposcopy; and the importance of vaccination and patient education. Participants can expect to strengthen their ability to coordinate care, improve follow-up systems, and apply trauma-informed practices during pelvic exams. Enhanced collaboration among clinicians, advanced practitioners, nurses, laboratory professionals, and public healthcare providers supports comprehensive, patient-centered cervical cancer prevention and care.

courses.title: Water Vapor Thermal Ablation of the Prostate
courses.description: Water vapor ablation of the prostate (WVAP) is a minimally invasive surgical treatment for lower urinary tract symptoms caused by benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH). WVAP relieves prostatic urethral obstruction by ablating the hyperplastic tissues restricting urine flow. Ablation is achieved by directly injecting water vapor produced by convective heat transfer into the obstructing prostatic tissue. WVAP is an effective, minimally invasive treatment alternative for carefully selected men experiencing moderate to severe lower urinary tract symptoms. This procedure is particularly effective in men with larger prostatic volumes and is the only procedure that allows for relief of obstruction due to enlargement of the prostatic median lobe. Additionally, WVAP requires only minutes to complete, can be performed in various settings, and may be performed with local anesthesia in select patients. This activity reviews the indications, patient selection protocols, surgical techniques, outcomes, complications, and postoperative care protocols for WVAP and highlights the role of the interprofessional healthcare team in improving outcomes for men with symptomatic BPH undergoing this minimally invasive procedure.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Corticobasal Degeneration
courses.description: Corticobasal degeneration (CBD) is a rare, progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by asymmetric motor dysfunction, cognitive impairment, and various extrapyramidal and cortical symptoms. Classified as a 4-repeat tauopathy, it has pathological findings, including tau-positive neuronal and glial inclusions, astrocytic plaques, and neurodegeneration primarily affecting the basal ganglia and frontoparietal cortex. Clinically, CBD manifests with limb rigidity, dystonia, apraxia, myoclonus, and cognitive decline, often overlapping with corticobasal syndrome, progressive supranuclear palsy, and other tauopathies. Diagnosis remains challenging due to heterogeneity in presentation and the lack of definitive biomarkers, relying on clinical evaluation, advanced neuroimaging techniques such as magnetic resonance imaging and positron emission testing, and cerebrospinal fluid biomarkers. There are no disease-modifying treatments, and management is symptomatic, focusing on physical, occupational, and speech therapy and supportive care to improve the patient's quality of life. Clinicians participating in this course gain a comprehensive understanding of CBD, including its clinical presentation, differential diagnosis, and the latest advancements in diagnostic imaging and biomarker research. The course enhances their ability to distinguish CBD from other Parkinsonian and atypical neurodegenerative syndromes, improving diagnostic accuracy and patient care. Additionally, clinicians learn about current and emerging therapeutic strategies, interdisciplinary management approaches, and best patient education and caregiver support practices. By integrating this knowledge into clinical practice, participants are better equipped to navigate the complexities of CBD, facilitate early diagnosis, and provide optimal, evidence-based care for affected patients.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Mohs Micrographic Surgery Evaluation and Treatment of Dermatofibrosarcoma Protuberans
courses.description: Dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans (DFSP) is a rare, locally aggressive soft tissue tumor originating from the dermal layer of the skin. This condition typically presents as a slow-growing, indurated plaque or nodule, predominantly occurring on the trunk and proximal extremities. While DFSP is characterized by local infiltration along tissue planes, it rarely metastasizes. However, high-grade sarcomatous changes within the tumor can occur, potentially affecting both the prognosis and the approach to treatment. Diagnosis relies on clinical examination and histopathological evaluation, with imaging used to assess the extent of the tumor when necessary. Treatment modalities for DFSP include micrographic dermatologic surgery (MDS), such as Mohs micrographic surgery (MMS), wide local excision, radiation therapy, and pharmacologic therapy. Through participation in the course, healthcare professionals gain a comprehensive understanding of DFSP's etiology, epidemiology, pathogenesis, clinical manifestations, and optimal diagnostic and management strategies. Special emphasis is placed on micrographic dermatologic surgery, particularly MMS, which is critical for achieving tumor-free margins while preserving function and cosmesis. Learners also acquire skills in collaborating with an interprofessional team, including dermatologists, oncologists, radiologists, and pathologists, to enhance patient outcomes. This collaborative approach ensures precise tumor removal, minimizes the risk of recurrence, and addresses the complex needs of patients with DFSP, ultimately leading to improved care and patient satisfaction.

courses.title: Laryngeal Clefts
courses.description: Laryngeal cleft represents a rare congenital defect in which the posterior structures of the larynx and trachea fail to separate from the esophagus. This anatomical gap permits ingested material to pass into the airway, predisposing infants and children to persistent coughing, feeding difficulty, aspiration pneumonia, and recurrent respiratory tract infections. Type I cleft is confined to the interarytenoid region, whereas types II through IV extend progressively into the cricoid cartilage and tracheoesophageal wall, requiring increasingly complex intervention. Diagnosis follows a high index of suspicion once more prevalent causes of aspiration or chronic cough are excluded, and confirmation relies on flexible or rigid endoscopic examination, often supplemented by contrast imaging. Management ranges from conservative thickened-feed strategies and interarytenoid injection augmentation for type I lesions to definitive endoscopic or open surgical repair for higher-grade clefts. Recent refinements in endoscopic techniques and perioperative care have markedly improved survival and functional outcomes, particularly for the historically challenging type III and IV lesions. The course provides participants with a structured framework for recognizing laryngeal clefts early, selecting appropriate imaging or microlaryngoscopy, and tailoring interventions to the severity of the cleft. Content emphasizes clear communication pathways among otolaryngology, pulmonology, gastroenterology, anesthesiology, speech-language pathology, and nutrition services. This interprofessional team coordinates perioperative planning, optimizes airway protection, and streamlines postoperative feeding rehabilitation. Learners acquire practical skills in counseling caregivers, interpreting videofluoroscopic swallow studies, and implementing temporary injection augmentation as both a diagnostic aid and a bridge to surgical intervention. The curriculum highlights evidence-based outcome data...

courses.title: Hydrogen Peroxide Toxicity
courses.description: Hydrogen peroxide is an oxidizing chemical found in many households and industrial settings. It is generally safe at household concentrations (usually about 3%) but can be dangerous if used inappropriately. Industrial concentrations (usually up to 70%) can cause significant mortality and mortality. The signs and symptoms of toxicity must be identified and promptly treated to improve outcomes. More concentrated hydrogen peroxide solutions, as are often found in industrial strength solutions, cause significant damage with all types of exposures. This activity outlines hydrogen peroxide toxicity and its resultant complications and highlights the role of the interprofessional team in evaluating and treating patients presenting with this condition.

courses.title: Agent Orange Toxicity
courses.description: Agent Orange, a herbicide used during the Vietnam War, contains components such as 2,4,5-trichlorophenoxyacetic acid (2,4,5-T), 2,4-dichlorophenoxyacetic acid (2,4-D), and the contaminant 2,3,7,8-tetrachlorodibenzo-p-dioxin. The toxicity associated with Agent Orange arises from both acute exposure and long-term effects of these chemicals. The primary populations affected are United States service members who participated in Operation Ranch Hand and residents in Vietnam, Cambodia, and Laos. Despite the low prevalence of exposure due to the specific populations involved, the long-term health implications of Agent Orange exposure have been significant. The Agent Orange Act of 1991 led to comprehensive investigations and studies to understand the health effects better. Participants in the course gain insights into the critical role of the healthcare team in managing cases related to Agent Orange exposure. By learning about the identification, care, and improved outcomes for affected individuals, participants understand how interprofessional collaboration enhances patient care. Collaborative efforts between various healthcare disciplines are essential for recognizing the signs and symptoms of both acute and remote dioxin exposure.

courses.title: Implicit Bias
courses.description: Implicit bias is the attitude or internalized stereotypes that unconsciously affect our perceptions, actions, and decisions. These unconscious biases often affect behavior that leads to unequal treatment of people based on race, ethnicity, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, disability, health status, and other characteristics. In medicine, unconscious bias-based discriminatory practices negatively impact patient care and medical training programs, hinder effective communication, limit workforce diversity, lead to inequitable distribution of research funding, impede career advancement, and result in carriers and disparities in the access to and delivery of healthcare services. This activity will address strategies to reduce the harm of implicit bias, clinician self-awareness and self-assessment of personal biases, and the role of the interprofessional team in increasing awareness and reducing bias-based discriminatory behavior.

courses.title: Nail Surgery
courses.description: Nail surgery encompasses various procedures that address conditions affecting the nail unit, such as ingrown nails, infections, tumors, trauma, and painful deformities that cause pain or functional issues. Common nail surgery techniques, including partial or total nail avulsion, matrixectomy, excision of nail bed tumors, and repair of nail bed injuries, aim to alleviate symptoms and restore function. Each procedure requires careful handling of the nail bed and surrounding tissues to prevent permanent deformities or scarring. Biopsies are essential in nail surgery, allowing for precise tissue sampling to differentiate between benign and malignant lesions. Proper specimen orientation and mapping are emphasized to ensure accurate histological processing and diagnosis. Although a few complications are associated with nail surgery, this surgery effectively relieves pain, improves function, and often restores the appearance of the affected nail. This activity for healthcare professionals reviews essential anatomical landmarks and various biopsy and avulsion techniques, providing a comprehensive foundation for performing nail biopsies and related procedures. This activity also addresses the management of common postoperative complications, offering practical strategies to minimize patient discomfort and promote healing. In addition, this activity enhances clinician proficiency and confidence, enabling effective collaboration within an interprofessional healthcare team to optimize care for patients undergoing nail surgery.

courses.title: Hydrazine Toxicology
courses.description: Hydrazines are a generic group of structurally related chemicals with numerous commercial uses. Different kinds of hydrazine compounds include hydrazines, hydrazones, 1,1-dimethylhydrazine, and 1,2-dimethylhydrazine. Most hydrazines are manufactured as an intermediate during agricultural chemicals and plastics production, a component of rocket propellant and fuels, water treatments, and a metabolite of the gyromitra mushroom and anti-tuberculosis drug isoniazid. Hydrazine exposure has toxic effects on multiple organ systems, including the neurological, hematological, pulmonary, dermatologic, and hepatic systems. Hydrazines produce a functional pyridoxine deficiency by inhibiting its synthesis by deactivating key coenzymes. Management involves aggressive supportive care and the administration of pyridoxine (vitamin B6) for refractory seizures. This activity reviews the history, potential for exposure, pathophysiology, evaluation, and management of hydrazine toxicity. The role of the interprofessional team in evaluating and managing patients exposed to this chemical compound is highlighted.

courses.title: Stargardt Disease
courses.description: Stargardt disease (STGD1) is the most common cause of juvenile macular dystrophy. Mutations in the adenosine triphosphate binding cassette transporter alpha 4 subunit (ABCA4) gene cause this condition and are inherited in an autosomal recessive pattern. STGD1 is a heterogeneous disease with many clinical presentations and varying rates of the age of onset and disease progression. Patients can easily be misdiagnosed and subjected to multiple investigations like neuroimaging, lumbar punctures, and therapies. Multimodal imaging is required to establish an early diagnosis. Several therapeutic options are currently under evaluation; however, they have yet to receive the United States Food and Drug Administration recommendation. This activity reviews the pathophysiology, presenting clinical features, various imaging modalities, differential diagnosis, and the various treatment modalities of STGD1.

courses.title: Posterior Polar Cataract
courses.description: Posterior polar cataract (PPC) is a unique form of congenital cataract, which results in defective distance and near vision and affects the patient's daily activities. The inheritance is autosomal dominant, but a sporadic form has also been reported. Various genes have been implicated in the pathogenesis of PPC. PPC presents as an elevated plaque-like onion ring-shaped central discoid lens opacity densely adherent to the posterior capsule. It is a surgical challenge for all ophthalmologists due to the dense adherence to the posterior capsule or pre-existing posterior capsular dehiscence. Clinically Daljit Singh sign and anterior segment optical coherence tomography imaging can predict the posterior capsular dehiscence preoperatively and prevent dreaded complications like posterior capsular rupture, nucleus drop, aphakia, and vitreous prolapse. Various surgical techniques with variable success have been proposed for the management of PPC. This activity deals with etiology, epidemiology, clinical features, differential diagnosis, complications, and prognosis of posterior polar cataracts and evaluation and management by an interprofessional team.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Sodium-Glucose Transport 2 (SGLT2) Inhibitors
courses.description: Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors, including canagliflozin, dapagliflozin, empagliflozin, and ertugliflozin, have transformed the management of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) by providing glucose-lowering efficacy together with cardiovascular and renal protection. Initially approved as adjuncts to diet and exercise for glycemic control, these agents now have expanded indications that include reducing hospitalizations for heart failure, preserving renal function, and lowering cardiovascular mortality in patients with or without diabetes. The mechanism of action of SGLT2 inhibitors involves inhibiting glucose reabsorption within the proximal renal tubules, resulting in glucosuria, modest weight loss, and blood pressure reduction. Evidence demonstrates benefits in heart failure with reduced or preserved ejection fraction and in chronic kidney disease, supporting their incorporation into major international guidelines. Despite substantial clinical advantages, therapy requires attention to safety considerations such as volume depletion, genital infections, diabetic ketoacidosis, and potential lower extremity complications. Optimizing patient outcomes depends on appropriate selection, dosing, monitoring, and interprofessional strategies that enhance adherence and long-term care. This activity for healthcare professionals is designed to enhance learners' proficiency in integrating SGLT2 therapy into the comprehensive care of patients with T2DM and high cardiovascular or renal risk. Participants will gain deeper insights into the pharmacologic mechanisms, clinical benefits, dosing strategies, safety considerations, and guideline-based monitoring of these drugs. Strengthened skills will equip clinicians to participate in the interprofessional care of patients with T2DM and cardiovascular or renal comorbidities, improving outcomes.

courses.title: Neuronal Brain Tumors
courses.description: Neuronal brain tumors are a diverse group of primary central nervous system tumors consisting of lesions with either a primarily neuronal background or a mixed glial and neuronal background, termed glioneuronal tumors. These are rare tumors most commonly associated with epilepsy, although other symptoms may also occur, such as headaches, focal neurological deficits, and acute hydrocephalus. This activity reviews the evaluation and treatment of neuronal brain tumors. It highlights the role of the interprofessional team in evaluating and treating patients who are found to harbor these tumors.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Hearing Loss Assessment in Children
courses.description: Congenital and childhood hearing loss can disrupt speech, language, cognitive, educational, and psychosocial development when identification and intervention are delayed. Despite widespread newborn hearing screening, clinicians may inconsistently select age-appropriate screening and diagnostic modalities, recognize risk factors requiring additional evaluation, interpret abnormal findings, or coordinate timely follow-up and intervention. This continuing medical education activity reviews physiologic and behavioral hearing assessment across infancy and childhood, including otoacoustic emissions, auditory brainstem response testing, tympanometry, behavioral audiometry, imaging, genetic evaluation, and treatment options. Participants will strengthen competence in identifying children who require further evaluation, selecting appropriate diagnostic strategies, differentiating conductive, sensorineural, and neural hearing disorders, and applying evidence-based early intervention pathways. The activity also emphasizes coordinated interprofessional care to reduce loss to follow-up, support timely rehabilitation, and improve communication, developmental, educational, and quality-of-life outcomes for children with hearing loss.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Trauma to the Primary Dentition
courses.description: Traumatic dental injuries (TDIs) are common and can have significant long-term consequences for both the hard and soft tissues of the oral cavity. This article outlines the presentation, clinical features, and management of TDIs affecting the primary teeth. As these injuries are common, this article contains information pertinent to clinicians in both primary and secondary care.

courses.title: Silicosis
courses.description: Silica is the most plentiful mineral on earth and is the primary constituent in most rocks. The respirable form of silica is small enough to reach the terminal bronchioles and alveoli of the respiratory system. Typical immune mechanisms cannot clear these particles from the lung, initiating a pathologic cycle of inflammation and parenchymal damage that ultimately leads to silicosis. Silicosis is the world's most prevalent occupational lung disease and is characterized by irreversible, progressive pulmonary fibrosis leading to restrictive lung disease. Silicosis is a preventable disease with significant morbidity and mortality that has no cure. Education on prevention, screening, timely diagnosis, avoidance of exacerbating factors, and treatment of complications is imperative. This activity reviews the etiology, epidemiology, pathogenesis, pathophysiology, clinical evaluation, and management of silicosis and highlights the role of the interprofessional team in caring for patients with this occupational pneumoconiosis.

courses.title: Assisted Reproductive Technology (ART) Techniques
courses.description: Assisted reproductive technology (ART) encompasses a range of medical procedures used to address infertility and assist individuals and couples in achieving pregnancy. Since the first successful birth from in vitro fertilization (IVF) in 1978, ART has evolved into a highly specialized and rapidly advancing field that integrates reproductive endocrinology, embryology, genetics, and personalized patient care. At its core, ART involves the handling of both eggs and sperm outside the human body to facilitate fertilization. Common techniques include IVF, intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI), and embryo cryopreservation, with newer advancements such as preimplantation genetic testing (PGT) and time-lapse embryo monitoring further refining outcomes. These technologies offer hope to patients facing a wide range of reproductive concerns, from age-related infertility and male factor issues to genetic disorders and same-sex family planning. Understanding the indications, protocols, and laboratory processes behind ART is essential for healthcare professionals involved in fertility care. This course offers a comprehensive overview of current and emerging techniques in ART, including indications for use, recommended techniques, and common complications. Participants will enhance their understanding of both the science and clinical practice of ART. The activity also highlights the importance of a coordinated interprofessional team.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Chromium Deficiency
courses.description: Trivalent chromium is considered an essential trace element for metabolizing lipids and carbohydrates. Some clinical trials suggest that it enhances the effect of insulin in peripheral tissues. Trivalent chromium is believed to be an essential component of metalloenzymes in metabolizing carbohydrates, proteins, and fats. Therefore, it is a recommended component of a regular diet in most individuals and an essential supplement for those on total parenteral nutrition. However, there has been debate regarding the status of trivalent chromium as an actual essential element. Recent studies in animal models suggest that chromium is beneficial but not necessary for normal physiological functions. Case studies initially indicating chromium deficiency as the cause of glucose intolerance and insulin resistance suggest that chromium may have a therapeutic role in treating these conditions. However, it is unlikely that chromium is the cause of these complications. Current guidelines note that an essential function of chromium can not be substantiated. To ensure adequate use of chromium replacement therapy, a team of healthcare professionals, including clinicians, pharmacists, and dieticians, must become aware of current recommendations regarding the status of chromium as an essential element. Understanding chromium's role in the normal physiology of the human body and developing appropriate chromium supplementation guidelines for individuals on total parenteral nutrition are essential. Moreover, clinicians must understand the role of chromium replacement therapy in health conditions marketed to benefit from it. This activity provides an up-to-date review of the current literature regarding chromium as a dietary trace element, its role in normal physiological functions, the postulated clinical consequences of its deficiency, and the recommended replacement thresholds in individuals receiving total parenteral nutrition.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Laboratory Evaluation of Sepsis
courses.description: Sepsis is a medical emergency caused by organ dysfunction resulting from a dysregulated host response to an infection. Early identification and treatment of sepsis and septic shock are essential for improving outcomes. Timely initiation of antimicrobial therapy is one of the most effective interventions to reduce sepsis-related morbidity and mortality. Identifying sepsis and septic shock can be difficult due to their variable clinical presentation. Patients with suspected sepsis or septic shock are evaluated with various laboratory studies, including different biomarkers essential for diagnosis, early recognition of severity, risk stratification, and prognosis. The results of these studies and various clinical criteria can be used to effectively screen patients for sepsis and gauge the severity of the disease. This activity reviews the laboratory evaluation of patients with suspected sepsis or septic shock and highlights the role of the interprofessional team in improving care for patients with this life-threatening condition.

courses.title: Bacterial Keratitis
courses.description: Bacterial keratitis or corneal ulcer is a common sight-threatening ocular corneal pathology. In some cases, there is rapidly progressive stromal inflammation. If untreated can lead to progressive tissue destruction, corneal perforation, or extension of infection to adjacent tissue. Bacterial keratitis is commonly associated with risk factors that disturb the corneal epithelial integrity. A meticulous slit lamp clinical examination, corneal scraping with smearing, and culture are mandated to reach a conclusive diagnosis. Antibacterials are the mainstay of treatment and adjuvant in the form of cycloplegics, antiglaucoma medications, and oral anti-inflammatory drugs. Rapidly progressive cases unresponsive to medical treatment require therapeutic keratoplasty. This activity aims to give deeper insight into etiology, risk factors, epidemiology, clinical presentation, microbiological and histopathological analysis, treatment, complication, differential diagnosis, and prognosis of bacterial keratitis.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Duodenal Trauma
courses.description: Duodenal trauma is a rare and potentially life-threatening injury. It is most commonly caused by a penetrating mechanism. The duodenum is the first and smallest portion of the small bowel. These injuries, however, are challenged by complex anatomic and physiologic relationships. As a result, the diagnosis and subsequent management may be delayed. This delay is associated with increased morbidity and mortality. Treatment, as well, is difficult given these relationships and the surgical approach is often complex. This activity will review the pathophysiology, presentation, evaluation, and management of duodenal trauma. It highlights the role of the interprofessional team in evaluating and treating patients with this condition.

courses.title: Patisiran
courses.description: Patisiran is indicated for treating polyneuropathy associated with hereditary transthyretin-mediated amyloidosis (hATTR) in adults. The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) of the United States of America approved this therapeutic usage in August 2018. It is in the RNA interference therapeutics class of drugs. This activity will highlight the mechanism of action, adverse event profile, and other key factors (eg, off-label uses, dosing, pharmacodynamics, pharmacokinetics, monitoring, relevant interactions) pertinent for members of the interprofessional team in the management of patients with polyneuropathy associated with hereditary transthyretin-mediated amyloidosis (hATTR), wild-type of transthyretin-mediated amyloidosis (ATTR), and related conditions.

courses.title: Infectious Complications of Blood Transfusion
courses.description: A safe and reliable blood supply is a crucial part of medical services. Modern blood banking technology has led to increased safety but should not be taken for granted. Infectious complications of blood transfusion, although rare in developed countries, can be life-threatening and lead to significant morbidity and mortality. Knowledge of infectious complications of blood transfusion is imperative for an interprofessional team regularly performing blood transfusions. This activity highlights the various bacterial and non-bacterial infection risks, mitigation strategies, emerging infectious risks, challenges in maintaining a safe blood supply in developing countries, cost considerations, and the challenge of estimating infectious risk when considering the infectious complications of blood transfusion.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Marburg Virus Disease
courses.description: Marburg virus disease, or Marburg fever, caused by the highly pathogenic Marburgvirus (MARV), is a rare but severe hemorrhagic fever with a high case-fatality rate, transmitted through contact with excreta of the fruit bat Rousettus aegyptiacus (the natural reservoir of MARV), infected individuals bodily fluids, or exposure in healthcare and laboratory settings. This course reviews the characteristic features of this disease, which presents after an incubation period of 3 to 21 days, beginning with nonspecific symptoms such as fever, myalgia, and headache, progressing to gastrointestinal symptoms, hemorrhagic manifestations, and, in severe cases, multiorgan failure and shock. Participants will gain an in-depth understanding of this rare virus and the importance of prompt diagnosis to prevent the high morbidity and mortality associated with this condition. Public health preparedness, supportive management, including fluid replacement and blood transfusions, which remains the primary treatment for this condition, as well as stringent infection control measures critical to limiting the spread of the disease and managing and containing outbreaks effectively, are also explored. This activity for healthcare professionals is designed to enhance the learner's competence in recognizing the clinical features of the Marburg virus disease, performing the recommended evaluation, and implementing an appropriate interprofessional management approach to improve patient outcomes.

courses.title: Nuclear Medicine Applications in Prostate Cancer
courses.description: Prostate cancer is the 2nd most common cancer in men and the 4th overall. In 2020 , more than 1.4 million new prostate cancer cases were reported. In recent years, the incidence of prostate cancer has reached its highest levels due to more precise and timely diagnoses and an increase in average lifespan. Therefore, prostate cancer must be promptly diagnosed and treated to avoid high morbidity and mortality. This activity reviews the role of nuclear medicine in evaluating and treating patients with this condition.

courses.title: Laboratory Evaluation of Bone Marrow
courses.description: Bone marrow laboratory evaluation is essential for classifying, diagnosing, and managing neoplastic and certain nonneoplastic hematologic conditions. This comprehensive evaluation encompasses bone marrow aspiration, trephine biopsy, clot specimen analysis, flow cytometry, and molecular studies, aligning with the World Health Organization 2022 classification guidelines. The emergence of advanced molecular techniques has allowed the identification of molecular alterations carrying prognostic and therapeutic implications. Understanding nomenclature and identifying prognostically and therapeutically relevant testing options is essential to healthcare providers. This activity for healthcare providers enhances learners competence in identifying bone marrow laboratory evaluation indications and understanding the therapeutic and prognostic significance of the test results. This activity aims to improve clinicians proficiency in implementing the best bone marrow evaluation reporting practices, enabling them to communicate the information efficiently in interprofessional care settings.

courses.title: Hereditary Hemorrhagic Telangiectasia (HHT)
courses.description: Hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia (HHT) is a rare autosomal dominant vascular disorder characterized by mucocutaneous telangiectasias and arteriovenous malformations involving the lungs, brain, liver, gastrointestinal tract, and other organ systems. Clinical manifestations vary widely, ranging from recurrent epistaxis and chronic iron deficiency anemia to serious complications such as stroke, hemorrhage, paradoxical embolization, and high-output cardiac failure. Early recognition and appropriate screening are essential to reduce morbidity and prevent life-threatening outcomes. This course reviews the pathophysiology, genetic basis, clinical presentation, diagnostic criteria, and evidence-based management strategies for HHT across the lifespan. Participants gain knowledge of risk assessment, surveillance recommendations, treatment options, and complication prevention. Emphasis is placed on timely referral, patient education, and coordinated care. Collaboration among clinicians, nurses, genetic counselors, radiologists, hematology specialists, and other interprofessional team members enhances diagnostic accuracy, supports comprehensive management, and improves patient outcomes and safety.

courses.title: Malignant Eyelid Lesions
courses.description: Malignant eyelid lesions are a unique subset of cancers that range from some of the most common forms of cutaneous malignancy, such as basal cell and squamous cell carcinoma, to much rarer forms of metastatic disease. Many cases may resemble or arise from benign or premalignant lesions, necessitating a thorough history, careful examination, and prompt biopsy to ensure optimal patient outcomes. This course discussion focuses on the broad concepts of eyelid malignancy, including etiology, epidemiology, and prevention. This course also reviews lesion-specific details ranging from histopathology to modern treatment and prognosis. Lesions discussed include basal cell carcinoma, squamous cell carcinoma, actinic keratosis, melanoma, Merkel cell carcinoma, sebaceous cell carcinoma, and others. The aim of this in-depth review is not only to provide concise, up-to-date, and easily digestible information but also to emphasize the importance of interprofessional management of patients with malignant eyelid lesions. This course presents essential, high-yield information on precancerous and cancerous eyelid lesions that will enhance learners' clinical skills and scientific knowledge, regardless of specialty or level of training.

courses.title: Laboratory Evaluation of Alpha Thalassemia
courses.description: -thalassemia is a heterogeneous group of genetic erythrocyte disorders characterized by the absence or deficiency of hemoglobin's -globin chains. Decreased -globin synthesis causes a relative excess of -globin chains, which damages erythroblasts and causes anemia. -thalassemia has varied presentations, presenting silently in adult genetic carriers, but tends to be fatal in the fetal stage when all 4 -globin chains are absent. Laboratory evaluation techniques can help diagnose the condition early and improve patients' life expectancy. This activity for healthcare professionals is designed to improve learners' competence in evaluating -thalassemia and managing the condition based on laboratory findings. This activity also enhances learners' ability to collaborate effectively with interprofessional teams caring for -thalassemia patients.

courses.title: Rh Blood Group System
courses.description: The Rh blood group system has been extensively studied and remains clinically relevant. This highly polymorphic system comprises over 50 expressed antigens embedded in the red blood cell (RBC) membrane. The function of these highly immunogenic proteins is unknown. Patients with specific Rh phenotypes require special attention during transfusion and pregnancy to avoid potentially life-threatening complications. This activity reviews the evaluation and management of patients with various Rh blood group phenotypes and highlights the role of the interprofessional healthcare team in caring for these patients in various clinical settings.

courses.title: Pediatric Dyslipidemia
courses.description: Cardiovascular disease is the number one cause of morbidity and mortality among adults in the United States and many other countries. Dyslipidemia is a well-established risk for the development of atherosclerosis which leads to cardiovascular disease. There is strong evidence to suggest that atherosclerotic plaque development begins early in childhood and adolescence and subsequently leads to premature adverse cardiovascular events. As per the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) data, 20% of 12-19-year-olds have lipid disorders. In children with obesity, the prevalence of dyslipidemia is even higher at 42%. Because dyslipidemia is largely a silent disease, a significant pediatric population remains undiagnosed. With timely diagnosis and treatment of pediatric dyslipidemia, the risk for cardiovascular events and mortality can be reduced. Furthermore, with rising rates of pediatric obesity, dyslipidemia is an even more important childhood health issue to be recognized and managed. This activity will review the definitions, etiology, and management of pediatric dyslipidemia and highlight the importance of an interprofessional team in the evaluation and management of this disease.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Synovial Cell Sarcoma
courses.description: Synovial sarcoma is a mesenchymal tumor that presents mainly in adolescents and adults younger than 30. It is a relatively rare tumor, with 800 to 1000 cases reported annually. Synovial sarcoma is defined by the translocation between chromosome X and 18, which leads to the expression of SS18:SSX fusion proteins. This activity reviews the presentation, diagnosis, treatment, and role of interprofessional teams in managing patients diagnosed with synovial sarcoma.

courses.title: Compare and Contrast the Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists (GLP1RAs)
courses.description: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RA) are a class of medications used to treat adult type 2 diabetes and obesity. They are in the drug class of incretin mimetics. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RA, GLP-1DAs, incretin mimetics, or GLP-1 analogs) are a class of medications utilized in treating type 2 diabetes and obesity. Clinical trials show the superiority of GLP-1RA to other antihyperglycemic drugs in improving glycemic efficacy, reducing weight and blood pressure, and having a cardioprotective effect, all without the risk of hypoglycemia. These drugs have transformed the guidelines for the management of diabetes. This activity reviews the indications, mechanism of action, adverse effects, and other critical elements of these drugs. In addition, this activity highlights the comparison between different GLP-1 receptor agonists within the same class based on pharmacokinetics, duration of action, efficacy, and safety profile pertinent to the interprofessional healthcare team in using this class of medications for treating diabetes, obesity, and their sequelae.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Pseudoexfoliation Syndrome and Glaucoma
courses.description: Pseudoexfoliation syndrome is a chronic, age-related disorder of the extracellular matrix that results in the deposition of abnormal fibrillary (pseudoexfoliative) material within various body tissues. This condition manifests primarily in the anterior segment of the eye. Individuals with this condition can develop pseudoexfoliation glaucoma in the presence of chronic elevated intraocular pressure, glaucomatous optic neuropathy, and visual field damage. This activity reviews the evaluation and treatment of pseudoexfoliation syndrome and highlights the role of the interprofessional team in evaluating and treating patients with this condition.

courses.title: Prostate Cancer Tissue-Based Biomarkers
courses.description: Prostate cancer is the fourth most commonly diagnosed cancer worldwide, with approximately 1.4 million new cases, and is more commonly diagnosed in developed countries. To combat the disease, advanced biomarkers are constantly in development. Even though patients with prostate cancer have improved overall survival, from a global perspective, this is a disease that requires attention in terms of better diagnostic and treatment modalities, especially in the metastatic setting. This activity describes tissue-based biomarkers useful in clinical practice to help determine risk stratification at critical decision points in prostate cancer, which will help determine the relative need for a re-biopsy or further intervention, thus aiding physicians and patients in personalizing care for their disease.
