courses.title: Lafora Disease
courses.description: Lafora disease is a severe, autosomal recessive, progressive myoclonic epilepsy predominantly affecting previously healthy adolescents. Presenting with myoclonus, occipital seizures, and rapid cognitive decline, it progresses rapidly to death within a decade of initial symptom onset. This disease is diagnosed through clinical, electrophysiological, histological, and genetic findings. No curative treatments or preventative interventions are available at present for Lafora disease. Management of Lafora disease focuses on symptomatic relief of seizures and myoclonus, together with palliative, supportive, and rehabilitative measures. By understanding the genetic underpinnings and pathophysiology, healthcare clinicians can better navigate diagnostic challenges and optimize treatment approaches to improve patient outcomes. This activity for healthcare professionals aims to enhance learners' competence in selecting appropriate diagnostic tests, managing Lafora disease, emphasizing supportive care and symptomatic relief, and fostering effective interprofessional teamwork to improve outcomes.

courses.title: Intracranial Pressure Monitoring
courses.description: According to the Monro-Kellie theory, the cranial compartment is incompressible, and its contents (blood, cerebrospinal fluid, and brain tissue) are in an internal milieu of volume balance; thus, an increase in one must be offset by a reduction in the other components. Intracranial pressure guided therapy has been the cornerstone in managing severe traumatic brain injury. Intracranial pressure (ICP) monitoring allows for the judicious use of interventions with a defined target point, thereby avoiding potentially harmful aggressive treatment. Participants get an in-depth examination of ICP-guided therapy, emphasizing its role in managing severe traumatic brain injury. The course outlines current monitoring recommendations, covering invasive techniques like intraventricular catheters and noninvasive methods like transcranial Doppler ultrasound. Practical insights into judicious interventions with defined target points aim to prevent potentially harmful aggressive treatments. The activity also addresses the need for the collaborative efforts of an interprofessional team to minimize complications regarding the process and thereby safeguard patient safety.

courses.title: Kawasaki Disease
courses.description: Kawasaki disease (KD) is an acute, self-limited medium vessel vasculitis that has a predilection for the coronary arteries. This activity reviews the evaluation and treatment of Kawasaki disease and highlights the role of the interprofessional team in improving care for patients with this condition.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Intravenous Immunoglobulin (IVIG)
courses.description: Intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) is a pooled antibody, and a biological agent used to manage various immunodeficiency states and a plethora of other conditions, including autoimmune, infectious, and inflammatory states. The ultimate goal of this therapy is to normalize a compromised immune system. This activity reviews the indications, mechanism of action, contraindications, adverse effects, and monitoring of IVIG in the treatment of several immune deregulated states. It also highlights the key information pertinent to the healthcare teams managing patients with conditions affecting the immune system and other immune-related conditions.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Stillbirth
courses.description: Stillbirth is defined as the death of a fetus at 20 weeks' gestation or later in the United States, or at 28 weeks' gestation internationally, and can result from a broad range of maternal, fetal, and placental conditions. Common causes include hypertensive disorders, diabetes, congenital or genetic anomalies, placental insufficiency, and infections. Intrapartum complications and prolonged pregnancies also contribute significantly. Despite advances in obstetric care, many stillbirths remain unexplained, with global data suggesting that up to 76% of cases lack a definitive cause. The emotional, psychological, and societal consequences of stillbirth are profound and long-lasting. Global stillbirth reporting remains inconsistent, which limits our understanding and the development of preventive strategies. Accurate identification of causes and standardization in reporting are essential to support affected families and reduce recurrence in future pregnancies. This educational activity provides clinicians with evidence-based tools for evaluating, managing, and supporting patients affected by stillbirth. Participants gain knowledge of the current definitions, global disparities, diagnostic workup, and counseling principles. Emphasis is placed on trauma-informed communication, cause identification, and prevention strategies. Interprofessional collaboration among obstetricians, nurses, social workers, mental health professionals, and genetic counselors is vital in delivering comprehensive care. Coordinated teamwork enhances diagnostic accuracy, promotes emotional support, and improves continuity of care, ultimately leading to better short- and long-term maternal and family outcomes.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Intra-Aortic Balloon Pump
courses.description: This activity reviews the indications and contraindications of intra-aortic balloon pump in patients with cardiogenic shock secondary to various cardiac conditions, including myocardial infarction and subsequent mechanical complications. It covers the structure of the IABP device and its hemodynamic effects, the complications related to IABP use, and, most importantly, how an interprofessional team approach in caring for patients with cardiogenic shock requiring IABP support can help improve the clinical outcomes.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

practice_areas: Advanced Heart Failure and Transplant Cardiology

courses.title: Junctional Ectopic Tachycardia
courses.description: Junctional ectopic tachycardia (JET) is a rare but potentially life-threatening arrhythmia most commonly seen in infants and young children, originating from the atrioventricular junction or bundle of His. This condition is classified into congenital and postoperative types, with the former often associated with high morbidity and mortality due to its refractory nature and potential for progression to heart failure or sudden cardiac death. Diagnosis relies on electrocardiographic features such as narrow-complex tachycardia and ventriculoatrial dissociation, and management includes correcting electrolyte imbalances, pharmacological therapy most notably with amiodarone and, in select cases, catheter ablation. Early recognition, multidisciplinary coordination, and individualized therapy are essential to improving outcomes. Clinicians participating in this course enhance their understanding of JET's pathophysiology, diagnostic challenges, and nuanced management strategies. They gain practical insights into recognizing early signs and symptoms, interpreting complex electrocardiogram findings, and implementing evidence-based interventions. The course emphasizes interprofessional collaboration and highlights the roles of various team members, including physicians, nurses, pharmacists, and allied health professionals, in delivering coordinated, high-quality, patient-centered care. Ultimately, participants are equipped to improve clinical outcomes, reduce complications, and contribute to safer, more effective treatment pathways for pediatric patients with JET.

courses.title: Intracerebral Hemorrhagic Stroke
courses.description: Intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) is a life-threatening subtype of stroke characterized by bleeding into the brain parenchyma, resulting in primary mechanical injury and secondary inflammatory damage. Representing 10% to 15% of all strokes, non-traumatic ICH carries high morbidity and mortality, particularly when associated with intraventricular extension. This course outlines the underlying etiologies of ICH, with chronic hypertension and cerebral amyloid angiopathy accounting for most primary cases, while vascular malformations, anticoagulation, neoplasms, and hemorrhagic transformation of ischemic stroke contribute to secondary causes. The need for rapid diagnosis with non-contrast computed tomography (CT) is also discussed, as hematoma expansion within the first 24 hours is common and strongly predicts outcome. This activity reviews current evidence regarding risk stratification, imaging interpretation, acute stabilization, and medical and surgical management strategies, focusing on airway stabilization, blood pressure control, reversal of coagulopathy, prevention of secondary brain injury, and selective surgical or minimally invasive intervention. Participants will strengthen their ability to recognize early neurological deterioration, mitigate hematoma expansion, manage complications, eg, hydrocephalus and seizures, and apply guideline-directed blood pressure and anticoagulation reversal protocols. This activity for healthcare professionals is designed to enhance the learner's competence in identifying ICH, performing the recommended evaluation, and implementing an appropriate interprofessional approach when managing this condition.

courses.title: Conjugated Hyperbilirubinemia
courses.description: Conjugated hyperbilirubinemia is usually secondary to hepatocellular disease or cholestasis (intrahepatic and extra-hepatic ). Early workup and diagnosis is necessary for the appropriate management and to prevent future complications. This activity outlines the evaluation and management of conjugated hyperbilirubinemia and highlights the role of the interprofessional team in improving care for patients with this condition.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Hypothermia
courses.description: Hypothermia occurs when the body loses more heat than it can absorb or produce, leading to an inability to maintain homeostasis and proper bodily function. While hypothermia is often caused by exposure to excessive cold or insufficient heat production, certain external factors can also increase the risk of developing this condition. If not treated promptly, hypothermia can be potentially fatal. Therefore, healthcare professionals must be familiar with its various presentations, potential causes, and management strategies. This educational activity for healthcare professionals reviews the pathophysiology, etiology, recognition, management, and prevention of hypothermia. It aims to enhance the learner's competence in evaluating and treating patients with this condition. By participating in this activity, clinicians will be better equipped to contribute effectively to the multidisciplinary care of patients affected by hypothermia.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Evaluation and Management of Perioperative Hypertension
courses.description: Perioperative hypertension (HTN) is a common clinical challenge that requires careful evaluation and management to minimize cardiovascular, neurologic, renal, and surgical complications. Effective care depends on accurate blood pressure assessment, recognition of end-organ involvement, appropriate management of antihypertensive medications, and individualized hemodynamic goals before, during, and after surgery. This continuing education activity reviews the interprofessional management of patients with HTN throughout the perioperative period, emphasizing collaboration among anesthesiologists, nurses, surgeons, primary care providers, and physician assistants. Incorporating recommendations from the 2025 American Heart Association/American College of Cardiology (AHA/ACC) multisociety hypertension guideline and the 2024 AHA/ACC guideline for perioperative cardiovascular management for noncardiac surgery, the activity equips clinicians to apply current blood pressure classifications, conduct appropriate preoperative assessments, and implement evidence-based strategies to optimize perioperative blood pressure and patient outcomes.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Female Infertility
courses.description: Female infertility, defined as the inability to achieve pregnancy after 12 months of unprotected intercourse in women younger than 35 or 6 months in women 35 or older, remains a major global health concern affecting nearly 15% of couples. This activity reviews the female factors that contribute to about half of all infertility cases, stemming from ovulatory dysfunction, tubal or uterine abnormalities, endometriosis, genetic disorders, and lifestyle influences, as well as advances in diagnostic techniques, hormonal assays, imaging modalities, and assisted reproductive technologies that have improved outcomes, though disparities in access, cost, and emotional burden persist. Participants will gain an understanding of the complex etiology of infertility and evidence-based management. This activity for healthcare professionals is designed to enhance learners' competence in identifying the physiologic mechanisms of female infertility, performing the recommended evaluation, applying individualized treatment approaches, and implementing an appropriate interprofessional approach when managing this condition to improve patient outcomes and support emotional well-being.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Hypoplastic Lung Disease
courses.description: Hypoplastic lung disease is a rare developmental anomaly characterized by incomplete lung formation, resulting in reduced airway branching, alveoli, and pulmonary vasculature. The disease's etiology is multifactorial, encompassing genetic mutations, mechanical compression, and environmental or maternal factors during critical periods of fetal development. Cases can range from lethal respiratory insufficiency at birth to subclinical presentations in adulthood. Diagnostic evaluation involves imaging modalities like chest x-rays, computed tomography scans, and advanced fetal magnetic resonance imaging, alongside laboratory tests for associated anomalies and genetic assessments. Treatment focuses on addressing underlying causes, managing complications such as pulmonary hypertension and respiratory distress, and providing supportive care. Prognosis varies widely, depending on the severity, associated anomalies, and promptness of intervention. Clinicians participating in this course gain an in-depth understanding of the pathophysiology, etiology, and diagnostic approach to hypoplastic lung disease, enabling accurate identification and differentiation from other pulmonary conditions. They learn to interpret advanced imaging and pathology findings, recognize prenatal and postnatal risk factors, and tailor management strategies to individual patient presentations. Additionally, the course provides insights into multidisciplinary care coordination, emphasizing collaborative efforts with neonatologists, geneticists, and pulmonologists to optimize outcomes for affected patients. This course enhances clinical decision-making skills and prepare participants to address immediate and long-term challenges in managing hypoplastic lung disease.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Hyperoxaluria
courses.description: The most common type of kidney stone, calcium oxalate, is formed primarily due to an imbalance between calcium and oxalate levels in the body or a lack of adequate crystallization inhibitors. Hyperoxaluria is a significant contributor to nephrolithiasis, and the causes of excess urinary oxalate can be classified based on etiology into primary and secondary hyperoxaluria. Though both can present with kidney stones, the classifications differ in the extent of disease, rapidity of onset, and local and systemic complications. Even relatively small changes in urinary oxalate can have a very significant impact on kidney stone production. In addition, the presence of hyperoxaluria alone, without concurrent nephrolithiasis, also has deleterious effects on the kidney, resulting in fibrosis, acute kidney injury, and tubular atrophy. Unfortunately, there is currently a lack of an effective, specific, simple treatment for this important contributor to recurrent nephrolithiasis. Therefore, clinicians caring for these patients should become familiar with the available testing and treatments for hyperoxaluria and endpoints to measure therapy effectiveness.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Polio Vaccine
courses.description: Poliomyelitis is a highly infectious viral illness that can lead to permanent disability. Global vaccination efforts have drastically reduced the incidence of polio, bringing the disease to the brink of eradication. The oral polio vaccine remains a vital tool in many parts of the world due to its low cost and ease of administration, though there is a rare risk of paralysis associated with this vaccine. In contrast, the inactivated polio vaccine is used exclusively in countries with adequate sanitation infrastructure, including the United States, where the risk of vaccine-derived poliovirus is minimized. This activity reviews the mechanisms of action, administration routes, formulations, adverse events, and patient eligibility for both oral and inactivated polio vaccines. With ongoing wild-type polio transmission in Afghanistan and Pakistan and the emergence of vaccine-derived poliovirus, vaccination remains a priority for global public health. The role of the interprofessional healthcare team is crucial in achieving the eradication goal, ensuring widespread immunization, and monitoring for adverse effects.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Lactic Acidosis
courses.description: Lactic acidosis is a common cause of metabolic acidosis in hospitalized and critically ill patients, serving as both a clinical marker of disease severity and a contributor to multiple organ dysfunction and mortality. The condition is defined by a serum lactate concentration above 4 mmol/L, often accompanied by a blood pH below 7.35 and low plasma bicarbonate levels. Lactic acidosis results from increased lactate production, decreased lactate clearance, or both, typically due to tissue hypoperfusion, mitochondrial dysfunction, or the effects of certain medications. Lactic acidosis is classified into type A (hypoperfusion-related) and type B (non-hypoperfusion related) forms. Septic shock remains a frequent cause of type A lactic acidosis. Diagnosis involves measuring serum lactate, performing corrected anion gap calculations (especially in cases of hypoalbuminemia), and analyzing arterial blood gases. Prompt recognition and treatment focused on the underlying cause are essential. Management strategies include fluid resuscitation, vasopressors, renal replacement therapy, and cautious bicarbonate use, with elevated and persistent lactate levels indicating a poorer prognosis. This activity provides a comprehensive overview of lactic acidosis, including its pathophysiology, classification, common and rare etiologies (such as shock, organ failure, medication toxicity, and D-lactic acidosis), diagnostic evaluation, and evidence-based management strategies. Additionally, this activity addresses prognostic indicators, common pitfalls in clinical judgment, and the nuances of interpreting lactate levels. This activity underscores the importance of interprofessional collaboration among healthcare providers in ensuring timely diagnosis, effective monitoring, patient education, and coordinated care, ultimately enhancing patient safety and outcomes.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Ibuprofen
courses.description: Ibuprofen is a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) used to manage various conditions, including inflammatory diseases, rheumatoid disorders, mild to moderate pain, fever, dysmenorrhea, and osteoarthritis. This drug is available over-the-counter and in prescription strength. This activity reviews ibuprofen's mechanism of action, adverse event profiles, dosing considerations, pharmacokinetics, contraindications, box warnings, and monitoring protocols, which are critical areas of focus. Understanding ibuprofen's pharmacology enables healthcare professionals to optimize dosage regimens and minimize potential adverse effects. This educational activity also discusses the role of the interprofessional healthcare team in providing quality patient care using ibuprofen therapy, improving patient outcomes.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

certifying_boards: American Board of Otolaryngology - Head and Neck Surgery

courses.title: Cholangiocarcinoma
courses.description: Cholangiocarcinoma is an aggressive malignancy that originates from the biliary epithelium, both inside and outside the liver. Certain preexisting conditions and diseases can increase the risk of developing cholangiocarcinoma. This neoplasm is difficult to diagnose because obtaining a tissue sample for confirmation is not always possible. Unfortunately, cholangiocarcinoma is often locally invasive or metastatic by the time it is detected. While surgery is the only cure, radiation, chemotherapy, and targeted therapy can also be used in conjunction with surgery. This activity explores the diagnosis, evaluation, and treatment of cholangiocarcinoma and its various subtypes, highlighting the importance of an interprofessional team in managing the complicated decision-making process for these patients.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Hydrofluoric Acid Toxicity
courses.description: Hydrofluoric acid is a highly corrosive inorganic acid and potent dehydrating agent used in numerous industrial applications. Household products containing hydrofluoric acid are typically dilute, often around 0.5%, whereas industrial formulations may approach 100% concentration. Hydrofluoric acid readily penetrates deep into tissues, causing liquefactive necrosis and cellular destruction. Dermal, ocular, inhalational, and ingested exposures can result in severe local injury and systemic fluoride toxicity. Systemic effects include electrolyte abnormalities, enzyme inhibition, and cardiovascular, pulmonary, renal, and neuromuscular complications. Severe toxicity may lead to life-threatening cardiac dysrhythmias and death. This activity, designed for healthcare professionals, will enhance the learner's knowledge, clinical judgment, and management skills related to hydrofluoric acid toxicity. Learners will review the recognition of local and systemic manifestations, appropriate diagnostic and therapeutic interventions, and the essential contributions of the interprofessional team to reducing morbidity and mortality and improving patient outcomes.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

certifying_boards: American Board of Otolaryngology - Head and Neck Surgery

courses.title: Hyperammonemia
courses.description: Hyperammonemia is a metabolic disorder characterized by elevated plasma ammonia, a neurotoxin capable of causing encephalopathy, cerebral edema, and life-threatening herniation. Clinical manifestations vary widely, ranging from subtle neurocognitive deficits to seizures, coma, and rapid neurologic decline. Causes include both increased ammonia production and impaired clearance. Pediatric cases often arise from genetic and non-genetic inborn errors of metabolism, while acquired causes include hepatic dysfunction, malignancy, infections, and medication-related toxicity. Impairment of either hepatic or renal clearance can precipitate hyperammonemia. Because early clinical signs are nonspecific, diagnostic delays are common, and specimen handling during ammonia measurement is critical to accuracy. Prompt recognition and urgent intervention with anti-catabolic support, ammonia-lowering agents, renal replacement therapy, or targeted hepatic encephalopathy treatment are essential to minimize morbidity and mortality. Participants in this activity learn to recognize both congenital and acquired causes of hyperammonemia, apply diagnostic algorithms sensitive to patient age and clinical context, and implement evidence-based management strategies. Instruction emphasizes urgent stabilization, appropriate use of nitrogen-scavenging agents, and individualized nutritional interventions, including evidence-supported protein intake in cirrhosis. Learners strengthen competence in selecting dialysis techniques for refractory cases and coordinating care with subspecialists. Collaboration among clinicians, nurses, pharmacists, dietitians, nephrologists, and hepatologists ensures timely intervention, improves diagnostic precision, and optimizes long-term outcomes. An interprofessional team approach reduces complications, supports comprehensive patient education, and enhances quality of care across acute and chronic hyperammonemia settings.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Syndromic Sensorineural Hearing Loss
courses.description: According to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, hearing loss affected 1.7 per 1,000 babies screened in 2022. More than 6,000 infants with permanent hearing loss were identified in the U.S. Early detection in infancy is critical to minimizing delays in speech, language, learning, and social development. The American Academy of Pediatrics recommends confirming a diagnosis of hearing impairment by 12 weeks of age or earlier. Hearing loss occurs in isolation classified as nonsyndromic in many children. In contrast, "syndromic hearing loss" refers to cases where auditory impairment presents alongside other medical abnormalities. Approximately 20% of children with genetic hearing loss also exhibit additional clinical findings, such as vision deficits, cardiac defects, or pigmentary changes, depending on the underlying syndrome. Diagnosis involves audiologic testing paired with genetic evaluation and targeted imaging to identify associated systemic features. Management depends on the specific syndrome but typically includes hearing amplification or cochlear implantation, combined with interprofessional coordination for comorbidities. Prognosis varies widely and depends on the severity of associated abnormalities and the timing of intervention. This activity for healthcare professionals is designed to enhance learners' proficiency in evaluating and managing syndromic sensorineural hearing loss. Participants will broaden their grasp of the condition's risk factors, etiology, epidemiology, pathophysiology, and clinical presentation. The best diagnostic and therapeutic practices will also be emphasized. Greater proficiency will enable clinicians to collaborate within an interprofessional team caring for affected individuals.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

certifying_boards: American Board of Otolaryngology - Head and Neck Surgery

courses.title: Abnormal Labor in Obstetrics: Recognition and Management
courses.description: Abnormal labor encompasses deviations from the expected progression of childbirth, which is typically characterized by regular, painful uterine contractions that produce progressive cervical effacement and dilation. The normal process is divided into 3 stages, involving cervical dilation, fetal delivery, and placental expulsion. Abnormalities may arise in any stage, presenting as prolonged, protracted, or arrested progression of labor. Classification is guided by defined time parameters outlined by the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists and the World Health Organization. Contributing factors include inadequate uterine contractions, cephalopelvic disproportion, fetal malposition, or soft tissue obstruction. Early recognition and timely management of abnormal labor are essential to minimizing maternal and fetal morbidity, reducing the risk of unnecessary cesarean delivery, and optimizing obstetric outcomes. Clinicians must understand physiologic labor patterns and pathologic variations to guide appropriate interventions. Participation in this course equips clinicians with practical knowledge to identify and evaluate normal and abnormal labor progress using standardized assessment tools and evidence-based guidelines. Learners develop skills to recognize complications such as dystocia, arrest disorders, and fetal distress, and to implement timely management strategies. The course emphasizes patient-centered care, effective communication, and interprofessional collaboration among obstetric clinicians, midwives, anesthesiologists, nurses, and neonatologists. This collaborative approach ensures coordinated decision-making during labor, enhances maternal safety, and improves neonatal outcomes. By strengthening competence in labor assessment, timely intervention, and multidisciplinary teamwork, participants are prepared to deliver safer, higher-quality obstetric care that reduces complications and supports optimal birth experiences.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Hypotonia
courses.description: Hypotonia is an easily recognizable entity but determining the etiology is a challenging task for a clinician given its vast differential. Systematically approaching the case can help determine the underlying etiology, which is crucial for further management and prognosis of the disease. Having a multidisciplinary approach in the management of these patients has been found to have overall better outcomes. This activity reviews the evaluation and management of hypotonia and highlights the role of the interprofessional team in managing patients with this condition.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Idiopathic Pulmonary Hemosiderosis
courses.description: Idiopathic pulmonary hemosiderosis is a diagnosis of exclusion within the broad clinical syndrome of diffuse alveolar hemorrhage, representing rare but potentially life-threatening pulmonary disorders associated with recurrent alveolar bleeding, progressive lung injury, and substantial morbidity and mortality. This course reviews the diagnostic complexity arising from the broad differential diagnosis of idiopathic pulmonary hemosiderosis, which includes immune-mediated vasculitis, infection, coagulopathy, cardiovascular disease, structural abnormalities, and drug-induced causes, and its clinical features, including hemoptysis, diffuse pulmonary infiltrates, respiratory failure, or isolated iron-deficiency anemia, particularly in children. This activity examines growing evidence supporting immune dysregulation as a major pathogenic mechanism and highlights clinically important associations, such as Lane Hamilton syndrome and ANCA-associated vasculitis. Participants will gain an understanding of the classification, imaging, bronchoscopy, histopathology, and evidence-informed management strategies for idiopathic pulmonary hemosiderosis, including corticosteroid therapy, steroid-sparing immunosuppression, dietary interventions, and emerging therapies. This activity for healthcare professionals is designed to enhance the learner's competence in identifying idiopathic pulmonary hemosiderosis, performing the recommended evaluation, and implementing an appropriate interprofessional approach when managing this condition.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Hypertensive Crisis
courses.description: Hypertensive crisis is a severe elevation in blood pressure that may result from uncontrolled hypertension, renal or endocrine disorders, medication nonadherence, or other underlying conditions. Rapid increases in blood pressure can lead to endothelial injury, impaired autoregulation, and ischemic damage to vital organs. Hypertensive crises are classified as urgencies, which occur without acute target-organ injury, or emergencies, which are accompanied by life-threatening damage to the brain, heart, kidneys, or other organs. Clinical manifestations may include headache, visual disturbances, altered mental status, chest pain, heart failure, oliguria, or hematuria. Diagnosis requires prompt assessment of blood pressure and evaluation for target-organ involvement using laboratory studies, electrocardiography, and imaging. Management depends on the presence or absence of acute organ injury and ranges from oral antihypertensive therapy with close follow-up to immediate intravenous treatment. Early recognition and intervention are essential to prevent stroke, myocardial infarction, renal failure, and death.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Inborn Errors of Metabolism
courses.description: Inborn errors of metabolism are inherited disorders that disrupt metabolic pathways and may present with acute decompensation, progressive multisystem disease, or neuropsychiatric symptoms across the lifespan. Delayed recognition remains a clinically important gap because nonspecific presentations can resemble common pediatric emergencies, leading to missed diagnoses, preventable complications, and avoidable mortality. This activity reviews age-specific clinical clues, initial laboratory evaluation, advanced diagnostic testing, acute stabilization, long-term treatment strategies, and complication prevention. Participants will strengthen their ability to identify high-risk presentations, interpret metabolic patterns, initiate timely emergency measures, and select appropriate confirmatory testing. The activity also emphasizes coordinated interprofessional care, including dietary treatment, genetic counseling, emergency planning, and specialty collaboration, to improve patient-centered outcomes, reduce recurrent metabolic crises, and support long-term quality of life.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Hypertensive Heart Disease
courses.description: Hypertensive heart disease (HHD) refers to a constellation of changes affecting the left ventricle, left atrium, and coronary arteries resulting from chronic elevation of blood pressure. This sustained pressure increases cardiac workload, leading to both structural and functional alterations, including left ventricular hypertrophy, which may progress to heart failure. HHD encompasses both the direct and indirect consequences of prolonged high blood pressure, including systolic or diastolic heart failure, conduction abnormalities, particularly atrial fibrillation, and an elevated risk of coronary artery disease. Risk factors for HHD include long-standing hypertension, older age, male sex, Black race, obesity, diabetes, and chronic kidney disease. Clinically, patients may present with exertional dyspnea, fatigue, palpitations, or signs of heart failure, such as bipedal edema and hepatomegaly. Diagnosis is based on a combination of clinical history, electrocardiography, echocardiography, and cardiac imaging to assess left ventricular mass, function, and evidence of hypertrophy or fibrosis. Management focuses on strict blood pressure control using agents such as angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors, angiotensin receptor blockers, calcium channel blockers, and diuretics, along with lifestyle modification and treatment of comorbid conditions to prevent disease progression and reduce cardiovascular risk. Prognosis depends on the degree of hypertrophy and cardiac dysfunction, with more advanced disease associated with an increased risk of heart failure, arrhythmias, and cardiovascular mortality. Patients with left ventricular hypertrophy face significantly higher morbidity and mortality. This activity for healthcare professionals is designed to hone learners' skills in evaluating and managing HHD. Participants will deepen their understanding of the condition's etiology, epidemiology, pathophysiology, and symptomatology. Evidence-based diagnostic and therapeutic...
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

practice_areas: Advanced Heart Failure and Transplant Cardiology

courses.title: Insulin Resistance
courses.description: Insulin resistance, identified as an impaired biologic response to insulin stimulation of target tissues, primarily involves liver, muscle, and adipose tissue. Insulin resistance impairs glucose disposal, resulting in a compensatory increase in beta-cell insulin production and hyperinsulinemia. The metabolic consequences of insulin resistance can result in hyperglycemia, hypertension, dyslipidemia, hyperuricemia, elevated inflammatory markers, endothelial dysfunction, and a prothrombotic state. The predominant consequence of insulin resistance is type 2 diabetes(T2D). Insulin resistance is thought to precede the development of T2D by 10 to 15 years. Lifestyle modifications should be the primary focus when treating insulin resistance. Nutritional intervention with calorie reduction and avoidance of carbohydrates that stimulate excessive insulin demand is a cornerstone of treatment. Physical activity helps to increase energy expenditure and improve skeletal muscle insulin sensitivity. Medications also can improve insulin response and reduce insulin demand. Most of the complications from insulin resistance are related to the development of vascular complications and nonalcoholic fatty liver disease. This activity reviews the etiology, pathogenesis, epidemiology, presentation, treatment, and potential complications of insulin resistance and highlights the crucial role of the interprofessional team in its management.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Ischemic Stroke
courses.description: Acute ischemic stroke remains a leading cause of death and long-term disability worldwide, requiring rapid recognition, accurate etiologic classification, and timely reperfusion therapy to improve neurologic outcomes. This course reviews advances in neuroimaging, thrombolytic therapy, mechanical thrombectomy, and evidence-based stroke systems of care, which continue to reshape the early management of acute ischemic stroke across diverse clinical settings. This activity explores the pathophysiology, vascular syndromes, cerebral autoregulation, ischemic penumbra, diagnostic evaluation, and current treatment strategies outlined in contemporary stroke guidelines. Participants will gain an in-depth understanding of stroke subtypes using the TOAST classification system, characteristic clinical presentations associated with major vascular territories, imaging findings relevant to treatment eligibility, and current recommendations for intravenous thrombolysis, endovascular thrombectomy, blood pressure management, and acute inpatient care. This activity for healthcare professionals is designed to enhance the learner's competence in identifying acute ischemic stroke, performing the recommended evaluation, and implementing an appropriate interprofessional approach when managing this condition.

courses.title: Echinococcus Granulosus
courses.description: Echinococcosis (Echinococcus granulosus) is a zoonotic larval infection that infects humans globally. Patients with this condition may be asymptomatic for years and only present symptoms when the liver cysts (hydatid cysts) rupture. This activity illustrates the evaluation and management of echinococcosis and reviews the role of the interprofessional team in improving care for patients with this condition.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Neonatal Jaundice
courses.description: Neonatal jaundice is a clinical manifestation of elevated total serum bilirubin, termed neonatal hyperbilirubinemia, which results from bilirubin that is deposited into an infant's skin. The characteristic features of neonatal jaundice include yellowish skin, sclerae, and mucous membranes. Neonatal jaundice is usually a mild, transient, and self-limiting condition known as physiologic jaundice. However, this should be distinguished from the more severe pathologic jaundice. The two types of neonatal hyperbilirubinemia are unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia and conjugated hyperbilirubinemia. In most neonates, unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia is the cause of clinical jaundice. However, some infants have conjugated hyperbilirubinemia, which is always pathologic and signifies an underlying medical or surgical etiology. Failure to identify and treat pathologic jaundice may result in bilirubin encephalopathy and associated neurological sequelae. When neonatal jaundice is clinically identified, the underlying etiology of neonatal hyperbilirubinemia must be determined. Unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia is diagnosed by assessing bilirubin levels with a transcutaneous measurement device or blood samples for total serum bilirubin. Conjugated hyperbilirubinemia is typically diagnosed through laboratory studies, including serum aminotransferase, prothrombin time, urine cultures, tests for inborn errors of metabolism, and, in some cases, imaging studies. Phototherapy and exchange transfusions are the mainstays of treatment of unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia, and a subset of patients also respond to intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG). Treatment of conjugated hyperbilirubinemia is more complex and depends on the etiology of the jaundice. This activity for healthcare professionals is designed to enhance the learner's competence when managing neonatal jaundice, equipping them with updated knowledge, skills, and strategies for timely identification, effective interventions, and improved...
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Familial Hypercholesterolemia
courses.description: Familial hypercholesterolemia is a group of inherited genetic defects that lead to the severe elevation of serum cholesterol concentrations. Clinically familial hypercholesterolemia is diagnosed by a high serum level of low-density lipoprotein (LDL) cholesterol and genetically is characterized into two subgroups: (1) autosomal dominant (AD), (2) codominant transmission with 90% or higher penetrance. This activity reviews the evaluation and management of familial hypercholesterolemia and highlights the interprofessional team's role in evaluating and treating patients with this disease.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: ICU Delirium
courses.description: Delirium is defined by DSM-5 criteria as an impairment in attention and awareness that develops over a relatively short time interval that is associated with additional cognitive deficits. There is a prevalence of delirium within the ICU setting (ICU delirium). This activity reviews the evaluation and treatment of ICU delirium and highlights the role of the interprofessional team in evaluating and treating critically ill patients with this condition.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Hypoplastic Left Heart Syndrome
courses.description: Hypoplastic left heart syndrome (HLHS) is a rare but severe congenital heart defect characterized by underdevelopment of left-sided heart structures, including the left ventricle, aortic valve, mitral valve, and ascending aorta. This condition leads to critically impaired systemic circulation, necessitating a patent ductus arteriosus for survival in the immediate neonatal period. Diagnosis often occurs prenatally through fetal echocardiography, with postnatal clinical findings including cyanosis, weak pulses, and signs of low cardiac output as the ductus closes. Management requires a staged surgical approach, including the Norwood, Glenn, and Fontan procedures, to establish single-ventricle physiology compatible with life. Despite advancements in care, HLHS patients face significant risks of morbidity and mortality, including heart failure, arrhythmias, and thromboembolic events, with long-term survival dependent on specialized medical and surgical interventions. This course provides clinicians with a comprehensive understanding of HLHS, from its pathophysiology and diagnostic approach to the intricacies of surgical management and long-term care. Participants gain insights into optimizing perioperative hemodynamics, managing complications of staged palliation, and addressing long-term issues such as Fontan physiology failure and associated comorbidities. Additionally, the course highlights the importance of interdisciplinary collaboration and patient-family education in improving outcomes. Clinicians emerge with enhanced clinical competence and confidence to care for patients with HLHS across the lifespan, contributing to improved survival rates and quality of life for this complex population.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

practice_areas: Advanced Heart Failure and Transplant Cardiology

courses.title: Anterior Cruciate Ligament Knee Injury
courses.description: The anterior cruciate ligament is one of the two cruciate ligaments that aids in stabilizing the knee joint. It is the most commonly injured ligament in the knee, commonly occurring in football, soccer, and basketball players. Treatment consists of the RICE therapy, which includes rest, ice, compression of the affected knee, and elevation of the affected lower extremity. This activity describes the evaluation and management strategies for such injuries and stresses the role of team-based interprofessional care for patients with anterior cruciate ligament injuries.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

certifying_boards: American Board of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation

courses.title: Idiopathic (Genetic) Generalized Epilepsy
courses.description: A seizure can be defined as transient signs and symptoms associated with abnormal, hypersynchronous discharge of cortical neurons, and epilepsy is defined as a brain disorder "characterized by an enduring predisposition to generate epileptic seizures and by the neurobiologic, cognitive, psychological, and social consequences of this condition." Idiopathic generalized epilepsy is a subtype of generalized epilepsy and consists of childhood absence epilepsy, juvenile absence epilepsy, juvenile myoclonic epilepsy, and generalized tonic-clonic seizures alone. It is estimated that over 50 million people are affected by epilepsy worldwide. The pathophysiology of epilepsy will depend on its etiology, with thalamocortical interaction being the most well-understood. The diagnosis of epilepsy is primarily clinical based on history and lack of neurologic findings in the interictal state, with electroencephalogram (EEG) as supportive evidence. Treatment strategies will vary on etiology and the side effect profile of medications and other treatment modalities. This activity will review the diagnosis and management of idiopathic generalized epilepsy and highlight the importance of an interprofessional team in providing the highest standard of care for patients suffering from this disease.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Iritis
courses.description: Anterior uveitis (iritis) is the inflammation of the anterior chamber and the iris. Uveitis is often idiopathic, but it may be triggered by genetic, immune, traumatic, or infectious mechanisms. The symptoms include redness, sensitivity to light, and pain. Slit-lamp examination reveals cells in the anterior chamber. Proper evaluation is necessary for recurrent anterior uveitis. The management options include topical steroids and cycloplegics. With appropriate treatment and follow-up, it has a good prognosis. This activity highlights the role of the interprofessional team in caring for patients with this condition.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Keratoconus
courses.description: Keratoconus is a progressive bilateral corneal ectatic disorder characterized by cone-like steepening of the cornea, irregular stromal thinning, and significant vision loss. Keratoconus is a leading indication for corneal transplantation in Western countries and can be associated with other medical conditions. Although keratoconus was traditionally viewed as a noninflammatory disorder, recent studies suggest the involvement of potential inflammatory components. Patients affected by keratoconus experience decreased visual acuity due to irregular astigmatism and myopia, which results from corneal distortion and scarring. The initial detection of keratoconus can pose challenges, as patients often experience difficulty achieving adequate visual correction with spectacles and encounter variable reductions in visual acuity, image distortion, and increased sensitivity to glare and light. Microscopic examination reveals thinning of the stromal layer, the presence of iron in the epithelial basement membrane, and ruptures in the Bowman membrane. Although keratoconus may present independently, it can also be associated with other medical conditions such as Down syndrome, Leber congenital amaurosis, and mitral valve prolapse. Initial treatment options for keratoconus, personalized for each patient, include prescription spectacles, rigid gas-permeable contact lenses, and collagen cross-linking, which, if administered early, may slow or halt disease progression. In advanced cases where contact lenses prove ineffective, keratoplasty may be required as a further intervention. This activity delves into the etiology, epidemiology, pathophysiology, diagnosis, and management of keratoconus, emphasizing early detection of the condition. This activity also provides healthcare professionals with essential knowledge and tools to mitigate morbidity and enhance the overall quality of life for affected patients.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Perilymphatic Fistula
courses.description: Perilymphatic fistula (PLF) is an abnormal connection between the inner ear and surrounding structures, typically the middle ear or mastoid cavity, allowing perilymph leakage. Less commonly, it may connect to the intracranial space or other canals. While most cases are linked to trauma or surgical procedures, 20% to 40% remain idiopathic. Symptoms include hearing loss, disequilibrium, aural fullness, autophony, and tinnitus, often making diagnosis challenging. This course explores PLF, including the clinical manifestations and current diagnostic challenges, as the diagnosis of PLFs is controversial, with no clear consensus among experts in the field. This activity for healthcare professionals is designed to enhance the learner's competence in identifying PLF, performing the recommended evaluation, and implementing an appropriate interprofessional approach when managing this condition to optimize outcomes and minimize complications.

courses.title: Hyphema
courses.description: Hyphema is the accumulation of red blood cells (RBCs) in the eye's anterior chamber. Blood must be grossly visible, either on direct inspection or via slit-lamp examination. Blood accumulates from the disruption of the iris or ciliary body vessels, usually due to trauma or underlying medical conditions. This activity describes the pathophysiology, evaluation, and management of hyphema and highlights the role of the interprofessional team in caring for affected patients.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Fungal Keratitis
courses.description: This CME activity provides a comprehensive overview of fungal keratitis, a cause of corneal impairment. Participants will delve into its epidemiology, risk factors, and clinical manifestations, learning to differentiate it from bacterial and other forms of keratitis. Diagnostic approaches, including polymerase chain reaction and microscopic examination, and the latest advancements in antifungal treatments are explored. Through case studies and interactive discussions, healthcare professionals will enhance their ability to diagnose, manage, and prevent fungal keratitis, ultimately improving patient outcomes.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Ileostomy
courses.description: An ileostomy is a procedure in which the lumen of the ileum, part of the small bowel, is brought through the abdominal wall via a surgically-created opening called a stoma. The purpose of an ileostomy is to evacuate stool from the body via the ileum instead of the usual route via the anus. This activity reviews the indications, contraindications, and potential benefits of the ileostomy and highlights the role of the interprofessional team in the management of patients with a stoma.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Hyperpituitarism
courses.description: The pituitary gland produces and secretes various hormones that play a vital role in regulating endocrine function within the body. The pituitary gland consists of an anterior and a posterior lobe. Hormones produced by the anterior lobe of the pituitary gland include growth hormone (GH), thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH), luteinizing hormone (LH), follicular stimulating hormone (FSH), adrenocorticotropin (ACTH), and prolactin. The hormones stored and released from the posterior pituitary are antidiuretic hormone (ie, vasopressin) and oxytocin. Antidiuretic hormone (ADH) and oxytocin are produced by neurosecretory cells in the hypothalamus. Hyperpituitarism is defined as an excessive secretion or production of 1 of the hormones produced by the pituitary gland. The primary causes of hyperpituitarism are various hormone-secreting pituitary tumors. This activity for healthcare professionals is designed to enhance the learner's competence when managing hyperpituitarism, equipping them with updated knowledge, skills, and strategies for timely identification, effective interventions, and improved interprofessional care coordination, leading to improved patient outcomes.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Filarial Hydrocele
courses.description: Filarial hydrocele is a scrotal swelling caused by a parasitic infection, typically due to Wuchereria bancrofti. This condition is endemic to tropical and subtropical regions around the world, particularly in Asia and in areas of poor socioeconomic status. Filarial hydrocele causes physical and mental distress for affected males, impacting their fertility, mobility, and ability to earn a living. Understanding the transmission and clinical manifestations of filarial hydrocele is essential for its eradication and effective treatment. Preventive therapy in endemic regions is summarized, based on individual characteristics and local disease patterns. Public health measures and education about this condition are crucial to prevent the spread of this treatable disease and reduce morbidity. The surgical procedure to repair filarial hydroceles is reviewed along with tips to minimize postoperative complications, reduce recurrences, and improve outcomes. This activity outlines the prevention, evaluation, treatment, and surgical management of filarial hydroceles, highlighting the role of the healthcare team in patient care.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Immunodeficiency Disorders (Primary and Secondary)
courses.description: This continuing medical education activity provides clinicians with an evidence-based review of primary and secondary immunodeficiency syndromes, including inborn errors of immunity, acquired immune dysfunction, diagnostic evaluation, treatment strategies, and prevention of complications. Immunodeficiency disorders increase the risk of recurrent, severe, opportunistic, or unusual infections and may also present with autoimmunity, inflammation, lymphoproliferation, or malignant neoplasms. The activity addresses the gap between recommended systematic evaluation and real-world underrecognition, delayed diagnosis, incomplete immune testing, and inconsistent differentiation of inherited and acquired causes. Participants will review clinical warning signs, infection patterns, immune compartment defects, indications for targeted laboratory assessment, indications for genetic testing, infection prevention, immunoglobulin replacement, antimicrobial prophylaxis, and curative or disease-directed therapies. The activity is designed to strengthen diagnostic accuracy, improve evidence-based treatment selection, reduce preventable infections and complications, and support coordinated interprofessional care that improves long-term patient safety and outcomes.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Irritable Bowel Syndrome
courses.description: Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) is a complex and highly prevalent disorder of gut-brain interaction (DGBI), characterized by recurrent abdominal pain and altered bowel habits, including constipation, diarrhea, or a combination of both. Despite its chronic impact on quality of life and healthcare costs, IBS remains underdiagnosed. This activity reviews the epidemiology, pathophysiology, diagnostic criteria, and interprofessional management strategies for IBS. The role of visceral hypersensitivity, dysmotility, microbiota alterations, psychosocial influences, and gut-brain axis dysfunction in IBS pathogenesis is also discussed. This activity explores accurate diagnosis using the Rome IV criteria, appropriate evaluation strategies to exclude organic pathology, and evidence-based treatments tailored to the various subtypes of IBS, including lifestyle and dietary modifications, pharmacologic interventions, and the utility of gut-directed psychotherapies. Special attention is given to fostering a strong therapeutic alliance and shared decision-making to improve outcomes. This activity for healthcare professionals is designed to enhance the learner's competence in identifying IBS, performing the recommended clinical evaluation, and implementing an appropriate interprofessional approach when managing this condition, thereby reducing unnecessary diagnostic testing and providing personalized, patient-centered care.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Primary Hyperparathyroidism
courses.description: Primary hyperparathyroidism (PHPT) is a common endocrine disorder caused by autonomous parathyroid hormone secretion, leading to hypercalcemia and systemic complications involving bone, kidney, and neurocognitive function. This activity reviews the etiology, epidemiology, pathophysiology, and the varying clinical presentations of PHPT. Most cases arise from a single benign adenoma, with less frequent multigland disease or carcinoma. Widespread biochemical screening has shifted the most frequent presentation from classic symptomatic disease to predominantly asymptomatic hypercalcemia, including normocalcemic and normohormonal variants. Additionally, this course outlines the diagnostic evaluation, which relies on biochemical confirmation of elevated or inappropriately normal PTH, with imaging reserved for surgical planning and evidence-based management of PHPT, including criteria for parathyroidectomy, intraoperative PTH monitoring, and postoperative care, as well as nonsurgical options. Participants will also gain an understanding of typical and atypical presentations, interpreting laboratory findings, differentiating PHPT from secondary causes, and determining appropriate referral for surgical or medical management. This activity for healthcare professionals is designed to enhance the learner's competence in identifying the PHPT, performing the recommended evaluation, reducing complications such as bone loss and nephrolithiasis, and implementing an appropriate interprofessional approach when managing this condition to support patient safety, optimize outcomes, and enhance long-term monitoring and care coordination in clinical practice.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: IgA Nephropathy (Berger Disease)
courses.description: Immunoglobulin A (IgA) nephropathy, or IgAN, also known as Berger disease, is one of the leading causes of glomerulonephritis and renal failure. This disease is a prevalent form of glomerulonephritis characterized by the deposition of IgA in the glomerular basement membrane. Immune-mediated damage to the basement membrane results in hematuria, proteinuria, and renal insufficiency. Pathologically, a spectrum of glomerular lesions may be seen, with mesangial proliferation and prominent IgA deposition being the most commonly observed change. Despite being a common disease, accurate prevalence data for IgAN are limited due to the necessity of a renal biopsy to establish the diagnosis. Management entails inducing remission and preventing complications by addressing proteinuria, estimated glomerular filtration rate (GFR), blood pressure, and histological findings, while treatment strategies aim to mitigate immune reactions, reduce IgA deposition, and slow renal damage progression. This activity comprehensively reviews the etiology, pathogenesis, evaluation, and management of IgAN while also explaining the role of the interprofessional healthcare team in evaluating and treating patients with this condition effectively.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Keratitis
courses.description: Keratitis is a clinical entity wherein inflammatory cells infiltrate different corneal layers in response to noxious stimuli, either infectious exogenous agents or self-antigens. The inflammatory reaction may result in the suppurative melting of corneal epithelium and stroma, resulting in the formation of ulcers. This results not only in the loss of corneal clarity but also threatens the integrity of the globe. Such cases may result in corneal blindness. This activity helps clinicians identify the etiological agent at the earliest based on clinical features and appropriate diagnostic tests and manage these patients with the latest treatment options. It reviews the role of the interprofessional team.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Keratopathy
courses.description: The literal meaning of keratopathy is a disease of the cornea. Each keratopathy is seen in association with different clinical scenarios. Some may represent some local causes whereas some may point at systemic causes. This activity describes etiology, pathophysiology, clinical features, and highlights the role of the interprofessional team in the management of various commonly presenting keratopathies.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Iron Overload and Toxicity
courses.description: Iron overload and toxicity comprise a spectrum of clinical conditions resulting from excessive iron accumulation in the body. Chronic iron overload typically arises from hereditary hemochromatosis or repeated blood transfusions, especially in patients with thalassemia or sickle cell disease. Acute toxicity often results from the ingestion of iron supplements, particularly in pediatric populations. Unregulated iron absorption or parenteral administration bypasses hepcidin-ferroportin regulation, leading to intracellular deposition and the generation of reactive oxygen species. This oxidative stress damages key organs, including the liver, heart, pancreas, and endocrine glands. Clinical manifestations vary with disease duration and severity, ranging from fatigue and arthralgia to life-threatening complications such as cirrhosis, cardiomyopathy, and hepatic failure. Diagnosis relies on clinical suspicion supported by laboratory findings, such as elevated serum ferritin and transferrin saturation, alongside imaging studies. Depending on acuity, management strategies include chelation therapy, gastrointestinal decontamination, or therapeutic phlebotomy. Through this educational activity, healthcare professionals gain a comprehensive understanding of iron overload and toxicity, including underlying etiologies, risk factors, pathophysiologic mechanisms, and clinical presentations. Participants review current evidence-based diagnostic tools and therapeutic interventions tailored to acute and chronic presentations. Emphasis is placed on early recognition and timely intervention to mitigate long-term organ damage. Collaborative care within interprofessional teams encompassing physicians, nurses, pharmacists, and dietitians optimizes treatment planning and patient monitoring. This coordinated approach enhances clinical outcomes by integrating diverse expertise, improving adherence to therapeutic regimens, and supporting patient-centered decision-making.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

practice_areas: Advanced Heart Failure and Transplant Cardiology

courses.title: Hypercoagulability
courses.description: Hypercoagulability or thrombophilia is the increased tendency of blood to thrombose. A normal and healthy response to bleeding for maintaining hemostasis involves the formation of a stable clot, and the process is called coagulation. Hypercoagulability describes the pathologic state of exaggerated coagulation or coagulation in the absence of bleeding. Arterial thrombosis, such as in myocardial infarction and stroke, is different from venous thromboses, such as deep venous thrombosis (DVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE). This activity reviews the cause and presentation of hypercoagulability and highlights the role of the interprofessional team in its management
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Hyperuricemia
courses.description: Hyperuricemia is a common disorder that affects patients of all ages and genders. The most common manifestation of hyperuricemia is gout, which can be very painful and is amenable to treatment. Hyperuricemia is also associated with uric acid and calcium nephrolithiasis. Hyperuricemia affects about 38 million Americans, over 11% of the population, and the incidence is increasing worldwide. Most patients with hyperuricemia are asymptomatic, and the diagnosis requires a high degree of suspicion as serum uric acid levels are no longer routinely measured on serum blood panels. Patients with hyperuricemia who develop gout are usually best treated with a xanthine oxidase inhibitor like allopurinol. Depending on the urinary chemistry and stone type, allopurinol, potassium citrate, or both may be recommended in nephrolithiasis. This activity reviews the pathophysiology, presentation, evaluation, and treatment of hyperuricemia, as well as highlights the interprofessional team's role in caring for affected patients.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Hyperphosphatemia
courses.description: This article summarises the basics of Hyperphosphatemia, including its pathophysiology, evaluation, and management. Though this condition is seen more often in renal failure patients, several other non-renal conditions can also manifest with hyperphosphatemia. For complete management of hyperphosphatemia, it is essential to have an understanding of various regulatory mechanisms that affect phosphate levels.

courses.title: Hypothyroid Myopathy
courses.description: Hypothyroid myopathy, present in 30% to 80% of hypothyroid patients, manifests in both congenital and acquired cases with generalized myalgias, muscle weakness, and muscle pain or stiffness. Thyroid hormone plays a vital role in metabolism, growth, and organ function and is a primary regulator of energy availability and consumption in the musculoskeletal system. Proximal muscles such as thighs, hips, shoulders, and neck are commonly involved, impacting activities such as stair climbing, rising from a seated position, and lifting objects. Severe or untreated hypothyroidism can prompt substantial muscle disease, leading to severe functional limitations. Symptoms of hypothyroid myopathy can be gradual in onset and nonspecific, requiring a high index of suspicion from clinicians. All patients diagnosed with hypothyroidism should be questioned about musculoskeletal symptoms. Rarely, severe hypothyroid myopathy can result in muscle necrosis, acute compartment syndrome, or respiratory failure. This activity discusses its presentation, assessment, and management, underscoring the pivotal role of the interprofessional team.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Hysteroscopy
courses.description: Hysteroscopy involves inserting a rigid or flexible hysteroscope through the cervical canal into the uterus and then using distending media to allow for complete visualization of the endometrial cavity, allowing for minimally invasive diagnosis and surgical management of endocervical and intrauterine pathology. Hysteroscopy is considered the gold standard technique for evaluating and managing intrauterine pathology. Indications for hysteroscopy are numerous, including abnormal uterine bleeding, infertility, removal of intrauterine foreign bodies, and congenital müllerian anomalies. This course explores this commonly performed procedure, including the current indications, established guidelines on disstention mediums, and complications associated with hysteroscopy. This activity for healthcare professionals is designed to enhance the learner's competence in identifying the indications for hysteroscopy, performing the procedure with proper technique, and implementing an appropriate interprofessional approach when managing this condition.

courses.title: The Impact of an Increasingly Toxic Drug Supply on Growing Morbidity among People who Inject Drugs: Epidemiologic Update from the Field
courses.description: Originally presented live at the 2026 Kentucky Overdose Prevention Summit (Louisville, KY). This keynote examines trends in the illicit drug supply and growing morbidity among people who inject drugs, drawing on epidemiologic data from law enforcement drug seizures and community-based drug checking programs. The presenter explores how an increasingly synthetic and toxic drug supply dominated by illicit fentanyl and novel adulterants is reshaping patterns of use and escalating overdose and infectious disease risk. Attendees gain an understanding of how drug market dynamics, including consumer preferences for specific substances and drug combinations, interact with harm reduction and treatment access. Upon completion of this activity, participants will be able to: 1. Learn how law enforcement drug seizures and community-based drug checking data can serve as proxy indicators for the illicit drug supply. 2. Understand the pharmacologic effects associated with an increasingly synthetic and toxic drug supply and their impact on public health and safety. 3. Recognize how the illicit drug market exerts influence on consumer preference for specific drugs, drug combinations, and modes of use, including the intent to be treated. Presented by: Jon Zibbell, PhD Senior Scientist, Center for Behavioral Health & Wellbeing, RTI International.

The faculty will provide guidance to assist participants in applying new knowledge to their practices.

courses.title: Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) Compliance
courses.description: The US Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA), enacted in 1996, was established to safeguard patient privacy and secure health information. HIPAA sets strict standards for managing, transmitting, and storing protected health information. HIPAA applies to healthcare providers, insurers, and other organizations handling patient data, mandating safeguards to prevent unauthorized access or misuse of sensitive information. HIPAA regulations uphold patients' rights to confidentiality and empower them to control the disclosure of their health information, fostering trust in healthcare systems. This activity covers key aspects of HIPAA regulations, including privacy and security rules, breach notification requirements, and practical applications to ensure compliance. This activity also focuses on educating healthcare professionals on their legal and ethical responsibilities regarding patient privacy and data security. This activity underscores the importance of HIPAA in daily healthcare practices, strengthening patient trust and ensuring compliance with legal requirements.

courses.title: Gonorrhea
courses.description: Gonorrhea is a common sexually transmitted infection caused by Neisseria gonorrhoeae, characterized by infection of columnar epithelium at urogenital, rectal, pharyngeal, and conjunctival sites. This course reviews the clinical presentation of gonorrhea, which ranges from asymptomatic infection particularly in individuals assigned female at birth to symptomatic urethritis, cervicitis, or pelvic inflammatory disease, with potential progression to infertility, ectopic pregnancy, or disseminated disease. Participants will also gain an understanding of the pathophysiology, risk assessment using trauma-informed sexual history-taking, appropriate use of diagnostic modalities, and evolving treatment options for this condition, driven by increasing antimicrobial resistance, including newly approved oral agents. This activity for healthcare professionals is designed to enhance learners' competence in identifying varied presentations, implementing effective treatment and partner management strategies, applying updated screening recommendations, performing the recommended evaluation, and coordinating an appropriate interprofessional approach to managing this condition, thereby reducing complications, transmission, and public health burden.

courses.title: Hemophilia A
courses.description: Hemophilia encompasses a group of inherited disorders that alter blood coagulation. Classical hemophilia, also known as hemophilia A, is a hereditary hemorrhagic disorder resulting from a congenital deficit of factor VIII that manifests as protracted and excessive bleeding either spontaneously or secondary to trauma. This activity describes the cause of hemophilia A, reviews its presentation, and highlights the role of the interprofessional team in its management.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Hand and Wrist Rheumatoid Arthritis
courses.description: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is an immune-mediated multisystem inflammatory disease that predominantly affects the synovial joints. This activity provides a brief review of rheumatoid arthritis, with a focus on rheumatoid arthritis of the hands as regards the presentation, evaluation, and management and highlights the role of the interprofessional team in the diagnosis and management of RA of hand.

courses.title: Gestational Trophoblastic Disease
courses.description: Gestational trophoblastic disease (GTD) is a group of tumors defined by abnormal trophoblastic proliferation involving both benign and malignant entities. Histologically, GTD is divided into hydatidiform moles (containing villi) and other trophoblastic neoplasms (lacking villi). The nonmolar or malignant forms of GTD are called gestational trophoblastic neoplasia (GTN) and include the invasive mole, choriocarcinoma, epithelioid trophoblastic tumor (ETT), and placental-site trophoblastic tumor (PSTT). GTN can occur weeks or years following any pregnancy but occurs most commonly after a molar pregnancy. GTN can metastasize and be fatal if not treated. This activity reviews the causes and pathophysiology of GTD and highlights the role of the interprofessional team in its management. Participants gain insights into evidence-based diagnostic approaches, including histopathological evaluation and imaging modalities, to facilitate accurate and timely diagnosis. Challenges in treatment, including considerations for fertility preservation, chemotherapy regimens, emerging targeted therapies, and follow-up surveillance, are addressed. Clinicians gain insight into patient-centered care and the need for effective communication and collaboration among the interprofessional team to achieve optimal, comprehensive care for patients with GTD.

courses.title: Supracondylar Humerus Fractures
courses.description: Elbow fractures are more common in the pediatric population than in the adult population. Children often utilize an outstretched arm as a protective mechanism when falling, creating a high incidence of fractures about the elbow. Supracondylar fractures of the humerus account for up to 18% of pediatric fractures and 60% of elbow fractures. Despite evolutions in the evaluation and treatment over the years, these fractures still pose considerable challenges to orthopedic surgeons. This activity reviews the mechanism of injury, classification, and management of these injuries in the pediatric population and highlights the role of the interprofessional team in evaluating and improving the care of patients with this condition.
