courses.title: Electrophysiology Lab Maneuvers to Differentiate Supraventricular Tachycardia
courses.description: Supraventricular tachycardia (SVT) refers to a group of tachyarrhythmias that originate at or above the His bundle. These arrhythmias are typically characterized by atrial and/or ventricular rates exceeding 100 beats per minute (bpm) in adults and more than 200 bpm in children. This activity reviews key electrophysiology laboratory maneuvers used to differentiate the various subtypes of SVT, including atrial tachycardia, atrioventricular nodal reentrant tachycardia, atrioventricular reciprocating tachycardia, and junctional tachycardia. Atrial fibrillation and flutter are also acknowledged as common SVTs. Accurate diagnosis is critical for effective treatment, especially with the widespread use of catheter ablation. Maneuvers performed during sinus rhythm and tachycardia include atrial and ventricular pacing, premature contractions, and observations of conduction intervals. Observations such as concentric versus eccentric atrial activation help distinguish nodal from extranodal pathways. Techniques such as ventricular overdrive pacing and His-synchronous premature ventricular contractions are also used to clarify the underlying mechanism of SVT. Overall, these diagnostic strategies are essential for guiding targeted therapy and improving outcomes in patients with complex arrhythmias. This activity focuses on procedural techniques used in the electrophysiology laboratory rather than pharmacological management. This activity also provides healthcare professionals with practical tools and interpretive strategies to enhance diagnostic accuracy during electrophysiology studies, which help to effectively diagnose and treat patients with SVT. Additionally, this activity aims to enhance clinical decision-making and ultimately improve patient outcomes in the management of these complex and prevalent arrhythmias.

courses.title: Keshan Disease
courses.description: Keshan disease, discovered in 1935 in China's Keshan County, is a rare cardiomyopathy primarily found in regions with selenium-deficient soils, notably in specific rural and remote areas. This condition primarily presents as a potentially fatal and progressive form of heart disease, emphasizing the urgency for early identification and intervention due to its significant impact on cardiac health and the potential for chronic complications. The hallmark of the condition is myocardial necrosis and fibrosis, resulting in severe heart complications, such as cardiogenic shock and heart failure, with clinical manifestations ranging from acute cardiac episodes to arrhythmias. Distinguishing early-stage Keshan disease from other cardiomyopathies presents diagnostic challenges. Treatment usually includes diuretics and guideline-directed medical therapy. The complex nature of its etiology, multifaceted presentation, and the potential for long-term cardiac sequelae require healthcare professionals to comprehensively understand the disease. By fostering an environment of early detection and intervention, clinicians can substantially mitigate the complications associated with Keshan disease, improving patient outcomes and highlighting the importance of tailored dietary interventions and selenium supplementation. This activity centers on the complexities of Keshan disease, highlighting the critical roles of interprofessional healthcare team members in early recognition and intervention in latent cases to halt disease progression. This activity also emphasizes the importance of involving patients in collaborative decision-making, particularly regarding selenium supplementation or personalized dietary interventions. These strategies help prevent the progression of Keshan disease and significantly enhance the overall quality of life for those affected by this cardiac condition.

courses.title: Postbariatric Surgery Hypoglycemia
courses.description: Bariatric surgery has been reported to help achieve more significant and sustained weight loss than non-surgical management in patients with severe obesity. The number of bariatric surgeries performed has increased yearly from 2011 through 2019. Post-bariatric surgery hypoglycemia is an increasingly recognized complication. It can have significant effects on the quality of life of an individual. This activity reviews the various patterns of post-bariatric surgery hypoglycemia, pathophysiology, evaluation, differential diagnosis, and treatment and highlights the role of the interprofessional team in evaluating and treating patients with this condition.

courses.title: Coral Toxicity
courses.description: Coral toxicity, specifically caused by palytoxin, is a serious condition resulting from exposure to certain species of soft corals, such as Zoanthid corals. Palytoxin is a potent toxin that can be absorbed through inhalation or skin contact, particularly during the cleaning or removal of corals from home or public aquariums. Symptoms of exposure can include respiratory distress, skin irritation, and, in severe cases, cardiovascular issues. Early recognition and management are crucial in preventing complications and improving outcomes for affected individuals. Participants in this course learn how to effectively identify, evaluate, and treat coral toxicity caused by palytoxin. The course emphasizes the importance of working collaboratively with an interprofessional team, including emergency care professionals, toxicologists, and dermatologists, to ensure accurate diagnosis and prompt treatment. This integrated approach enhances patient outcomes by enabling timely interventions and coordinated follow-up care.

courses.title: Central Post-Stroke Pain Syndrome
courses.description: Central poststroke pain syndrome (CPSPS) presents as a complex neuropathic pain syndrome following a cerebrovascular accident (CVA), distinct from thalamic pain syndrome due to broader neural involvement. Symptoms, such as paresthesias and hyperalgesia, typically emerge 3 to 6 months post-CVA, with a variable onset. Diagnosis is challenging, requiring ruling out other post-stroke pathologies. Pharmacologic interventions, including analgesics and antidepressants, aim to alleviate pain and improve mood disturbances, while nonpharmacologic approaches, such as physical therapy and psychological interventions, address functional impairment and psychological well-being. This activity enhances CPSPS evaluation and management proficiency, deepening insight into its etiology, clinical characteristics, and evidence-based strategies. Treatment necessitates an interprofessional approach, integrating pharmacologic and nonpharmacologic interventions. Collaborating within an interprofessional healthcare team optimizes CPSPS management, tailoring treatment plans to individual needs. Clinicians optimize patient care by synergizing expertise across disciplines, ensuring timely interventions and comprehensive support. Improved collaboration enhances treatment adherence and patient satisfaction, ultimately enhancing the quality of life for individuals with CPSPS.

courses.title: Appendiceal Tumors
courses.description: Appendiceal tumors are a rare and heterogeneous group of neoplasms, often discovered incidentally during appendectomy or on histopathologic examination. These lesions account for approximately 0.9% to 1.4% of all appendectomy specimens. The etiology is unclear, although chronic inflammation, mucosal hyperplasia, and genetic alterations have been implicated. Risk increases with age and is slightly higher in women. Pathophysiologically, tumor development may arise from epithelial or neuroendocrine cells, leading to mucinous, nonmucinous, or mixed histologic patterns. Clinical presentation is frequently nonspecific, mimicking acute or chronic appendicitis, with symptoms including right lower quadrant pain, abdominal distention, or unexplained weight loss. Diagnosis relies on imaging modalities, such as ultrasound or computed tomography, and is confirmed by histopathologic evaluation. Management depends on tumor type and stage, ranging from appendectomy for localized lesions to right hemicolectomy or cytoreductive surgery with hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy for advanced disease. Complications include pseudomyxoma peritonei and metastatic spread. Prognosis varies according to histologic subtype and extent of dissemination. This activity for healthcare professionals is designed to sharpen learners' skills in evaluating and managing appendiceal tumors. Participants will deepen their understanding of the condition's etiology, risk factors, pathophysiology, clinical presentation, and current diagnostic and therapeutic recommendations. Strengthened proficiency will enable clinicians to collaborate with interprofessional teams caring for affected individuals.

courses.title: Brachytherapy, Skin Cancer
courses.description: Nonmelanoma skin cancers (NMSC) are the most common malignancies worldwide, with basal cell carcinoma and squamous cell carcinoma comprising the majority of cases. These tumors frequently develop on chronically sun-exposed areas of the head and neck, where delayed or inadequate treatment may result in substantial local tissue destruction, functional impairment, or cosmetic deformity. Surgical excision, particularly Mohs micrographic surgery, remains the standard of care for many lesions. However, a subset of patients are suboptimal surgical candidates because of advanced age, medical comorbidities, tumor location, prior surgeries, or concerns regarding functional or aesthetic outcomes. In these settings, radiation-based therapies serve as important alternatives, providing effective local control while preserving surrounding structures. External beam radiation and brachytherapy have emerged as valuable modalities for selected patients, offering high cure rates and favorable cosmetic results when appropriately applied. This activity equips clinicians with a comprehensive understanding of contemporary NMSC management, with a focused examination of the role of brachytherapy. Participants learn to evaluate indications and contraindications, compare brachytherapy with surgical and external beam approaches, and apply fundamental principles of treatment planning, dosing, and toxicity mitigation. Emphasis is placed on patient selection, management of acute and late adverse effects, and optimization of cosmetic outcomes. Collaboration within an interprofessional team, including dermatology, radiation oncology, medical physics, nursing, and pathology, enhances treatment precision, patient safety, and continuity of care. Coordinated decision-making supports individualized, patient-centered management strategies and improves clinical outcomes in cosmetically sensitive and high-risk disease contexts.

courses.title: Lipodermatosclerosis
courses.description: Lipodermatosclerosis, a chronic inflammatory disorder of the lower extremities, is characterized by subcutaneous fibrosis and skin induration. Lipodermatosclerosis is primarily associated with chronic venous insufficiency and venous hypertension and typically affects middle-aged and older adults. It is most common in women. The diagnosis is primarily clinical, but histological examination may be necessary for confirmation. Treatment of lipodermatosclerosis may include compression therapy, leg elevation, topical or intralesional corticosteroids, physical activity, weight reduction, or systemic therapy with anabolic steroids. Lipodermatosclerosis can progress to venous ulcers, and chronic pain is a common symptom. Lipodermatosclerosis is frequently chronic and recurrent, emphasizing the need for ongoing management. This activity reviews the risk factors, identification, evaluation, and management of lipodermatosclerosis and highlights the role of the multidisciplinary, interprofessional team in caring for patients with this chronic condition.

courses.title: Single-Anastomosis Duodeno-Ileal Bypass
courses.description: Single-anastomosis duodeno-ileal bypass (SADI), also referred to as single-anastomosis duodeno-ileostomy with sleeve gastrectomy, is a complex bariatric procedure designed for patients with severe obesity who require both restrictive and malabsorptive interventions to achieve significant and sustained weight loss. This procedure involves 2 primary components: a sleeve gastrectomy to reduce gastric volume and a single anastomosis between the duodenum and a distal loop of the ileum. By bypassing a large portion of the small intestine, SADI enhances metabolic improvements, supports diabetes remission, and yields superior or comparable outcomes to more traditional surgeries, such as Roux-en-Y gastric bypass or biliopancreatic diversion with duodenal switch. Despite its technical advantages, including reduced operative time and simplicity of a single anastomosis, SADI presents unique nutritional and surgical risks, requiring ongoing, lifelong management. Through this course, participants gain comprehensive knowledge of the SADI procedure, including surgical technique, patient selection criteria, and perioperative care protocols. The curriculum emphasizes evidence-based strategies to address common clinical challenges such as inconsistent patient selection and inadequate nutritional follow-up. Participants also refine their clinical decision-making skills through exposure to current data on outcomes, complications, and long-term metabolic effects. Collaborative training with interprofessional teams, including surgery, nursing, nutrition, behavioral health, and pharmacy, enables clinicians to deliver safer, more effective, and patient-centered bariatric care. This integrated approach enhances communication and coordination, ultimately improving surgical outcomes, minimizing postoperative complications, and supporting long-term success in managing obesity.

courses.title: Kidd Blood Group System
courses.description: The Kidd blood group system is a collection of glycoprotein antigens on the surface of red blood cells responsible for the urea transport and maintaining the osmolarity of red blood cells. This activity describes the role of the Kidd blood group system in improving the knowledge of clinicians, researchers, technicians, and other healthcare providers dealing with transfusion-related activities. This activity empowers healthcare professionals to understand the basic genetics of the SLC14A1 gene, the antigenic structure of the Kidd blood group system on the red cell membrane, and the urea transport function of Kidd glycoprotein. The Kidd blood group system has 3 major antigens Jka, Jkb, and Jk3. The antibodies against Kidd antigens are of the complement binding type and can lead to intravascular and extravascular hemolysis. This activity also discusses the clinical role of the Kidd blood group system in transfusion reactions, hemolytic disease of the fetus and newborn, transplantation, and bladder cancer treatment. The clinically significant antibodies against the Kidd blood group system can cause acute and delayed hemolytic transfusion reactions in fetuses and newborns after transfusion and hemolytic disease.

courses.title: Orbital Apex Syndrome
courses.description: Orbital syndromes include orbital apex, superior orbital fissure, and cavernous sinus syndrome. The orbital apex consists of the superior orbital fissure and the optic canal with its contents. The orbital apex syndrome is a complex multiple cranial nerve pathology that results from the involvement of the bony orbital apex. The causes of orbital apex syndrome include infectious, inflammatory, traumatic, iatrogenic, hormonal, and neoplastic pathologies. The patient may present with reduced or complete loss of vision with ophthalmoplegia which may be associated with pain. A multidisciplinary approach is required for accurate diagnosis, identifying the underlying cause, and managing this condition. This activity summarizes the anatomy of orbital apex and various etiologies resulting in orbital apex syndrome and describes the clinical evaluation, investigative modalities, and management of orbital apex syndrome.

courses.title: Bronchoalveolar Lavage
courses.description: Bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) is a diagnostic procedure used in pulmonary medicine to obtain a fluid sample from the lungs' bronchoalveolar spaces. During BAL, a bronchoscope is inserted into the airways, and a small amount of sterile saline is instilled and then suctioned back, collecting cells and other components for analysis. This technique is valuable in diagnosing various lung conditions, such as infections, interstitial lung diseases, and malignancies, providing clinicians with essential insights into the underlying pathology and guiding appropriate treatment strategies. By engaging in this continuing education activity, clinicians can understand bronchoalveolar lavage comprehensively, refining their expertise in performing and interpreting the procedure. This educational initiative may cover updated techniques, advancements in technology, and evidence-based practices related to BAL. Clinicians stand to enhance their proficiency in ensuring patient safety during the procedure, sharpen their skills in obtaining and analyzing BAL samples, and integrate the latest research findings into clinical decision-making. Furthermore, participation in this CME activity can foster a deeper appreciation for interdisciplinary collaboration, ultimately empowering clinicians to provide more informed, patient-centered care in pulmonary medicine.

courses.title: Carbon Disulfide Toxicity
courses.description: Carbon disulfide (CS2) is a volatile, colorless liquid commonly used in various industrial processes, including the production of rayon, rubber, cellophane, dyes, and pesticides. Although acute exposures to CS2 are relatively rare, chronic, low-level exposure poses a significant health concern, particularly among workers in factories and industries. CS2 toxicity can present with various nonspecific symptoms, ranging from respiratory and mucosal irritation to severe neurological, cardiovascular, renal, and reproductive complications. The subtle and progressive nature of chronic exposure often leads to delayed diagnosis and management. Evaluation of CS2 toxicity begins with a thorough exposure history, symptom assessment, and targeted physical examination, supported by diagnostic tests such as ECG, chest imaging, and laboratory studies to assess potential involvement of various organ systems. The treatment of CS2 toxicity is primarily supportive, focusing on symptom management, decontamination when appropriate, and monitoring for complications such as respiratory or neurological compromise; no specific antidote exists. This activity provides a comprehensive review of CS2 pathophysiology and toxicokinetics, highlights key diagnostic approaches, including symptom recognition and relevant laboratory testing, and outlines evidence-based strategies for both acute care and long-term monitoring. This activity is designed to enhance clinicians understanding of CS2 exposure, including its industrial applications, routes of absorption, clinical manifestations, and long-term health implications, while providing practical strategies for assessing, diagnosing, and managing CS2 toxicity across diverse clinical settings. Additionally, this activity highlights the importance of early identification, routine workplace screening, interprofessional collaboration, and public health education in mitigating exposure risks.

courses.title: Konno-Rastan Aortic Root Enlargement
courses.description: The Konno-Rastan procedure is used to enlarge the aortic root and subvalvular region, primarily in cases of aortic stenosis and complex left ventricular outflow tract obstruction. This condition often presents in those with pediatric or congenital heart disease where standard valve replacement is not feasible due to a small or hypoplastic aortic annulus. By making a longitudinal incision through the right coronary sinus and extending it into the right ventricular outflow tract and the muscular septum, the procedure effectively increases the diameter of the aortic root and alleviates the obstruction. This significantly reduces transvalvular pressure gradient and promotes favorable left ventricular remodeling, improving long-term cardiac function and overall outcomes. Through this educational activity, participants gain detailed knowledge of the Konno-Rastan procedure, including its indications, surgical steps, equipment, and potential complications. Learners enhance their ability to plan and execute complex aortic root enlargements and understand when adjunct procedures may be necessary. Emphasis is placed on interprofessional collaboration among cardiothoracic surgeons, anesthesiologists, perfusionists, cardiologists, nurses, and operating room staff to optimize surgical outcomes, ensure patient safety, and facilitate comprehensive perioperative care.

courses.title: Brachytherapy, Gallbladder Cancer
courses.description: Gallbladder cancer is a rare but aggressive malignancy with a poor prognosis due to late diagnosis. Risk factors include chronic inflammation, gallstones, primary sclerosing cholangitis, obesity, advanced age, and chronic infections. Symptoms often remain silent early on but may later present with jaundice, right upper quadrant pain, weight loss, and nausea. Diagnosis relies on imaging and histopathologic analysis, while treatment depends on staging, ranging from surgical resection to chemotherapy, radiotherapy, or palliative care. This course focuses on brachytherapy, a targeted radiotherapy option for unresectable or recurrent gallbladder cancer. Brachytherapy delivers high-dose radiation directly to tumors, minimizing damage to surrounding tissues. Learners explore its principles, indications, contraindications, and clinical applications, gaining insights into patient selection and treatment planning. The course also covers the diagnostic process, staging techniques, and multidisciplinary management strategies. This activity empowers healthcare professionals to collaborate effectively in the interprofessional care of gallbladder cancer patients, improving symptom control, disease management, and quality of life.

courses.title: Fluorides and Fluorocarbons Toxicity
courses.description: Fluorocarbons are fluorinated carbon chain polymers that are used in an assortment of household and commercial products as waterproofing agents, lubricants, sealants, and leather conditioners. These products have been implicated in sporadic outbreaks of respiratory illness characterized by dyspnea, cough, and chest pain. Though typically self-limited, more severe exposure may lead to respiratory failure, acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), and even death. Studies investigating the mechanism of fluoropolymer-related respiratory illness in humans have been difficult to perform for the following reasons: chemical formulation of these products is proprietary, chemical formulations are intermittently reformulated, product labels and safety data sheets (SDS) may not report fluorocarbon presence if present only in small amounts. This activity reviews the etiology, presentation, evaluation, and management/prevention of fluoride/fluorocarbon toxicity, and reviews the role of the interprofessional team in evaluating, diagnosing, and managing the condition.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Pit and Fissure Sealants
courses.description: Dental caries remain one of the most common chronic conditions, with pits and fissures on posterior teeth representing the most vulnerable sites due to their complex morphology, plaque-retentive nature, and reduced fluoride protection. Permanent first molars are particularly susceptible, as caries often develop soon after eruption. This activity reviews pit and fissure sealants, which provide an effective physical barrier that prevents food and bacterial accumulation, reducing the incidence of new lesions and arresting early noncavitated caries. Participants will also gain an in-depth understanding of the factors that can lead to the success of sealant therapy, including careful case selection, the appropriate choice of material, and proper application techniques, such as moisture control, etching, placement, and curing. This course explores the use of sealants for both primary and permanent dentition as well as the indications across age groups and patient populations, the relative benefits of resin-based versus glass ionomer sealants, and evidence-based strategies to maximize retention and long-term effectiveness. Clinicians will enhance their ability to assess caries risk, select the most suitable preventive approach, and apply sealants effectively under various clinical conditions. This activity for healthcare professionals is designed to enhance the learner's competence in the clinical application of pit and fissure sealants, preventing occlusal caries, performing recommended assessments and techniques, and implementing an appropriate interprofessional approach when managing patients undergoing these procedures to promote improved oral health outcomes.

courses.title: Ozone Toxicity
courses.description: Ozone normally occurs in a gas state as three oxygen atoms are linked in a cyclic structure. It is a by-product of water purification, bleaching, and any process generating a spark or electric arc in the presence of oxygen. It is also found in the atmosphere, with higher altitudes containing higher ozone levels. Ozone is also an environmental air pollutant, along with other pollutants such as sulfur dioxide and particulate matter. Despite this, ozone can be generated by medical devices for therapeutic purposes. Outside of medicine, ozone has been proposed for use in various settings, such as in the pretreatment of textile wastewater. While ozone can cause health troubles, it can also react with chemicals found in many products to lead to other potentially toxic substances, such as formaldehyde. Despite proponents for its use and its potential applications, toxicity can occur even at environmental levels and may be related to cardiac, respiratory, and neurologic events. This activity reviews the etiology, presentation, evaluation, and management/prevention of ozone toxicity and reviews the role of the interprofessional team in evaluating, diagnosing, and managing the condition.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Autoimmune Disease and Gonadal Failure
courses.description: Autoimmune gonadal failure significantly impacts fertility and requires accurate diagnosis for effective management. This activity explores the various autoimmune causes of gonadal failure in both males and females, emphasizing the importance of thoroughly evaluating and considering multiple differential diagnoses before developing a management plan. The etiologies include primary disorders and secondary rheumatologic and associated conditions. In addition, potential factors such as immune dysregulation and genetic and environmental contributors play a role in autoimmune gonadal failure. Given the rarity of autoimmune causes, their identification is crucial to prevent delays in treatment. The current data and the need for further field research are highlighted, which holds significant potential to improve diagnostic accuracy. This activity aims to guide medical professionals in accurately identifying and evaluating these cases, ensuring timely and appropriate management.

courses.title: Reinke Edema
courses.description: Reinke edema, or polypoid corditis, is a benign disorder of the vocal folds commonly resulting in symptomatic dysphonia that may result in dyspnea when severe. Reinke edema is most commonly secondary to cigarette smoking and is most prevalent in females. A thorough evaluation for other potential causes of dysphonia is critical to ensure no malignant diagnoses are missed. Treatment of Reinke edema is frequently multimodal, anchored on speech-language pathology, smoking cessation, and surgical management. Surgical management is dictated by the clinician's expertise and available equipment and may be office-based or performed in the operating room. This activity reviews the evaluation and management of Reinke edema and highlights the role of the interprofessional team in improving care for patients with this benign condition.

courses.title: Endosalpingiosis
courses.description: Endosalpingiosis refers to the presence of ectopic cystic glands lined with fallopian tube-like epithelium outside the fallopian tubes, most commonly in the pelvic region. This condition has been associated with pelvic pain, abnormal bleeding, and infertility, as well as other symptoms that can significantly affect a patient's quality of life. Endosalpingiosis has also been linked to gynecological malignancies, raising concerns about its potential role as a precursor to cancer. A rare subtype, florid cystic endosalpingiosis, presents with benign tumor-like lesions. Although initially confused with endometriosis, research has shown key histological differences. Diagnosis remains challenging, as there are no specific guidelines or imaging features, with confirmation requiring histological examination after surgery. Treatment is typically symptom-based, including medications such as oral contraceptives or GnRH agonists, and surgery for symptomatic cases. Given the potential association with ovarian and uterine cancer, clinicians should remain vigilant for malignancy and consider long-term follow-up for affected patients, as no formal treatment guidelines currently exist. This activity reviews the current research on endosalpingiosis, including its etiology, epidemiology, pathophysiology, histopathology, and other relevant information necessary for diagnosis and effective treatment. This activity explores current literature on the associations related to endosalpingiosis and enhances clinicians' ability to provide comprehensive patient care through effective collaboration with interprofessional healthcare team members in treating patients with this condition.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Photodynamic Therapy for Dermatologic Conditions
courses.description: Photodynamic therapy is a noninvasive and cosmetically favorable treatment option for a range of dermatologic conditions, including actinic keratoses, superficial basal cell carcinoma, and Bowen disease. This therapy is particularly effective in managing field cancerization and offers advantages in patients with multiple lesions or contraindications to surgery. However, despite its clinical utility, photodynamic therapy remains underutilized in many settings due to persistent knowledge and implementation gaps among healthcare providers. Many clinicians lack familiarity with appropriate patient selection, protocol variations based on lesion type and location, and management of procedure-related discomfort or adverse effects. Training in photodynamic therapy is often limited during residency, and many practitioners have little exposure to its use in clinical practice. Additionally, uncertainty surrounding contraindications such as photosensitivity disorders or specific medication use and logistical concerns with light source availability and reimbursement create further barriers to adoption. This activity aims to bridge this gap by enhancing healthcare providers' competence in selecting appropriate candidates, applying evidence-based treatment protocols, and managing photodynamic therapy associated adverse effects. By improving healthcare providers' confidence and standardizing clinical use, this activity seeks to expand access to photodynamic therapy, optimize therapeutic outcomes, and ensure this valuable treatment modality is more consistently integrated into dermatologic care.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Respiratory Syncytial Virus Prefusion F (RSVPreF3) Vaccine
courses.description: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a prevalent respiratory pathogen that primarily affects infants, young children, older adults, and individuals with compromised immune systems. RSV is a significant cause of acute respiratory infection, lower respiratory tract disease (LRTD), clinical complications, and death in infants and older adults. The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved the first vaccines against RSV in 2023. The recombinant subunit RSV prefusion F3 (RSVPreF3) vaccine contains the RSV F glycoprotein stabilized in its prefusion (pre-F) state. By targeting the pre-F glycoprotein, the vaccine stimulates the production of neutralizing antibodies, activates both humoral and cellular immune responses, and promotes the formation of memory B and T cells. This activity provides comprehensive information on the indications, administration, dosage recommendations, mechanism of action, monitoring, adverse reactions, precautions, and contraindications associated with RSVPreF3 vaccines. This activity empowers healthcare teams to identify patients at high risk of severe RSV infection outcomes and to recommend and administer the RSVPreF3 vaccine according to nationally accepted guidelines.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Musculoskeletal Amyloidosis Imaging
courses.description: Amyloidosis is a rare disease involving the accumulation of insoluble proteins within various tissue types, ultimately leading to end-organ failure. The clinical characteristics and radiologic features of amyloidosis depend on the subtype of amyloid protein, the involved tissues, and whether amyloid deposition represents a primary or secondary disease process. While there are around 40 identified protein subtypes of amyloidosis, the most common amyloid subtypes that involve the musculoskeletal system include the immunoglobulin light chain (AL), the beta-2 microglobulin (AB2M), and the transthyretin (ATTR) proteins--the latter having genetic and senescent variants. While certain primary disease states predispose to amyloidosis, the prognosis remains poor due to delays in prompt diagnosis and treatment. This activity illustrates the key radiologic features of musculoskeletal amyloidosis and the role of radiology in reducing diagnostic uncertainty in managing patients with this condition.

courses.title: Mohs Micrographic Surgery Guidelines of Care and Staging Systems for Melanoma
courses.description: Mohs micrographic surgery is increasingly being used in the management of melanoma, particularly melanoma in situ and thin invasive melanoma occurring in anatomically and cosmetically sensitive areas. Advances in immunohistochemical staining, margin assessment, and surgical techniques have expanded the role of Mohs micrographic surgery beyond traditional treatment of nonmelanoma skin cancers. Clinicians must understand the current evidence, evolving guideline recommendations, patient selection criteria, and the limitations associated with Mohs surgery for melanoma, including challenges in frozen-section interpretation, upstaging risk, and coordination of sentinel lymph node biopsy. This activity reviews melanoma epidemiology, staging, surgical margins, and the comparative outcomes of Mohs micrographic surgery versus wide local excision. Participants will gain knowledge of current NCCN and dermatologic surgery recommendations, immunohistochemical applications, recurrence data, and multidisciplinary considerations necessary to optimize melanoma treatment planning and patient outcomes.

courses.title: Toluene Toxicity
courses.description: Toluene, or toluol, is an aromatic hydrocarbon used as a solvent in producing gasoline, glue, paint, paint thinners, and cleaning solutions, amongst other products. The hydrocarbon is preferred over benzene, which has significant toxicity and carcinogenicity associated with exposure. Although less toxic than benzene, toluene is not without its risks. In addition to long-term exposure risks, toluene is also abused and misused owing to its ability to induce euphoria and central nervous system depression. Chronic exposure to levels above the recommended limit can produce metabolic acidosis, electrolyte abnormalities, cognitive impairment due to cerebellar ataxia or atrophy, ventricular enlargement, and white matter abnormalities. This activity reviews the etiology, toxicokinetics, evaluation, and treatment of toluene toxicity and highlights the role of the interprofessional team in managing and improving care for patients with this condition.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Tapinarof
courses.description: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved tapinarof in May 2022 to treat plaque psoriasis in adults aged 18 and older. Tapinarof is a nonsteroidal, topical treatment that belongs to the unique class of naturally derived aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR) agonists, distinguishing it as the first agent of its kind and differentiating it from steroid-based treatments. Plaque psoriasis, a chronic immune-mediated disease, represents the most common subtype of psoriasis. This activity provides a comprehensive review of tapinarof, covering its indications, mechanisms of action, and administration as an effective agent for managing plaque psoriasis are discussed. In addition, the activity delves into off-label uses of tapinarof, such as for treating atopic dermatitis. Various aspects of tapinarof therapy, including possible adverse effects, monitoring, and potential contraindications. All interprofessional healthcare team members should be aware of this information and possess a general understanding of tapinarof, as it is crucial for treating adults with plaque psoriasis.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Steatocystoma
courses.description: Steatocystomas are benign dermatological cystic lesions that arise from the pilosebaceous unit and are true sebaceous cysts characterized by the presence of sebaceous glands within the cyst wall. These lesions can present as single nodules (steatocystoma simplex) or multiple lesions (steatocystoma multiplex), often appearing as smooth, round, mobile nodules on the chest, axillae, or groin. These cysts range from a few millimeters to about a centimeter in size and release an odorless, oily fluid if punctured. If these cysts are punctured, they release an oily, fluid-like substance. Although generally asymptomatic, they often pose aesthetic concerns rather than significant health risks. Steatocystoma multiplex is often associated with genetic mutations following an autosomal-dominant inheritance pattern. Steatocystomas may occur with comorbid conditions, such as pachyonychia congenita. Although most cases are sporadic, familial forms or links to other congenital abnormalities should prompt a detailed family history and possible genetic testing. Diagnosis relies on clinical evaluation, dermoscopy, and histopathological confirmation. Treatment is typically unnecessary but may be initiated for cosmetic reasons or diagnostic clarity. Management approaches include medical or surgical therapies. Newer techniques have shown promising cosmetic outcomes for multiple lesions. This activity for healthcare professionals is designed to enhance the learner's competence in recognizing the clinical features of steatocystomas, performing the recommended evaluation, assessing differential diagnoses, and implementing an appropriate interprofessional management approach to improve patient outcomes.

courses.title: Osteonecrosis Imaging
courses.description: Osteonecrosis refers to the ischemic death of elements of a bone caused by compromised vascular integrity, such as loss of blood supply to a region of bone. This condition is a common pathology with diverse etiologies and can affect nearly any bone in the body. The most common etiologies are chronic corticosteroid use, alcoholism, trauma, and idiopathic factors. Timely and accurate identification of osteonecrosis changes through imaging is crucial to prevent irreversible joint damage. Magnetic resonance imaging is the most sensitive imaging modality as it can demonstrate early osseous changes that may be present before plain radiographic changes are visible. Integrated models incorporating clinical and imaging findings have been developed to aid healthcare professionals in understanding, diagnosing, and stratifying the risk of potential subchondral collapse and the benefits of prompt and appropriate treatment to improve patient outcomes in this important, potentially debilitating, yet prevalent condition. This activity enhances clinicians' understanding and proficiency in diagnosing and managing osteonecrosis through advanced imaging techniques. In addition, this activity comprehensively covers various imaging modalities available, including x-rays, computed tomography scans, magnetic resonance imaging, and nuclear medicine studies, highlighting their specific applications and sensitivities at various disease stages. By providing this knowledge, healthcare professionals are equipped to ensure timely diagnosis, mitigate complications, and optimize patient outcomes.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Platinum Hypersensitivity and Toxicity
courses.description: Platinum-based chemotherapeutic agents have revolutionized oncology practice since the accidental discovery of cisplatin's antineoplastic activity by Barnett Rosenberg in 1965 and its subsequent clinical use in the 1970s. Cisplatin, carboplatin, and oxaliplatin have become vital therapeutic options for several types of solid tumors, such as ovarian, testicular, lung, head and neck, gastrointestinal, and bladder cancers. To date, platinum compounds continue to play a central role in oncology practice, with approximately 40% to 80% of patients with cancer undergoing chemotherapy exposed to these compounds. However, the clinical utility of platinum compounds is significantly limited by 2 limitations hypersensitivity reactions and dose-limiting organ toxicities. These dose-limiting organ toxicities affect nearly all major body systems, particularly the renal, neurologic, and hematologic systems. These adverse events negatively impact a patient's quality of life and often force clinicians to decrease the dose, prolong treatment duration, or switch therapies, which may reduce treatment efficiency. Hypersensitivity reactions to platinum compounds have been observed to affect a variable number of patients. Various factors may influence the occurrence of the hypersensitivity reaction, including the type of platinum compound, the cumulative dose, previous allergic reactions to medication, and possibly genetic factors.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Catheter Management of Mitral Regurgitation
courses.description: Mitral regurgitation (MR) is a prevalent valvular abnormality, often requiring medical management or invasive surgery for severe cases. However, recent studies highlight the increased utilization of a minimally invasive transcatheter approach, particularly the edge-to-edge leaflet repair device. This catheter-based therapy employs a clip to combine the mitral valve leaflets, effectively reducing regurgitation. The activity explores primary and secondary MR, providing insights into noninvasive catheter management options, indications, contraindications, procedural techniques, and potential complications. Emphasizing the role of interprofessional teams in patient care, the activity offers a comprehensive understanding of catheter-based therapies for MR. Clinicians engaging in this activity gain in-depth knowledge of primary and secondary MR, its categorization, and appropriate treatment choices based on disease duration and severity. The activity explores the nuances of echocardiography, emphasizing the significance of transthoracic and transesophageal imaging modalities in evaluating mitral valve morphology and pathology. Specifically, focusing on the edge-to-edge leaflet repair device gives clinicians a nuanced understanding of minimally invasive, catheter-based approaches. Clinicians enhance their expertise in managing MR by comprehensively exploring indications, procedural techniques, and complications associated with noninvasive catheter interventions. Emphasis is placed on interprofessional collaboration, as it provides a holistic understanding of catheter-based therapies for MR, including indications and contraindications.

courses.title: Thrombotic Microangiopathy and the Kidney
courses.description: Thrombotic microangiopathy (TMA) is a clinicopathological condition characterized by microangiopathic hemolytic anemia, thrombocytopenia, and schistocytes on a blood smear, often accompanied by end-organ damage. This condition results from endothelial injury and microthrombi formation in the microvasculature, leading to ischemic damage with the kidneys being particularly vulnerable. TMA can be limited to the kidneys or involve multiple organ systems, complicating diagnosis and management. Early identification of the underlying etiology and swift intervention are critical to improving patient outcomes. This educational activity equips healthcare professionals with the knowledge to classify TMA, recognize its pathophysiology, and interpret key histopathological findings in the kidney. Participants gain skills in timely diagnosis, appropriate therapeutic interventions, and effective application of evidence-based strategies. The course also emphasizes the importance of interdisciplinary collaboration among hematologists, nephrologists, clinical pharmacists, and other healthcare professionals. This team-based approach ensures accurate evaluation, rapid intervention, and better care coordination, ultimately improving patient outcomes.

courses.title: Atorvastatin
courses.description: HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors (statins) are lipid-lowering medications used in the primary, secondary, and tertiary prevention of coronary heart disease. Atorvastatin is a medication primarily used to manage and treat dyslipidemias and prevent cardiovascular disease. This activity focuses on the indications, mechanism of action, and contraindications of atorvastatin as a valuable agent in managing these conditions. The activity reviews the warnings, adverse event profile, toxicity, and key considerations, including monitoring and relevant drug interactions. Understanding the intricate pharmacology of atorvastatin enables healthcare professionals to tailor treatment plans to individual patient needs. Notably, the emphasis lies on empowering healthcare professionals, highlighting the essential role of the interprofessional healthcare team in managing atorvastatin therapy for hyperlipidemia and reducing cardiovascular risk. This activity aims to equip healthcare professionals with the essential knowledge and tools necessary for delivering excellent patient care during atorvastatin administration, thereby advancing patient outcomes and care standards. A comprehensive understanding of atorvastatin equips healthcare professionals with a scientific foundation for the practical management of dyslipidemias and related cardiovascular conditions. This knowledge allows informed decision-making in prescribing atorvastatin and optimizing dosage regimens while minimizing adverse reactions. Overall, this activity enables healthcare professionals to deliver targeted, safe, and personalized care, enhancing patient outcomes related to atorvastatin.

courses.title: Pediatric Autoimmune Neuropsychiatric Disorders Associated With Streptococcal Infections (PANDAS)
courses.description: Pediatric autoimmune neuropsychiatric disorders associated with streptococcal infections (PANDAS) and the broader category of pediatric acute-onset neuropsychiatric syndromes (PANS) involve the abrupt onset of severe neuropsychiatric symptoms in children, often triggered by infections like streptococcal pharyngitis. These conditions manifest with a range of behavioral and neurological symptoms, including obsessive-compulsive behaviors, tics, anxiety, emotional instability, motor skill deterioration, and sleep disturbances. The classification of PANDAS as a distinct clinical entity remains controversial, with some experts proposing it as a variant of Sydenham chorea due to overlapping clinical features and genetic predispositions. Diagnosis is primarily clinical, relying on specific criteria such as the sudden onset of symptoms, association with streptococcal infection, and episodic symptom course, making it a diagnosis of exclusion. In this educational activity, healthcare professionals enhance their understanding of the epidemiology, neuropathophysiology, diagnosis, and treatment of PANDAS, providing them with the skills needed to provide optimal care for affected patients. Participants learn to recognize the complex presentation of PANDAS, differentiate it from other neuropsychiatric disorders, and implement comprehensive diagnostic evaluations, including psychoneurological assessments and infectious disease testing. Collaborating within an interprofessional team, including pediatricians, neurologists, psychiatrists, and infectious disease specialists, is emphasized to ensure timely diagnosis and effective treatment.

courses.title: Mohs Micrographic Surgery: Chemotherapeutic Agents Used in Cutaneous Oncology
courses.description: Skin cancer, including both nonmelanoma skin cancer and melanoma, continues to rise in incidence and remains the most common malignancy in patients. In dermatological practice, topical and intralesional chemotherapeutic agents are commonly used. For patients with advanced disease or those ineligible for other treatment modalities, systemic chemotherapy remains a therapeutic option. Mohs surgeons are encouraged to be familiar with nonsurgical treatment approaches, particularly for managing complex or residual tumors. Although surgery remains the gold standard for treating skin cancers, chemotherapy administered topically, intralesionally, or systemically may be a viable alternative for patients with advanced disease or those who are not candidates for or cannot tolerate surgery, immunotherapy, or targeted therapies. This activity provides a comprehensive review of available chemotherapeutic agents and their delivery methods, focusing on their role in treating nonmelanoma skin cancers, including basal cell carcinoma, squamous cell carcinoma, melanoma, and Merkel cell carcinoma. This activity also outlines the use of US Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-approved chemotherapeutic agents, their mechanisms of action, and the clinical trial evidence supporting their efficacy. Additionally, this activity provides healthcare professionals with the knowledge and tools necessary to support informed treatment decisions and enhance patient care. In addition, this topic emphasizes the importance of collaboration among healthcare providers to optimize treatment decisions and improve patient outcomes when delivering topical, intralesional, or systemic chemotherapy for patients with skin cancer.

courses.title: Electrophysiologic Study Interpretation
courses.description: Electrophysiologic study (EPS) interpretation is critical in diagnosing and managing complex cardiac arrhythmias. EPS involves using intracardiac catheters to assess electrical conduction, identify arrhythmia mechanisms, and guide therapeutic interventions such as catheter ablation or device implantation. Accurate interpretation requires an in-depth understanding of electrogram patterns, pacing maneuvers, and conduction system physiology. A specialized interprofessional team including electrophysiologists, cardiologists, nurses, and technicians must collaborate to ensure precise data collection, patient safety, and optimal treatment planning. Proper interpretation of EPS findings is essential for tailoring individualized management strategies for acute and chronic arrhythmia patients. This course provides clinicians with the necessary skills to interpret EPS data accurately, recognize conduction abnormalities, and apply findings to clinical decision-making. The course emphasizes interprofessional communication and teamwork, enhancing coordination among physicians, nurses, and allied health professionals involved in electrophysiology procedures. By the end of the course, clinicians will improve their proficiency in EPS interpretation, leading to more precise diagnoses, better patient outcomes, and safer, more effective arrhythmia management.

courses.title: Bioprosthetic Aortic Valve Replacement
courses.description: Bioprosthetic aortic valve replacement is a well-established treatment for severe aortic stenosis, aortic regurgitation, and selected cases of infective endocarditis requiring valve replacement. Advances in prosthetic valve design, perioperative management, and patient selection have expanded the role of bioprosthetic valves, particularly among older adults and patients wishing to avoid lifelong anticoagulation. Successful outcomes require a thorough understanding of valve pathology, indications for intervention, preoperative evaluation, operative techniques, postoperative management, and potential complications, as well as appropriate prosthesis selection based on patient-specific factors. This activity reviews the anatomy, indications, contraindications, surgical principles, perioperative care, and long-term outcomes associated with bioprosthetic aortic valve replacement. Upon completion, clinicians will be better equipped to select appropriate candidates, optimize perioperative management, recognize and manage complications, and collaborate effectively within the multidisciplinary heart team to improve patient outcomes.

courses.title: Acute Coronary Syndrome Catheter Interventions
courses.description: Acute Coronary Syndrome (ACS) catheter interventions, primarily percutaneous coronary intervention, are life-saving procedures aimed at restoring coronary blood flow in patients with unstable angina and myocardial infarctions. These interventions involve mechanical revascularization through balloon angioplasty and stent placement to alleviate myocardial ischemia and prevent infarct progression. Rapid diagnosis, prompt reperfusion, and evidence-based pharmacologic support such as antiplatelet and anticoagulant therapy are essential for optimizing outcomes. The success of these interventions relies on a coordinated, multidisciplinary approach involving cardiologists, nurses, advanced clinicians, and pharmacists to ensure patient safety, minimize complications, and promote long-term cardiovascular health. Clinicians participating in this course deepen their understanding of the pathophysiology, indications, and procedural techniques associated with ACS catheter interventions. They gain practical insights into pre-, intra-, and postprocedural management, including hemodynamic monitoring, medication optimization, and prevention of complications such as stent thrombosis or bleeding. The course emphasizes interprofessional collaboration, evidence-based decision-making, and patient education strategies to enhance care coordination and outcomes. By mastering these competencies, participants enhance their ability to deliver high-quality, patient-centered cardiovascular care, ultimately improving survival and recovery rates in patients with acute coronary syndromes.

courses.title: Chondroid Syringoma
courses.description: Chondroid syringoma is a rare, benign adnexal skin tumor, also known as a mixed tumor, due to its epithelial and mesenchymal components. The epithelial portion typically involves eccrine or apocrine sweat glands, while the mesenchymal part consists of myxoid or chondroid stroma. Clinically, it presents as a slow-growing, painless nodule commonly found on the head or neck of adult men. Diagnosis is confirmed via histopathology, and treatment is primarily surgical excision. Though usually benign, there is a rare malignant variant of chondroid syringoma that presents aggressively, particularly on the lower extremities. Participants in this activity learn how to improve diagnostic accuracy by recognizing chondroid syringoma's clinical and histological features, enabling timely and appropriate treatment. The course emphasizes distinguishing between benign and malignant mixed tumors, particularly when evaluating nodules in cosmetically sensitive areas. Collaboration with an interprofessional team ensures early diagnosis and effective management, improving patient outcomes and reducing morbidity.

courses.title: New Onset Diabetes After Transplant
courses.description: New-onset diabetes mellitus after transplantation (NODAT) is the development of diabetes mellitus after solid organ transplantation. NODAT frequently occurs, increasing the risk of infection as well as mortality rates. The appropriate evaluation and management of NODAT by the health care providers result in prompt diagnosis with a subsequent decrease in morbidity and mortality associated with this condition and increases the organ survival after a transplant. This activity describes the pathophysiology, evaluation, and management of NODAT and highlights the role of the interprofessional team in caring for affected patients.

courses.title: The Emerging Role of Bariatric Surgery in the Management of Nonalcoholic Fatty Liver Disease
courses.description: Nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) is a spectrum of disease characterized by excess fat accumulation in hepatocytes in the absence of secondary causes such as alcohol use. As excess fat deposits in the liver, hepatosteatosis may progress to nonalcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH). While the frequency of progression of NASH to cirrhosis is low, NASH is considered a significant risk factor for the development of cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma. Risk factors for developing NAFLD include central obesity, insulin resistance, type 2 diabetes, metabolic syndrome, dyslipidemia, and hypertension. The prevalence of NAFLD has increased, mirroring the rise in obesity. The primary treatment of NAFLD is weight loss via exercise and diet modifications. There are currently no approved pharmacotherapeutics for NAFLD. However, a potential treatment option for NAFLD is bariatric weight loss surgery. This activity reviews the epidemiology, pathophysiology, clinical findings, and diagnostic evaluation of NAFLD in patients who may benefit from bariatric surgery. The activity also highlights the role of the interprofessional team caring for patients with obesity and NAFLD.

courses.title: Prevention of Surgical Errors
courses.description: A surgical error is an unintentional, preventable injury that occurs during the perioperative period, is not considered a known acceptable risk of surgery, and could have been avoided by following appropriate procedure-specific training protocols. Surgical errors are a type of medical error and include retained foreign bodies, mislabeled surgical specimens, and wrong-site, wrong-procedure, and wrong-patient errors (WSPEs). An analysis of these errors over the last few decades has revealed that their causes are often multifactorial. However, miscommunication, unnecessary or emergent procedures, insufficient training, and provider burnout represent common causes of surgical error. Surgical errors can be potentially catastrophic, carry a significant financial burden, and are likely under-reported. Several organizations have developed strategies to determine why these errors occur and how to mitigate the incidence. The Joint Commission is one example of an organization that has developed a universal protocol to help monitor and decrease surgical errors. This activity reviews surgical errors and effective interprofessional team approaches to create a culture of safety that reduces surgical errors and improves patient outcomes.

courses.title: Congenital Femoral Deficiency
courses.description: Congenital femoral deficiency (CFD) is a complex condition encompassing a spectrum of femoral anatomical disorders, ranging from congenital short femur to severe proximal focal femoral deficiencies. Patients with CFD typically experience compromised hip joint stability and mobility, accompanied by joint malorientation and soft tissue contractures. The affected limb's growth is hindered, with the inhibition rate varying based on the underlying condition's severity. Notably, CFD is often associated with a myriad of skeletal abnormalities, with fibular hemimelia being the most common. Associated conditions include caudal regression syndrome, caudal dysplasia, cruciate ligament deficiency, and lumbosacral spine deformities. This activity for healthcare professionals is designed to enhance learner's competence in evaluating and managing CFD. Participating clinicians gain comprehensive insights into CFD's clinical presentations, characterized by coxa vara proximally and femoral valgus distally. A deeper understanding of the latest research findings and clinical approaches enables participants to collaborate effectively within an interprofessional team, providing optimal care for affected patients.

courses.title: Hypereosinophilic Syndrome
courses.description: Hypereosinophilic Syndrome (HES) is a rare and complex group of disorders posing diagnostic challenges for clinicians. Characterized by significant increases in eosinophil levels, HES can lead to tissue infiltration and damage. This course is designed to equip clinicians with a comprehensive understanding of the epidemiology, evaluation, and management of HES, offering valuable insights to enhance patient care. Throughout the course, participants will explore the diagnostic criteria for HES, emphasizing the importance of eosinophil counts, evidence of organ or tissue damage, and the exclusion of alternative causes. Delving into the prevalence rates and demographic patterns, learners will focus on the age group most commonly affected and the prevalence rate ranging from 0.36 to 6.3 per 100,000. Moreover, the course will provide a nuanced classification of HES variants based on the affected organ and initial patient evaluation. This interprofessional learning experience encourages collaboration among team members, fostering a holistic approach to HES. Participants will gain the expertise required to enhance patient outcomes by exploring the intricacies of epidemiology and diagnosis.

courses.title: Aluminum Toxicity
courses.description: Aluminum toxicity was previously common in dialysis patients due to elevated levels in dialysate, but it has become rare with improvements in the dialysate composition. Patients with end-stage renal disease are particularly susceptible, as aluminum relies on renal clearance and was historically present in some phosphate binders. Aluminum exposure occurs through cosmetics, food packaging, medications, water, and industrial sources. Although it was initially believed to primarily affect the nervous system and bones, aluminum toxicity is now known to impact the cardiac, pulmonary, reproductive, gastrointestinal, and hematological systems. Symptoms include anemia, pulmonary fibrosis, and decreased bone density. Diagnosis of this condition involves measuring aluminum levels in biological specimens using various advanced techniques. Treatment focuses on chelation therapy with deferoxamine, which binds aluminum for excretion, often requiring dialysis in patients with renal insufficiency. Other chelators exist, but deferoxamine remains the most effective. Early recognition, intervention, and prevention have transformed aluminum poisoning into a manageable condition with a favorable prognosis. This activity explores the current scientific understanding of aluminum poisoning, covering exposure sources, at-risk populations, organ-specific toxicology, treatment, and prevention to provide healthcare professionals with the ability to manage aluminum toxicity.

courses.title: Fetal Echogenic Bowel
courses.description: Fetal echogenic bowel (FEB) is defined as increased echogenicity, appearing as unusual brightness, of the fetal bowel, which is noted on the prenatal ultrasound. In the third trimester, this can be a normal finding, representing meconium in the bowel, but its detection in the second trimester can be associated with a range of conditions, including chromosomal abnormalities, congenital infections, cystic fibrosis, and intrauterine growth restriction. Due to its varied clinical implications, the detection of echogenic bowel warrants a thorough and systematic evaluation to guide further diagnostic testing and management. This activity reviews the incidence, pathophysiology, and outcomes associated with FEB, highlighting the role of the interprofessional team in investigating and managing pregnancies with this finding in the second trimester. Participants will gain an understanding of current guidelines, evidence-based approaches, and diagnostic pathways for assessing FEB prenatally and optimizing clinical outcomes.

courses.title: Asthma and COPD Overlap
courses.description: Asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) are the most common obstructive lung diseases observed during clinical practice. They have common characteristics and similar clinical presentation. Moreover, they usually have the same presentation on pulmonary function tests (PFT). Asthma and COPD overlap is a term to describe the patients who present with both asthma and COPD symptoms. This activity illustrates the clinical characteristics, diagnosis, and treatment of asthma-COPD overlap.

courses.title: Chloroform Toxicity
courses.description: Chloroform is a colorless liquid that has been used as an anesthetic historically and is still used in various industrial applications. The toxicity risks of the compound result from occupational exposures and intentional ingestion, which presents a significant concern for healthcare professionals. Due to its rapid absorption through inhalation, ingestion, and dermal contact, chloroform is considered hazardous. Upon entry into the body, chloroform rapidly affects the major organ systems, causing sedation and potentially damaging the liver and kidneys. While its usage has declined, chloroform remains regulated due to its harmful potential. This activity reviews the pathophysiology, clinical manifestations, and management strategies pertinent to chloroform exposure, as well as the adverse effects of chloroform toxicity. This activity also emphasizes vigilant history-taking and physical examinations of patients, guiding management and allowing healthcare providers to mitigate risks associated with this volatile organic compound more effectively.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Cobalt Toxicity
courses.description: Cobalt toxicity is an uncommon but potentially serious condition resulting from excessive exposure to cobalt, an essential trace element and a structural component of cobalamin (vitamin B12). Although cobalt is required for normal erythropoiesis and neurologic function, elevated levels, particularly from inorganic forms, can produce multisystem toxicity. Acute exposure is rare and most often related to excessive supplementation or accidental ingestion, whereas chronic toxicity more commonly occurs through occupational exposure in mining, metal processing, battery manufacturing, or from wear and failure of metal-on-metal hip prostheses. Pathophysiological mechanisms include mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, and disruption of calcium homeostasis, which together lead to cellular injury. Clinical manifestations vary based on exposure duration and dose and may include cardiomyopathy, peripheral neuropathy, sensorineural hearing loss, visual impairment, hypothyroidism, and polycythemia. Diagnosis depends on a thorough exposure history, measurement of serum or whole-blood cobalt levels, and targeted evaluation of affected organ systems. This activity for healthcare professionals is designed to enhance clinicians' competence in recognizing, evaluating, and managing cobalt toxicity. Participants strengthen their understanding of exposure sources, toxicokinetics, and multisystem clinical manifestations to support earlier diagnosis and intervention. The course reviews evidence-based diagnostic strategies, interpretation of cobalt levels, and management approaches, including exposure cessation, supportive care, and prosthesis revision when indicated. Emphasis is placed on coordinated care involving occupational medicine, cardiology, neurology, endocrinology, orthopedics, and toxicology. Effective interprofessional collaboration and communication are highlighted as critical to minimizing irreversible organ damage, optimizing treatment decisions, and improving patient.

courses.title: Plant Alkaloids Toxicity
courses.description: Plant alkaloids constitute a diverse group of compounds widely distributed in nature and increasingly encountered in households through indoor plants. Pharmacognosy has demonstrated the substantial therapeutic potential of these substances, though they are also the primary toxic components of many poisonous plants. Humans and animals may be exposed to these phytotoxins with harmful effects. Clinical manifestations range from nonspecific symptoms to classic toxidromes. Prognosis is generally favorable in mild exposures, although significant ingestions may result in severe complications and, in rare cases, mortality. This activity for healthcare professionals is designed to sharpen learners' skills in evaluating and managing plant alkaloid toxicity. Participants will deepen their understanding of the condition's etiology, risk factors, pathophysiology, clinical presentation, and evidence-based diagnostic and therapeutic recommendations. Enhanced competence will empower clinicians to collaborate with interprofessional teams caring for affected individuals.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Bazedoxifene
courses.description: Bazedoxifene is a selective estrogen receptor modulator used to manage osteoporosis in postmenopausal women. Osteoporosis is characterized by the gradual decline in overall bone density that exposes patients to an increased risk of proximal fractures. Approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) as a combination drug alongside conjugated estrogens, bazedoxifene is crucial in addressing vasomotor symptoms associated with menopause and preventing postmenopausal osteoporosis. This activity explores the approved indications, mechanisms of action, proper administration, potential adverse events, and contraindications of bazedoxifene. Participants gain insights to deliver optimal care to high-risk women with osteoporosis and associated menopausal symptoms, especially in cases where conventional therapies are contraindicated.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Small Interfering RNA (siRNA) Therapy
courses.description: This activity focuses on small interfering RNA (siRNA) therapy, exemplified by FDA-approved agents such as patisiran, givosiran, lumasiran, inclisiran, nedosiran, and vutrisiran. These therapies are pivotal in managing rare metabolic ailments, including hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis (hATTR), acute hepatic porphyria (AHP), primary hyperoxaluria type 1 (PH1), and lowering low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) in subjects with heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HeFH) or clinical atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD). The activity will discuss the mechanism of action of siRNA, its adverse event profile, and other key factors essential for interprofessional team members involved in patient care. Furthermore, participants will gain insights into administration techniques, contraindications, clinical toxicology, and monitoring strategies necessary to safely and effectively utilize siRNA therapies in clinical practice. Understanding the intricate pharmacology of siRNA is crucial for healthcare professionals to deliver precise therapeutic interventions in various clinical scenarios. This activity equips participants with comprehensive knowledge encompassing the mechanism of action, potential adverse reactions, and contraindications, empowering them to integrate advanced therapeutic strategies into patient care. This comprehension ensures that professionals possess the requisite expertise to provide optimal and innovative patient care within the dynamic realm of medical science, thereby enhancing patient outcomes and contributing to the advancement of medical practice.

courses.title: Mohs Micrographic Surgery: Chemoprophylaxis Options for Nicotinamide and Oral Retinoids
courses.description: Mohs surgeons should be knowledgeable in both nonsurgical treatments for nonmelanoma skin cancers (NMSCs) and preventive strategies for high-risk patients. Individuals with immunosuppression, extensive sun exposure, or genetic predispositions may benefit from chemoprophylaxis to reduce morbidity, mortality, and healthcare costs associated with NMSCs, particularly basal cell carcinoma (BCC) and squamous cell carcinoma (SCC). Nicotinamide and oral retinoids are medications used in NMSC prophylaxis. Nicotinamide and retinoids are derivatives of vitamin B3 and vitamin A, respectively. These agents can cause systemic adverse effects, including teratogenicity, mucocutaneous dryness, hepatotoxicity, and mood disturbances. Careful monitoring and patient counseling are essential. For patients unable to tolerate systemic agents, alternative chemoprophylactic options include topical therapies (eg, 5-fluorouracil, imiquimod) and photodynamic therapy. Coordination with transplant teams may be necessary, as modifying immunosuppressive regimens can also reduce skin cancer risk. This activity reviews the benefits, limitations, and risks of each agent, allowing Mohs surgeons to individualize treatment and improve patient outcomes. This activity for healthcare professionals is designed to enhance the learner's competence in identifying the indications, mechanisms of action, contraindications, and adverse event profiles for nicotinamide and oral retinoids as chemoprophylactic agents for nonmelanoma skin cancer and implementing an appropriate interprofessional approach when administering these therapies.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Bempedoic Acid
courses.description: Bempedoic acid is a lipid-lowering agent pivotal in managing patients with elevated low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) levels. The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has sanctioned its use as an adjunct to maximally tolerated statin therapy for the reduction of LDL-C, specifically in individuals afflicted by atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) and heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HeFH). Bempedoic acid is also a viable alternative for patients intolerant to statins. This program discusses the drug's indications, mechanism of action, administration modalities, significant adverse effects, contraindications, and monitoring protocols. The program also addresses monitoring strategies, pharmacokinetic nuances, and associated warnings and precautions. Healthcare providers can adeptly guide patient therapy and manage hyperlipidemia with this knowledge. A thorough understanding of bempedoic acid's intricate pharmacology empowers healthcare professionals to tailor treatment plans based on individual patient requirements. This enables informed decision-making in prescribing, optimizing dosage regimens, and mitigating potential adverse reactions. This activity equips healthcare professionals to deliver evidence-based care to improve outcomes for patients with hypercholesterolemia.

courses.title: Hoffa Pad Impingement Syndrome
courses.description: Hoffa pad impingement syndrome, also known as Hoffa disease, fat pad impingement, and infrapatellar fat pad (IFP) syndrome, is a painful impingement of the IFP between the patella and distal femoral condyle. The diseased fat pad is characterized by inflammation, swelling, hypertrophy, and fibrosis, most often caused by trauma or prior surgery. IFP pathology is often successfully treated nonoperatively with physical therapy. If refractory to conservative management, partial arthroscopic resection of the IFP has shown favorable results. This activity outlines the evaluation and management of Hoffa pad impingement syndrome and highlights the role of the healthcare team in evaluating and treating patients with this condition.

courses.title: Flibanserin
courses.description: Flibanserin, initially developed as an antidepressant, is the first medication approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for the management of hypoactive sexual desire disorder (HSDD) in premenopausal women. HSDD is characterized by limited or absent sexual fantasies or desires, resulting in interpersonal strain or heightened distress, which persist for a minimum of 6 months. Flibanserin is specifically indicated for patients whose diagnosis is unrelated to relationship issues, psychiatric or medical conditions, or the effects of medication or drugs. Recent trials involving premenopausal women who have endured HSDD for a minimum of 6 months have further reinforced the drug's potential as a practical therapeutic option. This makes flibanserin a pivotal choice for premenopausal women experiencing primary HSDD. This activity covers flibanserin's indications, contraindications, mechanism of action, administration, monitoring, and toxicity. This activity aims to enhance collaboration among healthcare professionals for improved management of HSDD in patients using flibanserin, ultimately leading to more effective patient care and superior outcomes.
