courses.title: Hepatic Biloma
courses.description: A hepatic biloma is a localized collection of bile within or adjacent to the liver, most commonly resulting from iatrogenic injury to the biliary tree during hepatobiliary surgery, percutaneous interventions, or trauma. Patients may present with abdominal pain, fever, jaundice, leukocytosis, or delayed postoperative recovery, though symptoms can be subtle or nonspecific. Early recognition through imaging, typically ultrasound or computed tomography, is essential to prevent progression to sepsis, biliary peritonitis, or hepatic dysfunction. Management focuses on controlling infection, draining the collection via endoscopic or percutaneous methods, and repairing the underlying bile leak when necessary. By participating in this course, clinicians improve their ability to recognize early signs of biloma formation, interpret relevant imaging, and implement evidence-based management strategies. The course reinforces comprehensive care coordination between surgery, interventional radiology, nursing, pharmacy, and infectious disease teams. Learners will strengthen skills in postoperative monitoring, patient education, drain management, and timely escalation of care, leading to enhanced patient safety, reduced morbidity, and more consistent outcomes for patients at risk for, or diagnosed with, hepatic bilomas.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Stiff Person Syndrome
courses.description: Stiff person syndrome (SPS) is a rare progressive and often underdiagnosed immune-mediated disorder of the central nervous system characterized by progressive rigidity and triggered painful spasms of predominantly axial and proximal limb muscles. The condition has an insidious onset with gradual worsening over time and, if left untreated, can lead to permanent disability and mortality. This activity reviews the evaluation and treatment of patients with SPS and emphasizes the importance of the interprofessional approach to managing this condition.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Tofacitinib
courses.description: Tofacitinib is FDA approved for the treatment of moderate to severe rheumatoid arthritis (RA), psoriatic arthritis (PA), ulcerative colitis (UC), and polyarticular course juvenile idiopathic arthritis (pcJIA). It is a second-generation selective Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitor targeting the JAK1 enzyme. This activity will highlight the mechanism of action, adverse event profile, and other key factors pertinent to interprofessional team members in the management of patients with moderate to severe rheumatoid arthritis (RA), psoriatic arthritis (PA), ulcerative colitis (UC), and polyarticular course juvenile idiopathic arthritis (pcJIA) that is unresponsive to first-line therapy.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Golimumab
courses.description: Golimumab, a human monoclonal antibody, belongs to the tumor necrosis factor alpha (TNF- ) blockers class. This medication binds to soluble and transmembrane forms of human TNF- , preventing binding with receptors. The FDA has approved golimumab for treating conditions such as moderate to severe rheumatoid arthritis (RA), psoriatic arthritis (PA), ankylosing spondylitis (AS), ulcerative colitis (UC), and polyarticular juvenile idiopathic arthritis (pcJIA). This activity discusses key aspects of golimumab usage, including its mechanism of action, adverse event profile, and optimal management strategies for patients with these inflammatory conditions, particularly those unresponsive to first-line therapies. Healthcare professionals benefit from updated knowledge regarding golimumab administration, making informed decisions, and optimizing dosage regimens to reduce adverse reactions. This program improves patient outcomes by providing healthcare professionals with evidence-based guidance on treating RA, PA, UC, and pcJIA with golimumab. This activity provides healthcare professionals with information regarding the latest therapeutic advances, allowing for better management of these challenging conditions.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Palliative Radiation Therapy For Bone Metastases
courses.description: Bone metastasis is a common occurrence in many cancers, frequently leading to debilitating symptoms such as pain, pathologic fractures, and compromised quality of life, with the spine being the most frequent site of tumor seeding. With advancements in systemic therapies prolonging the life expectancy of cancer patients, the demand for effective pain relief and functional improvement through palliative radiation therapy for bone metastases has significantly increased. This surge in demand has led to the establishment of outpatient and inpatient palliative radiotherapy centers, emphasizing the need for a coordinated, interdisciplinary approach to optimize patient care. With an estimated 280,000 new cases of bone metastases annually in the United States, primarily originating from cancers including breast, prostate, lung, bladder, thyroid, melanoma, kidney, colorectal, and multiple myeloma, effective management strategies are essential to alleviate symptoms and prevent further skeletal injury. Understanding the purpose of palliative therapy, which prioritizes improving quality of life over extending survival, is crucial for clinicians involved in cancer care. This course enhances the learner's understanding of the purpose of palliative therapy, patient selection criteria, treatment modalities, and indications, ensuring the minimization of adverse effects and the enhancement of overall quality of life for cancer patients with extended life expectancy, and underscores the importance of an interprofessional team in delivering high-quality care to patients with bone metastases.

courses.title: Baricitinib
courses.description: Baricitinib is a disease-modifying antirheumatic drug (DMARD) indicated for rheumatoid arthritis when conventional DMARDs prove inadequate. Furthermore, baricitinib is FDA-approved for treating COVID-19, presenting a valuable choice in combination with other therapies for hospitalized patients, including pediatric cases necessitating supplemental oxygen, invasive mechanical ventilation, or extracorporeal membrane oxygenation. This activity comprehensively reviews the indications, contraindications, mechanisms, adverse events, and other crucial aspects of baricitinib therapy within the clinical setting. courses.title: Environmental Toxins and Infertility
courses.description: Environmental toxins are increasingly recognized as significant factors affecting reproductive health and contributing to infertility. Although the effects of environmental toxins on reproductive health are often subtle and cumulative, their impact can be profound, interfering with hormonal balance, gamete quality, and overall reproductive outcomes. This activity focuses on the major categories of environmental toxins, such as endocrine disruptors, pesticides, heavy metals, persistent organic solvents, and air pollutants, affecting fertility. Each category has distinct mechanisms, presentations, and implications for reproductive health, highlighting the importance of understanding and mitigating these risks. This activity provides an in-depth review of the sources, effects, and strategies for managing exposure to these toxins. By enhancing interprofessional collaboration and increasing awareness among healthcare professionals, the course aims to equip participants with the knowledge and skills necessary to reduce environmental risks and improve reproductive outcomes.

courses.title: Entomophthoromycosis
courses.description: Entomophthoromycosis is a group of rare subcutaneous and mucocutaneous fungal infections predominant in tropical and subtropical areas. Entomon in Greek means "insect," reflecting the initial recognition of these fungi as parasites infecting insects. This gradually advancing infection commonly arises from the traumatic implantation of plant material or the inhalation of spores. The 2 distinct types of entomophthoromycosis include basidiobolomycosis and conidobolomycosis. Soil, insect, reptile, and amphibian excreta harbor Basidiobolus and Conidiobolus. Conidobolomycosis, most commonly caused by Conidiobolus coronatus, presents as a chronic rhinofacial subcutaneous infection that originates in the nasal sinuses and extends to the subcutaneous tissues of the face, resulting in disfigurement among immunocompetent hosts. Basidiobolomycosis is a chronic subcutaneous infection caused by Basidiobolus ranarum, which affects the limbs, trunk, buttocks, and gastrointestinal system. The symptoms of gastrointestinal basidiobolomycosis closely resemble those of more common illnesses, such as malignancy and inflammatory bowel disease, thereby challenging accurate diagnosis. Basidiobolomycosis affects both immunocompetent and immunocompromised patients. With early treatment, the prognosis is favorable. However, in untreated cases or patients with compromised immune systems or systemic illness, disfigurement and death may occur. Accurate diagnosis necessitates a high index of suspicion. Healthcare professionals should consider entomophthoromycosis in patients with classic symptoms, especially those who lived in or traveled to tropical or subtropical climates, due to its potential for disfigurement and mortality. This activity reviews the etiology, pathophysiology, evaluation, and management of entomophthoromycosis, providing healthcare professionals with the knowledge and tools necessary to improve patient outcomes for this rare condition.

courses.title: Single Ventricle and Anesthesia Management
courses.description: Single ventricle physiology represents a group of complex congenital heart defects in which only one functional ventricular chamber supports both systemic and pulmonary circulations. Due to the mixing of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood within the heart, affected neonates often present with hypoxemia shortly after birth, particularly as fetal shunts close and pulmonary vascular resistance drops. The condition frequently necessitates urgent intervention to stabilize oxygen delivery and systemic perfusion. Long-term management typically involves staged palliative surgeries such as the Norwood, Glenn, and Fontan procedures or, in select cases, attempts at biventricular repair, depending on the specific anatomy and functional reserve. This continuing education activity addresses the perioperative and anesthetic considerations for patients with single ventricle physiology. Participants learn to assess hemodynamic parameters, optimize ventilation strategies, and mitigate perioperative risk across both cardiac and non-cardiac procedures. The curriculum emphasizes interdisciplinary collaboration among anesthesiologists, cardiologists, surgeons, nurses, and critical care teams to enhance communication, clinical decision-making, and patient safety. Improved teamwork and a shared understanding of complex physiology are essential to achieving favorable surgical outcomes in this high-risk population.

courses.title: Expiration Dating and National Drug Code Rules
courses.description: National Drug Code Law and Expiration Dating are two laws created by the Food and Drug Administration to help regulate the use, production, and management of medications in the United States. courses.title: Capgras Syndrome
courses.description: Capgras syndrome is the most prevalent delusional misidentification syndrome and is characterized as a delusion of doubles. Patients falsely believe that an identical person has replaced a person close to him or her. This activity aims to provide insight into this rare syndrome through an in-depth discussion about its symptoms, etiology, and pathophysiology. courses.title: OSHA Bloodborne Pathogen Standards
courses.description: The Occupational Safety and Health Administration Bloodborne Pathogen Standard (29 CFR 1910.1030) is a federal regulation that protects healthcare and laboratory personnel from occupational exposure to blood and other potentially infectious materials. This standard establishes a comprehensive framework for exposure prevention, requiring employers to develop and implement written exposure control plans, provide appropriate personal protective equipment, and ensure the use of engineering and work practice controls to minimize risk. The Occupational Safety and Health Administration Bloodborne Pathogen Standard also mandates hepatitis B virus vaccination at no cost to at-risk employees, annual safety training, proper sharps disposal, and prompt post-exposure evaluation and follow-up care. These measures collectively aim to reduce the transmission of bloodborne pathogens, such as HIV, hepatitis B virus, and hepatitis C virus, while fostering a culture of accountability and safety across healthcare settings. This activity for healthcare professionals is designed to strengthen clinicians' competence in identifying, preventing, and managing occupational exposures. Participants reinforce their knowledge of regulatory requirements, safe handling procedures, and evidence-based post-exposure protocols. Clinicians learn to apply engineering and administrative controls, ensure appropriate use of personal protective equipment, and promote compliance within their teams. The emphasis on interprofessional collaboration, ethical responsibilities, and effective communication strategies enhances patient and worker safety. By integrating these principles into daily practice, clinicians not only reduce occupational risks but also contribute to a safer, more resilient healthcare environment that prioritizes prevention, accountability, and continuous quality improvement.

courses.title: Oral Lichen Planus
courses.description: Oral lichen planus (OLP) constitutes a chronic inflammatory disorder primarily affecting the oral mucosa, with potential involvement of the skin, nails, hair follicles, and genital or esophageal mucosa. The etiology remains incompletely understood, but immune-mediated mechanisms, particularly T-cell driven cytotoxicity against basal keratinocytes, play a central role. Risk factors include middle age, female sex, certain systemic conditions, and exposure to medications or dental materials. Clinically, OLP manifests as reticular, erosive, or atrophic lesions, often causing pain or functional impairment. Diagnosis relies on clinical examination supported by histopathology, with differentiation from lichenoid reactions, autoimmune vesiculobullous disorders, and lupus erythematosus. Management emphasizes topical or systemic immunomodulatory therapies, patient education, and lifestyle interventions. Complications include persistent discomfort, secondary infection, and a low but notable risk of malignant transformation. Prognosis varies with lesion type, treatment response, and adherence to long-term monitoring. This activity for healthcare professionals is designed to advance learners' skills in evaluating and managing OLP. The course will emphasize the condition's etiology, risk factors, pathophysiology, clinical presentation, and current diagnostic and therapeutic recommendations. Improved competence will enable clinicians to collaborate with interprofessional teams caring for affected individuals.

courses.title: Odontogenic Cysts
courses.description: Odontogenic cysts are frequently identified on routine examinations with head and neck imaging such as orthopantomograms and computed tomography (CT). In evaluating odontogenic cysts, the clinical examination and interpretation of radiographic studies are essential; however, tooth vitality testing is equally important. Tooth vitality testing is required to formulate an appropriate differential diagnosis for odontogenic cysts. This step is essential in determining treatment and ultimately guides patient outcomes. This activity reviews the most common odontogenic cysts, etiologies, and appropriate therapies and highlights the role of the healthcare team in evaluating, managing, and treating patients with these entities.

courses.title: Therapeutic Hypothermia for Neonatal Hypoxic-Ischemic Encephalopathy
courses.description: Hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy is a severe condition in neonates caused by oxygen deprivation at birth, leading to brain injury, significant morbidity, and high mortality rates. This condition remains a leading cause of long-term neurodevelopmental impairments, including cerebral palsy, cognitive deficits, and epilepsy. Therapeutic hypothermia has emerged as a standard intervention for neonates with moderate-to-severe hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy, as extensive research demonstrates its neuroprotective benefits in reducing brain injury and improving survival with fewer neurological complications. However, critical questions remain regarding optimal patient selection, timing, and efficacy in specific populations, such as preterm infants and neonates in resource-limited settings. This course provides clinicians with a comprehensive understanding of the indications, preparation, administration, and complications of therapeutic hypothermia in neonates with hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy. Participants explore the latest evidence, including controversial aspects of treatment, while developing skills to optimize neonatal care. The course highlights the importance of interprofessional collaboration, involving neonatologists, nurses, respiratory therapists, and neurologists, to ensure precise monitoring, timely interventions, and improved patient outcomes. By enhancing their knowledge of evolving treatment standards and research advances, participants can refine clinical decision-making and deliver high-quality, evidence-based neonatal care.

courses.title: Aortoenteric Fistula
courses.description: Aortoenteric fistula (AEF) is a rare but catastrophic vascular condition that poses significant diagnostic and management challenges for clinicians, particularly vascular surgeons and critical care teams. This condition is classified into primary and secondary forms primary AEF arises from the native aorta, typically associated with an aortic aneurysm. In contrast, secondary AEF is a complication of prior aortic reconstructive surgery, often involving prosthetic graft erosion into the gastrointestinal tract. The duodenum is the most frequent communication site, especially its second portion. Patients typically present with upper gastrointestinal bleeding, abdominal or back pain, and a history of aortic pathology or intervention. When left untreated, AEF is almost universally fatal. Even with prompt recognition and intervention, morbidity and mortality remain high, despite advances in operative techniques, antibiotic therapy, and critical care. Rapid identification and immediate management are essential to survival, often requiring endovascular repair as a bridge to definitive open surgical correction. This educational activity is designed to equip healthcare professionals with the knowledge and skills to effectively recognize, diagnose, and manage aortoenteric fistula. Clinicians learn to identify early warning signs, differentiate between primary and secondary AEF, and apply appropriate diagnostic imaging and hemodynamic stabilization strategies. The course emphasizes evidence-based decision-making, interprofessional collaboration, and timely coordination between vascular surgery, gastroenterology, radiology, critical care, and nursing teams. By strengthening these competencies, participants will enhance patient-centered care, improve diagnostic accuracy, and optimize outcomes in this life-threatening vascular emergency.

courses.title: Controlled Substance Act
courses.description: The Controlled Substance Act (CSA) establishes a federal policy to regulate the manufacturing, distribution, importation, exportation, and use of regulated substances. The CSA lays the framework for categorizing controlled substances and creates a legal foundation for their regulation. This statute was an effort to combine all previous federal drug laws and allow for federal law enforcement of controlled substances, serving as the legal foundation in the federal fight against drug abuse. The cornerstone of the CSA is the classification system by which it regulates controlled substances. This system has 5 schedules of these drugs, numbered I through V. The CSA stratifies these based on a substance s accepted medical use, potential abuse/addiction, and harmfulness. This activity highlights the categorization schedules, amendments, prescription requirements, and other pertinent factors for interprofessional team members to understand and apply the legal structure to their clinical practice.

courses.title: Sonography Fetal Assessment, Protocols, and Interpretation
courses.description: Fetal ultrasonography serves as a cornerstone in assessing fetal development, detecting anomalies, and monitoring well-being across all trimesters, with increasing importance in high-risk pregnancies complicated by obesity, hypertension, and gestational diabetes. This course reviews ultrasound examinations, which are standardized by major professional societies and are categorized as standard, specialized, or limited, each with trimester-specific indications and protocols. Advances in imaging now enable earlier detection of structural anomalies, improving opportunities for timely diagnosis, genetic counseling, and intervention. Participants will also gain an understanding of the variability in terminology and application, which contributes to clinical confusion and missed diagnostic opportunities. This activity for healthcare professionals is designed to enhance learners' competence in ultrasound classifications, indications, and trimester-based protocols, thereby improving their ability to select appropriate studies, interpret findings accurately, and implement an appropriate interprofessional approach when employing this modality to optimize patient outcomes through early identification of fetal and placental abnormalities.

courses.title: Nipah Virus
courses.description: Nipah virus (NiV) infection is an emerging zoonotic disease caused by a highly pathogenic Henipavirus that can cause severe encephalitis and acute respiratory illness, with high case fatality rates. Transmission occurs through exposure to infected bats or intermediate hosts, consumption of contaminated foods (eg, raw date palm sap), or close contact with infected individuals and their body fluids. Clinical presentation typically begins with nonspecific febrile symptoms that can progress rapidly to altered mental status, seizures, coma, and respiratory distress, with multiorgan dysfunction in severe cases. Diagnosis relies on clinical suspicion supported by epidemiologic risk factors and laboratory confirmation, most commonly with real-time reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction from respiratory samples, blood, urine, or cerebrospinal fluid. Management is primarily supportive and requires strict infection prevention and control practices to limit human-to-human transmission, alongside timely public health notification to facilitate contact tracing and community-level mitigation. Course participants learn to recognize the clinical spectrum of NiV infection, identify exposures and outbreak-related risk factors that increase pretest probability, and apply appropriate diagnostic strategies to confirm infection while differentiating NiV from other causes of encephalitis and acute respiratory distress syndrome. Participants also learn to implement isolation precautions, coordinate escalation of supportive care for neurologic and respiratory complications, and integrate public health actions such as reporting, contact tracing, and quarantine when indicated. Collaboration within an interprofessional team enhances outcomes by aligning early neurologic assessment, critical care support, infection control practices, and pharmacy input to consider investigational or regionally recommended therapies, while also supporting rehabilitation and mental health needs during...

courses.title: Pelvic Ultrasound in the Postmenopausal Patient
courses.description: Pelvic ultrasound is the imaging modality of choice to evaluate the uterus, cervix, ovaries, and adnexa. courses.title: First-Trimester Ultrasonography

courses.title: Gastrointestinal and Hepatic Manifestations of Coronavirus (COVID-19)
courses.description: Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) is an acute viral illness caused by severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) that primarily affects the respiratory system but frequently involves extrapulmonary organs. Gastrointestinal and hepatic manifestations are increasingly recognized and may occur with or without respiratory symptoms. Common gastrointestinal features include diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, and anorexia, whereas hepatic involvement often presents as elevated aminotransferases and cholestatic markers. Detection of SARS-CoV-2 ribonucleic acid and viable virus in fecal samples supports gastrointestinal tropism and raises concern for fecal-oral transmission. Patients presenting with gastrointestinal symptoms, particularly when accompanied by abnormal liver biochemistries, demonstrate higher rates of hospitalization and adverse outcomes. COVID-19 associated coagulopathy further contributes to gastrointestinal and hepatic morbidity through complications such as mesenteric ischemia and portal vein thrombosis. This activity strengthens the participant s ability to recognize, evaluate, and manage gastrointestinal and liver manifestations of COVID-19 using evidence-based strategies. Learners enhance competence in identifying atypical presentations, interpreting laboratory abnormalities, and assessing thrombotic risk in affected patients. Emphasis on diagnostic evaluation, supportive management, and escalation of care improves clinical decision-making across inpatient and outpatient settings. Collaboration among clinicians, nurses, gastroenterologists, hepatologists, radiologists, pharmacists, and critical care teams supports coordinated assessment, timely intervention, and consistent monitoring. Interprofessional communication enhances patient safety, optimizes resource utilization, and improves outcomes for individuals with COVID-19 and associated gastrointestinal or hepatic involvement.

courses.title: Physical and Chemical Lesions of the Oral Mucosa
courses.description: Physical and chemical lesions of the oral cavity are frequently identified during routine examinations. Common causes include continuous exposure to trauma, chemical agents, traumatic occlusion, sharp occlusal anatomy, acidic and alkaline substances, medications, and food or beverages at varying temperatures. Depending on the nature and extent of the insult, the lesions may present with symptoms such as pain, ulceration, erythema, or swelling. Evaluation involves a thorough history to identify potential causative factors, coupled with a physical examination to assess the lesion's appearance and location. Management typically includes addressing the underlying cause, providing symptomatic relief with analgesics or protective agents, and, in some cases, prescribing medications to promote healing or prevent infection. This activity for healthcare professionals is designed to enhance learners' proficiency in evaluating and managing physical and chemical lesions of the oral cavity. Participants will deepen their understanding of these lesions' possible etiologies, pathophysiology, and clinical presentation alongside the best diagnostic and therapeutic practices. Increased competence empowers clinicians to contribute meaningfully to interprofessional teams treating patients with these conditions.

courses.title: Intestinal Ultrasonography: Technique, Indications, and Clinical Applications
courses.description: Intestinal ultrasonography is a noninvasive imaging modality that can support diagnosis, monitoring, and follow-up of acute and chronic gastrointestinal conditions, including Crohn disease and ulcerative colitis. This activity reviews bowel wall anatomy, sonographic examination techniques, diagnostic findings, scoring systems, limitations, and the role of intestinal ultrasonography in the care of inflammatory bowel disease. The practice gap is that clinicians may have inconsistent competence in selecting intestinal ultrasonography, interpreting key bowel findings, applying validated scoring systems, and integrating results into patient-centered care. This gap can lead to delayed diagnosis, unnecessary repeated cross-sectional imaging, inconsistent monitoring, and missed opportunities for early treatment adjustment. This activity addresses the gap by strengthening diagnostic reasoning, evidence-based image interpretation, appropriate test selection, and interprofessional communication. Participants will gain actionable skills to improve diagnostic accuracy, follow-up planning, complication recognition, and coordinated care.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Resistant Hypercalcemia
courses.description: Hypercalcemia is a serum calcium (Ca) level over two standard deviations above the average mean values. That equates to a total serum calcium level greater than 10.5 mg/dl or an ionized calcium level greater than 5.3 mg/dl. Resistant hypercalcemia mainly occurs in diseased states with severely elevated serum calcium levels. It is predominantly reported in Malignancy-associated hypercalcemia and primary hyperparathyroidism and can sometimes be life-threatening. Early recognition and prompt diagnosis are essential to decrease mortality associated with this condition. This activity reviews the evaluation and management of resistant hypercalcemia and highlights the role of the healthcare team in managing patients with this condition.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Renal Doppler Ultrasonography
courses.description: Renal Doppler ultrasound is routinely performed because it is a useful technique for evaluating a wide range of various renal pathologic conditions. An understanding of normal anatomy, as well as important anatomic variants, as well as basic physical concepts, are necessary for correct interpretation. This activity outlines the vascular anatomy, imaging indications, and technique and briefly reviews some of the common pathologies where it may be used by an interprofessional team.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Siderosis Bulbi
courses.description: Siderosis bulbi is a chronic pigmentary degenerative process following the retention of an iron-containing foreign body. It can lead to sight-threatening complications. Thus, a detailed history and examination with necessary investigations are critical to diagnose this disease entity and plan appropriate management accordingly. This activity reviews the evaluation and treatment of siderosis bulbi and highlights the role of the interprofessional team in evaluating and treating patients with this condition.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Basic Concepts of Echocardiography Hemodynamics
courses.description: Echocardiographic hemodynamic parameter determination is a crucial step in valvular disease diagnosis and severity determination. Echocardiography can further be utilized to determine the various hemodynamic principles and their link to basic fluid mechanics principles. This activity reviews the basic hemodynamics of echocardiography and highlights the role of the interprofessional team in evaluating and treating patients with various cardiac pathologies, most notably valvular defects.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

practice_areas: Advanced Heart Failure and Transplant Cardiology

courses.title: Inferior Alveolar Nerve and Lingual Nerve Injury
courses.description: The inferior alveolar and lingual nerves provide sensation to the structures of the lower face, including the teeth, skin, and oral mucosa. Injuries to these nerves can be caused by surgical procedures, trauma, or tumors involving the mouth and mandible. Such injuries can cause significant discomfort during daily activities, including chewing, eating, and speaking. Healthcare providers need to understand the anatomical course of the nerves to minimize the risk of injuries. However, if an injury occurs, clinicians should be able to recognize it and accurately assess the extent of the damage. Moreover, patients with nerve damage should be managed promptly to minimize the likelihood of long-term dysfunction. This activity will cover the etiology, presentation, diagnosis, and management of inferior alveolar and lingual nerve injuries.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Peripheral Venous Duplex Ultrasound: Technique and Clinical Applications
courses.description: Peripheral venous duplex ultrasound is a noninvasive imaging technique that combines real-time B-mode sonography with Doppler flow analysis to assess the anatomy and hemodynamics of the peripheral venous system, primarily in the lower and upper extremities. The procedure evaluates vein compressibility, any intraluminal thrombus, valvular function, and venous flow direction. Peripheral venous duplex ultrasound assesses the superficial and deep venous networks, perforator veins, and functional valves, all essential for maintaining efficient venous return. Color and spectral Doppler imaging enable dynamic assessment of flow augmentation, reflux, and obstruction. Compared to contrast venography or computed tomography venography, duplex ultrasound avoids radiation, is widely available, and allows bedside evaluation. This imaging tool is the first-line modality for diagnosing deep vein thrombosis, chronic venous insufficiency, and venous outflow obstruction. Limitations include operator dependency, reduced sensitivity in pelvic or abdominal veins, and decreased accuracy in individuals with obesity or edema. This activity for healthcare professionals is designed to enhance learners' proficiency in performing Doppler peripheral venous duplex assessment and using it for evaluating suspected vascular pathologies. Participants will broaden their grasp of this modality's underlying principles, technical components, anatomical targets, clinical uses, and inherent constraints. Improved skills will equip clinicians to collaborate meaningfully within interprofessional teams caring for individuals with vascular disorders.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Vascular Medical Quality and Patient Safety
courses.description: Vascular medicine is the branch of medicine specializing in the prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of arteries, veins, and lymphatics. Healthcare providers in vascular medicine have obligations to deliver quality in the care they provide to patients. Quality control management is either not a part of the curriculum for health care professionals in vascular medicine in the United States or is of a limited extent. The prevalence of vascular disease in the United States remains relatively high in men and certain ethnic groups compared to the prevalence in other countries. Data indicate that, on a collective basis, American patients receiving care for vascular diseases suffer numerous injuries and deaths due to deficiencies in health care safety. This article highlights concepts that the interprofessional team can use to provide higher quality and safer care.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Uremic Pruritus Evaluation and Treatment
courses.description: Uremic pruritus, also known as chronic kidney disease (CKD)-associated pruritus (CKD-aP), is a common and debilitating symptom experienced by patients with CKD and end-stage renal disease (ESRD). Uremic pruritus is characterized by itching that is not attributable to other causes and can be either localized or generalized. Uremic pruritus significantly impacts patients' quality of life, affecting sleep and leading to poor clinical outcomes and adherence to treatments. Additionally, uremic pruritus is associated with poor adherence to treatments and worse clinical outcomes. Therefore, it is essential to recognize and treat uremic pruritus promptly. Several proposed pathogenetic mechanisms may explain uremic pruritus, and these mechanisms are potential targets for therapy. Before diagnosing CKD-aP, it is crucial to exclude other causes of pruritus, such as eczema, liver and thyroid diseases, and atopy. Management of uremic pruritus involves a stepwise approach, starting with topical emollients, followed by medications like gabapentin and phototherapy. In advanced cases, patients may undergo transplantation, as a successful renal transplant can relieve them from CKD-aP. This activity reviews the etiology, evaluation, and management of uremic pruritus and emphasizes the importance of collaboration within an interprofessional healthcare team to treat patients with this condition, thereby ensuring comprehensive care and improving patients' quality of life.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Alveolar Osteitis
courses.description: Alveolar osteitis, commonly known as "dry socket," is a self-limiting condition that is one of the most common complications following dental extractions. This review will first explore the etiology and pathogenesis of alveolar osteitis. The activity will then outline the evaluation and present recommendations for the treatment of the disease. After developing a more intuitive understanding of the process, the article will touch on complications associated with the treatment. Current recommendations for the prevention of alveolar osteitis will then be highlighted. The role of the interprofessional team in managing patients with this condition will be more precise after exploring these aspects of alveolar osteitis.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Extraintestinal Manifestations of Inflammatory Bowel Disease
courses.description: Extraintestinal manifestations of inflammatory bowel disease involve multiple organ systems. They are common and may result in significant morbidity. This activity reviews the features of the most commonly occurring extraintestinal manifestations and highlights the interprofessional team's role in evaluating and treating patients with these conditions.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Marijuana and Maternal, Perinatal, and Neonatal Outcomes
courses.description: Drug use and drug dependency are major public health problems. Marijuana is one of the most commonly used drugs among all genders and age groups. This activity reviews the epidemiology of marijuana use in pregnant women and its effects on maternal, fetal, and neonatal health and the interprofessional team's role in managing patients with marijuana use.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Chronic Interstitial Nephritis in Agricultural Communities (CINAC)
courses.description: Chronic interstitial nephritis in agricultural communities is a new form of chronic kidney disease. Its etiology is not linked to diabetes, hypertension, glomerulopathies, or other known causes of renal diseases. It had reached epidemic proportions in Central America, Sri Lanka, and other tropical countries. It was reported mainly in young men, occasionally women, and adolescents. The causes are potentially preventable and must be promptly diagnosed and treated to avoid the high morbidity associated with this condition. This activity examines the etiology and diagnosis of this condition and highlights the role of the interprofessional team in managing patients with chronic interstitial nephritis in agricultural communities to ensure the best patient outcomes.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Hepatic Doppler Ultrasonography
courses.description: Doppler liver ultrasonography provides a cost-effective, noninvasive method for evaluating hepatic vascular anatomy, blood flow direction, and hemodynamic abnormalities associated with a wide range of liver disorders. This course reviews normal and abnormal Doppler waveforms of the portal vein, hepatic veins, hepatic artery, and inferior vena cava, supporting accurate assessment of portal hypertension, thrombosis, Budd-Chiari syndrome, focal hepatic lesions, heart failure related congestion, and complications following liver transplantation or TIPS placement. This activity explores hepatic vascular anatomy, principles of hepatopetal and hepatofugal flow, Doppler examination techniques, waveform interpretation, and clinically relevant hemodynamic parameters. Participants will also gain the knowledge needed to recognize characteristic Doppler findings, differentiate physiologic from pathologic flow patterns, identify technical limitations and pitfalls, and apply Doppler ultrasonography effectively in diagnostic evaluation, disease monitoring, and postprocedural follow-up of patients with hepatic and portal vascular disorders. This activity for healthcare professionals is designed to enhance the learner's competence in applying Doppler liver ultrasonography techniques, interpreting waveforms to assess hepatic vasculature, and implementing an appropriate interprofessional approach when managing patients with hepatic disorders.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Cannabis Versus Opioids for Pain
courses.description: Opioids are commonly prescribed to treat and manage chronic and severe pain; however, their potential for abuse and dependency is a concern. Chronic and unrelenting pain can have significant psychological, physical, and emotional stress on individuals. Several strategies are employed to mitigate intractable pain that does not respond to nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), with opioids being widely recognized as the cornerstone of pain management protocols. In recent years, there has been emerging and growing evidence indicating the potential efficacy of cannabinoids in managing chronic pain. This activity offers an overview of the signs and symptoms of adverse events and the crucial aspects of monitoring, intervention, and other pertinent considerations in opioid therapy and cannabinoids for patients with chronic pain. These key points are indispensable for fostering effective collaboration among interprofessional team members responsible for patient care.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

certifying_boards: American Board of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation

courses.title: Neonatal Hyperglycemia
courses.description: Neonatal hyperglycemia, typically defined as serum glucose above 150 mg/dL, reflects an imbalance between glucose delivery, utilization, and insulin activity in both term and preterm infants. Contributing factors include prematurity, impaired insulin secretion, increased insulin resistance, elevated stress hormones, delayed enteral feeding, total parenteral nutrition related metabolic effects, sepsis, medication exposures, and rare genetic syndromes. This course reviews the clinical manifestations of neonatal hyperglycemia, which are often related to underlying etiologies and may include dehydration, weight loss, temperature instability, or feeding difficulties. Accurate diagnosis with serum glucose confirmation, electrolyte monitoring, and evaluation for infection or persistent dysglycemia requiring further endocrine and genetic assessment is also discussed. Management. This activity examines the mechanisms of neonatal hyperglycemia and evidence-based management strategies, focusing on adjusting glucose infusion rates, addressing contributing conditions, and cautiously considering insulin therapy with close monitoring to avoid hypoglycemia. Participants will gain an in-depth knowledge of underlying causes, nutrition and glucose delivery, monitoring of metabolic stability, and safe insulin protocols. This activity for healthcare professionals is designed to enhance the learner's competence in identifying neonatal hyperglycemia, performing the recommended evaluation, and implementing an appropriate interprofessional approach to manage this condition, thereby supporting better patient outcomes, reducing complications, and promoting safe, physiologic glucose control in at-risk infants.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Gastric Varices
courses.description: Gastric varices are an uncommon but high-risk manifestation of portal hypertension that may cause severe gastrointestinal bleeding, hemodynamic instability, rebleeding, and death. Effective care requires accurate differentiation of cirrhosis-related and noncirrhotic causes, recognition of high-risk variceal features, timely endoscopic evaluation, appropriate imaging, and coordinated treatment selection. The gap is that clinicians may inconsistently assess gastric variceal anatomy, bleeding risk, and underlying etiology, thereby delaying resuscitation, definitive therapy, and secondary prevention. This continuing medical education activity addresses that gap by reviewing classification, diagnostic evaluation, acute bleeding treatment, primary and secondary prophylaxis, and interprofessional coordination among gastroenterology, hepatology, critical care, hematology, pharmacy, blood bank services, and interventional radiology. Participants will gain practical strategies to improve diagnostic accuracy, treatment selection, complication prevention, and rebleeding risk reduction, as well as patient-centered outcomes.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Medial Epicondyle Apophysitis (Little League Elbow)
courses.description: Medial epicondyle apophysitis, commonly referred to as Little League Elbow, is an overuse injury that primarily affects adolescent athletes participating in sports that involve repetitive overhead motions, such as baseball, tennis, or volleyball. The condition results from repetitive valgus stress applied to the medial elbow during activities like pitching or serving, which leads to inflammation and microtrauma at the growth plate of the medial epicondyle. Medial epicondyle apophysitis typically presents with medial elbow pain that worsens with activity and may be accompanied by reduced throwing velocity or accuracy. Early recognition and intervention are crucial in preventing long-term complications, such as chronic instability or premature closure of the growth plate, which can impair function. This course equips participants with a detailed understanding of the pathophysiology, clinical evaluation, imaging, and evidence-based treatment strategies for medial epicondyle apophysitis. Emphasis is placed on activity modification, rehabilitation planning, and gradual return-to-play protocols. The course also highlights the collaborative role of pediatricians, sports medicine specialists, physical therapists, athletic trainers, and radiologists in managing medial epicondyle apophysitis. Through interprofessional communication and coordinated care, the healthcare team ensures accurate diagnoses, timely interventions, and individualized treatments, ultimately supporting safe recovery and preventing recurrence in young athletes.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Catheter-Based Management of Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy
courses.description: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is an inherited cardiac disorder characterized by unexplained left ventricular hypertrophy in the absence of systemic or metabolic causes. Diagnosis relies on noninvasive imaging, including echocardiography, cardiac magnetic resonance imaging, or computed tomography, with defined wall thickness criteria supporting confirmation. Dynamic left ventricular outflow tract obstruction may occur and contribute to symptoms such as dyspnea, chest pain, and syncope. Management includes pharmacologic therapy and, in symptomatic patients with persistent obstruction, septal reduction therapy (SRT). Surgical myomectomy remains the standard in selected individuals, whereas alcohol septal ablation (ASA) offers a catheter-based alternative for appropriately selected patients. This continuing education activity reviews catheter-based management of HCM, emphasizing patient selection, procedural technique, and outcomes associated with ASA. Participants gain knowledge of indications for SRT, peri-procedural considerations, and expected hemodynamic and symptomatic improvements. Emerging approaches, including septal scoring along the midline endocardium, are introduced within the context of evolving minimally invasive strategies. Collaboration with an interprofessional heart team enhances patient outcomes through comprehensive risk assessment, individualized treatment planning, and coordinated periprocedural care, particularly in patients with advanced age, comorbidities, or elevated surgical risk.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Bacterial Infections of the Oral Mucosa
courses.description: Bacterial lesions of the oral mucosa can appear throughout the oral cavity and often serve as the earliest indication of an underlying condition. In some cases, these diseases present without symptoms during the initial phase, creating significant diagnostic challenges. This activity provides a comprehensive overview of the most common bacterial lesions, including syphilis, tuberculosis, gonorrhea, and scarlet fever. It emphasizes the importance of early recognition of oral manifestations to ensure timely and accurate diagnosis. By focusing on the clinical presentation, diagnostic process, and treatment strategies, the activity highlights both the potential complications of missed or delayed recognition and the critical role of prevention in patient care. Through participation in this activity, the learner develops the ability to evaluate and manage bacterial lesions of the oral mucosa with greater precision and confidence. The course reinforces competence in identifying early signs and implementing appropriate treatment strategies to prevent complications. It also underscores the importance of interprofessional collaboration, as optimal outcomes often require coordinated efforts between dentists, oral surgeons, infectious disease specialists, and primary care providers. This teamwork ensures that patient care is both timely and comprehensive, improving diagnostic accuracy and treatment efficacy while reducing the risk of long-term sequelae.

courses.title: Vascular Ultrasonography
courses.description: Vascular sonography is a noninvasive imaging procedure that uses high-frequency sound waves to identify arterial, venous, and lymphatic pathology. Indications include suspected circulatory or lymphatic disorders, conditions commonly arising from atherosclerosis, thrombosis, inflammation, malignancy, trauma, or postoperative states. B-mode imaging characterizes vessel wall morphology, lumen patency, and lymph node architecture, while color-flow imaging assesses flow direction and patterns, and spectral Doppler quantifies blood velocity and hemodynamic indices. This activity for healthcare professionals is designed to advance learners skills in correlating vascular sonographic findings with clinical presentation to optimize patient evaluation and procedural or medical management. Participants learn procedural indications, contraindications, preparation protocols, equipment selection, and technical execution relevant to this assessment modality. Refined proficiency will strengthen clinician collaboration within interprofessional strategies to address the health needs of individuals undergoing sonographic assessment of arterial, venous, or lymphatic pathology.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Federal Regulation of Medication Production
courses.description: Federal regulation of prescription medications plays a critical role in ensuring that drugs available to patients are safe, effective, and manufactured according to established quality standards. Because medications are integral to the prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of disease, healthcare professionals must understand the legal and regulatory framework governing drug development, approval, marketing, and postmarketing surveillance. This activity reviews the historical evolution and foundational principles of federal drug regulation in the United States, including the role of key legislation, regulatory agencies, and safety-monitoring systems. Participants will examine how regulatory requirements influence medication safety, product quality, labeling, and adverse event reporting. The activity also highlights the contributions of pharmacists, physicians, nurses, and other healthcare professionals in maintaining regulatory compliance and promoting patient safety. Upon completion, clinicians will be better equipped to apply regulatory principles in practice, recognize medication-related safety concerns, and support evidence-based, patient-centered care.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Obesity in Pregnancy
courses.description: The global prevalence of obesity has significantly increased in the past decades, and the World Health Organization (WHO) has described the phenomenon as a global epidemic, with the number of overweight and obese people nearly tripling between 1975 and 2016. Accordingly, the incidence of maternal obesity has also been increasing, and this has become one of the most important health issues in pregnancy. Globally, the prevalence of overweight and obesity varies greatly. Obesity during pregnancy contributes to increased morbidity from the prenatal period to the post-partum period and can even affect offspring's health into adulthood, related to fetal programming. Clinicians need to be aware of potential prenatal complications, including increased risk of neural tube defects, preeclampsia, gestational diabetes, spontaneous abortion, and stillbirth. Delivery complications include increased risk of Cesarean sections, longer time to dilation, increased risk of thromboembolism, and infection. Post-partum women with obesity during pregnancy can have a harder time losing the weight gained during pregnancy and have other health problems. Clinicians must be aware of societal guidelines, recommended interventions, advised monitoring, and appropriate weight gain for the recommended body mass index. Following these guidelines will help improve outcomes for this burgeoning issue facing women with pregnancy and obesity.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Odontogenic Orofacial Space Infections
courses.description: Odontogenic and orofacial infections are rare but important sequelae of dental infections. Dental care and the evaluation, treatment, and follow-up of these sequelae affect providers of many medical disciplines. Treating these infections in the early stages can be simple and confer minimal morbidity. However, delay in treatment can allow these infections to require many treatments by an interdisciplinary team and lead to permanent disability or death. Dental disease is easily preventable, making these infections a good target for many primary and secondary prevention strategies. This activity reviews the anatomy, microbiology, evaluation, treatment, prevention, and optimization of managing infections secondary to odontogenic and orofacial sources.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Atezolizumab
courses.description: Atezolizumab is a humanized IgG1 monoclonal antibody that targets programmed cell death ligand 1 (PD-L1). Atezolizumab has received FDA approval for multiple neoplastic conditions and may be administered as monotherapy or in combination with chemotherapy. Indications include locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma, metastatic non-small cell lung cancer, extensive-stage small cell lung cancer, metastatic triple-negative breast cancer, and unresectable or metastatic hepatocellular carcinoma. This activity reviews the various pharmacological features of atezolizumab, including the mechanism of action and dosage adjustments. Additionally, warnings, precautions, and monitoring parameters are emphasized to ensure optimal patient outcomes. Adverse events and contraindications are also highlighted to guide clinicians in minimizing risks associated with atezolizumab therapy. Improved care coordination between interprofessional team members is essential to maximize the therapeutic benefits for patients receiving this medication.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Galactocele
courses.description: Galactoceles are benign milk retention cysts that primarily arise in lactating or recently lactating women due to a persistent obstruction of the lactiferous duct. This obstruction causes milk to accumulate in a cyst-like structure. Typically presenting as a moderately firm, painless mass, galactoceles may gradually or rapidly increase in size, with fluctuations noted throughout the day. While they are generally not associated with pain or inflammation, complications can lead to infection. Ultrasonography typically reveals a cystic fluid collection, and in symptomatic cases, aspiration may be performed for both diagnostic and therapeutic purposes. Although many galactoceles resolve spontaneously, those that are symptomatic or infected often require medical intervention, including drainage and antibiotics. This activity for healthcare professionals is designed to enhance the learner's competence in recognizing the clinical features of a galactocele, performing the recommended evaluation, and implementing an appropriate interprofessional management approach to improve patient outcomes.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Ergonomics
courses.description: Ergonomics is the study of matching job requirements and environment to the worker to maximize efficiency, quality, and quantity of work while minimizing work-related musculoskeletal disorders (WMSD), fatigue, and overexertion. An assessment is crucial for each job and should consider physical and psychosocial factors that impact the ergonomic outcomes. The assessment is usually initiated by a primary care clinician in response to the common complaints described above. If managed appropriately, work satisfaction increases, and most patients return to work as normal. Of course, adjustments are possible depending on a patient's changing employment, which may be informed by previous outcomes. This activity outlines the components of ergonomics and highlights the interprofessional team's role in maintaining proper ergonomics for their patients. Participating clinicians also review occupation-specific recommendations to enhance ergonomics, specifically in healthcare.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

certifying_boards: American Board of Otolaryngology - Head and Neck Surgery

courses.title: Lenvatinib
courses.description: Lenvatinib is FDA-approved for the treatment of radioactive iodine-refractory differentiated thyroid cancer (DTC), unresectable or advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), advanced renal cell carcinoma (RCC), and advanced endometrial carcinoma. The multiple receptor tyrosine kinase inhibitor demonstrates potent antiangiogenic properties. The inhibition of the VEGF receptors prevents tumor angiogenesis, and the inhibition of FGFR, RET, PDGFRa, and KIT prevents further proliferation of malignant cells. The prescribing team should include primary care clinicians, oncologists, nurses, and pharmacists, crucial for early diagnosis, monitoring potential adverse effects, and optimizing dosage adjustments based on renal function, liver enzymes, body weight, and cardiac health. Routine monitoring for adverse effects like hypertension, cardiac impairment, QT interval prolongation, thyroid function changes, and reproductive considerations is necessary, along with patient education for better treatment outcomes and increased quality of life. This activity highlights the mechanism of action, adverse event profile, and other key factors pertinent to interprofessional team members in managing patients with gastrointestinal or uterine cancers. Participating clinicians are informed to make decisions and optimize dosage regimens while minimizing adverse reactions.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: New Onset Refractory Status Epilepticus
courses.description: New-onset refractory status epilepticus (NORSE) is an uncommon clinical entity with a mortality rate of 16-27% in adults and significant long-term neurological sequelae. Approximately 50% of patients with NORSE have an unknown etiology despite an extensive workup. There is a lack of consensus regarding the best treatment options available for managing patients with NORSE. However, immediate cessation of seizure activity, early institution of continuous infusion of anesthetic agents, and immunotherapies can play an important role in reducing morbidity and mortality in NORSE. This activity reviews the evaluation and treatment options available and highlights the healthcare team's role in managing patients with this condition.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Dilation and Curettage
courses.description: Dilation and curettage (D&C) is one of the most common invasive procedures in the United States. The procedure can be performed on a pregnant or nonpregnant patient and be either diagnostic or therapeutic. Sometimes the circumstances lead to a diagnostic procedure becoming therapeutic. A D&C occurs in 2 steps: dilation of the cervix and curettage of the endometrial cavity. While current recommendations for endometrial sampling in the nonpregnant patient include hysteroscopy with directed endometrial sampling, if necessary resources are unavailable, a simple D&C may be performed to acquire tissue for histologic evaluation. Contraindications to D&C are few, and the overall mortality rate is low. This activity reviews the indications, absolute and relative contraindications, equipment needs, technique, and complications of diagnostic and therapeutic D&C in pregnant and nonpregnant patients. In addition, the role of the healthcare team in improving care for patients undergoing D&C is highlighted.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Posterior Cortical Atrophy
courses.description: This activity describes and reviews the role of physicians and nursing providers in evaluating and managing patients with posterior cortical atrophy. The article highlights the difference in the presentation of posterior cortical atrophy compared to typical Alzheimer's disease. It describes the common underlying etiologies for this condition. It reviews the most common symptoms upon presentation, course of the illness, co-morbid psychiatric symptoms and describes neuropsychological and radiological findings. This activity examines the possible early interventions, including safety measures required to be implemented, developing compensation strategies, psychosocial interventions, and patient education with prompt recognition and diagnosis of this neurodegenerative disorder. This activity emphasizes the interprofessional team's approach involving neurologists, psychiatrists, occupational therapists, physical therapists, and social workers.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Gastric Lymphoma
courses.description: Gastric lymphoma constitutes around 5% of all gastric neoplasms but is the most prevalent site for extranodal lymphomas, comprising 30% to 40% of extranodal cases and 55% to 65% of gastrointestinal lymphomas. This category predominantly includes mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue (MALT) lymphoma and diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL), with rare instances of mantle cell and follicular lymphomas. Notably, over 90% of gastric MALT lymphomas are associated with Helicobacter pylori infections, underscoring the importance of H pylori eradication in managing these lymphomas. Diagnostic evaluation for gastric lymphomas includes endoscopic biopsies, endoscopic ultrasounds, imaging techniques such as computed tomography, magnetic resonance imaging, and positron emission tomography, as well as immunohistochemical testing. Treatment strategies involve antibiotic therapy for H pylori eradication, biotherapy or immunotherapy, chemotherapy, and, sometimes, radiation therapy. This activity reviews and enhances clinicians' understanding of the epidemiology, diverse subtypes, evaluation, and treatment of gastric lymphoma, bolstering diagnostic proficiency with advanced imaging and biopsy techniques. This activity also provides clinicians with comprehensive insights into tailored treatment strategies, including H pylori eradication and diverse therapeutic modalities, aiming to improve clinical outcomes and patient care practices.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

certifying_boards: American Board of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation

courses.title: Esophageal Necrosis
courses.description: Acute esophageal necrosis is a life-threatening condition characterized by acute ischemia of the esophagus, typically caused by reduced blood flow or chemical injuries. This condition presents significant challenges in diagnosis and management. Symptoms may include severe chest pain, difficulty swallowing, and signs of systemic infection. The condition is associated with medically comorbid patients. Prompt diagnosis and aggressive supportive treatment are needed in the initial setting, with early consideration of surgical intervention to prevent poor outcomes. This review evaluates the etiology, clinical presentation, and diagnostic approaches to acute esophageal necrosis and the critical management steps required by the interprofessional team to treat this rare entity. Participants gain a thorough understanding of how to recognize early signs, interpret diagnostic findings, and implement effective treatment plans. The activity also highlights the role of an interprofessional healthcare team in enhancing patient outcomes through timely and informed interventions.
courses.accreditation: ACCME-accredited provider; AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™️

courses.title: Lipedema
courses.description: American physicians Allen and Hines described an abnormal deposition of adipose tissue affecting females in the 1940s in a Mayo Clinic termed lipedema. Lipedema is the disproportionate and symmetrical distribution of adipose tissue involving the lower extremities to a greater degree than the trunk or upper extremities. History and physical examination provide clues regarding the lipedema, which is evaluated more with nuclear medicine lymphangioscintigraphy, ultrasound, or MRI of the legs. To avoid more complications, it should be diagnosed and intervene early. This activity reviews the evaluation and management of lipedema. Treatment starts with conservative management, like diet and exercise, but then surgical options like bariatric surgery and liposuction should be considered.

courses.title: Submandibular Salivary Gland Excision
courses.description: Sialolithiasis of the submandibular gland is the most frequent pathology affecting the major salivary glands, arising from the formation of obstructive calculi within the Wharton duct. Obstruction impedes salivary flow, predisposing to secondary bacterial sialadenitis. Etiologic factors include altered salivary viscosity, dehydration, ductal stenosis, and medication-induced xerostomia, which are particularly common in older adults. Clinically, patients present with painful swelling of the gland, often exacerbated during meals, and may experience recurrent or persistent infections. Initial management includes hydration, gland massage, sialogogues, antibiotics for infection, and minimally invasive techniques such as sialendoscopy, ductal dilation, or lithotripsy. Submandibular salivary gland excision provides definitive treatment for patients with recurrent or refractory disease, as well as for neoplasms and symptomatic ranulas. Compared with conservative modalities, excision eliminates the diseased gland and prevents recurrence, though at the cost of greater invasiveness. Indications include chronic sialadenitis, recurrent calculi, and selected tumors. Contraindications are limited to poor operative candidacy or unresectable malignancy. Potential complications include lingual nerve or marginal mandibular nerve injury, hematoma, infection, fistula, and scarring. Reported success rates exceed 90%, making excision a reliable option when conservative measures fail. This activity for healthcare professionals is designed to improve learners' understanding of submandibular salivary gland excision, including procedural techniques and the selection of appropriate candidates. Participants will gain deeper insights into relevant anatomy and physiology and the indications and considerations for submandibular salivary gland excision. Enhanced interprofessional collaboration will improve patient outcomes through timely diagnosis, appropriate intervention, and coordinated care.

courses.description: Fluorine18 fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography (FDG PET/CT) is an essential imaging modality that plays a vital role in managing patients with lymphoma. Computerized tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) only provide the anatomic details but cannot detect morphologically normal but functionally abnormal tissues. On the other hand, PET provides functional information at the molecular level, which is vital in staging and assessing treatment responses in various malignancies. This activity highlights the role of PET/CT in the management of lymphoma patients, which includes initial staging, monitoring the interim response of the therapy, end of the treatment response, and detecting recurrence. It also addresses common pitfalls that can interfere with accurate image interpretation.

However, some studies report that up to 25 to 30% of HIV patients who are on antiretroviral therapy have IRIS. This activity outlines the risk factors, pathophysiology, clinical presentation, and the interprofessional team's role in managing immune reconstitution syndrome.

courses.title: Encapsulating Peritoneal Sclerosis
courses.description: Encapsulating peritoneal sclerosis (EPS) is a rare but serious condition characterized by the progressive development of a thickened, fibrocollagenous peritoneal membrane that encases the small intestine, often resulting in recurrent bowel obstruction, malnutrition, and severe morbidity. The condition most frequently arises as a late complication of long-term peritoneal dialysis, with prevalence estimates reaching up to 3.3% of patients within 5 years of therapy initiation. However, EPS may also occur in association with autoimmune diseases, intra-abdominal infections, malignancy, or after renal transplantation. The pathogenesis involves chronic peritoneal inflammation, fibrosis, and angiogenesis, resulting in the progressive encapsulation of the bowel. Diagnosis requires a high index of suspicion because EPS can develop even after discontinuation of dialysis and may not be evident on early imaging. The condition carries a high mortality rate, emphasizing the need for early recognition, multidisciplinary management, and tailored therapeutic strategies to prevent irreversible complications. This educational activity enhances clinicians competence in identifying, evaluating, and managing encapsulating peritoneal sclerosis through a comprehensive review of current evidence and diagnostic challenges. Participants learn to differentiate EPS from other causes of bowel obstruction, interpret radiologic findings, and apply evidence-based therapeutic approaches, including pharmacologic and surgical interventions. The course also emphasizes the importance of interprofessional collaboration among nephrologists, surgeons, radiologists, gastroenterologists, and dietitians in improving patient outcomes. Effective communication and coordination across disciplines optimize early diagnosis, guide individualized treatment plans, and support nutritional and perioperative management. courses.title: Non-Odontogenic Cysts
courses.description: Nonodontogenic cysts originate from tissues not involved in tooth formation and are predominantly developmental in nature. These lesions are uncommon but may be encountered by dental and medical professionals during routine oral examinations. Etiologic factors include aberrant epithelial remnants and congenital tissue malformations. Risk factors remain poorly defined, although certain cysts demonstrate a predilection for specific age groups or anatomical sites. Nonodontogenic cysts develop through epithelial proliferation and fluid accumulation, leading to localized expansion. Clinically, they may present as asymptomatic swellings, mucosal elevations, or radiolucent lesions on imaging. Diagnosis requires thorough clinical assessment, radiographic evaluation, and histopathologic confirmation, with particular attention to excluding odontogenic origin due to differences in management. Treatment typically involves surgical enucleation or marsupialization, depending on size and location. Complications may include infection, adjacent structure displacement, or recurrence. Prognosis is generally favorable following complete excision, with minimal risk of long-term sequelae. This activity for healthcare professionals is designed to sharpen learners' skills in evaluating and managing nonodontogenic cysts. Participants will deepen their understanding of the condition's etiology, risk factors, pathophysiology, clinical presentation, and evidence-based diagnostic and therapeutic recommendations. Enhanced competence will empower clinicians to collaborate with interprofessional teams providing care for individuals with these oral growths.

It has a diverse clinical trajectory and is a heterogeneous disease. This lymphoma is derived from germinal center B cells, centrocytes, and centroblasts. The growth pattern of this lymphoma is almost always nodular with a follicular pattern. Most people with this disease will have a clinically indolent course, needing only intermittent therapy over decades. Asymptomatic relapsed cases can be observed and monitored closely for symptom development and do not need immediate treatment. The treatment of late relapsed cases depends on several factors, such as comorbidities, disease burden, and performance status. This activity covers the diagnosis and management of follicular lymphoma.

courses.title: Sonography Assessment of Gestational Age
courses.description: Assessment of gestational age by sonography addresses a fundamental clinical problem in obstetric care: inaccurate dating of pregnancy, which may result from uncertain last menstrual period, irregular menstrual cycles, recent hormonal contraception, the use of assisted reproductive techniques, or delayed presentation to care. Imprecise gestational dating is associated with inappropriate timing of antenatal surveillance, misinterpretation of fetal growth, suboptimal management of preterm or postterm pregnancy, and avoidable maternal or neonatal morbidity. Patients commonly present with indications for sonographic dating during early prenatal visits, evaluation of uterine size date discrepancy, and assessment of threatened pregnancy complications, or prior to obstetric interventions. Obstetric sonography estimates gestational age through standardized biometric measurements, providing an objective and reproducible framework for pregnancy dating. Indications include uncertain clinical dating, high-risk pregnancy, and planning of obstetric management, whereas contraindications are limited and primarily relate to patient instability or inability to obtain adequate images. Technical challenges include poor acoustic windows, fetal position, and advanced gestational age. Failure to perform accurate sonographic dating may lead to gestational age misclassification, inappropriate intervention, or delayed recognition of fetal compromise. Procedural risks are minimal when performed correctly. This activity for healthcare professionals is designed to sharpen learners skills in integrating sonographic gestational age assessment into obstetric risk stratification and management. Participants will gain deeper insights into the procedure's diagnostic role, indications, contraindications, equipment and preparation requirements, and proper technique.
